items.slavonic_text: побѣ́дꙋ ва́їами, сї́есть, вѣ́твьми: ва́їа бо ᲂу҆ є҆вре́євъ вѣ́твь ма́тица глаго́летсѧ. Ѻ҆бы́чай бо бя́ше, ꙗ҆́кѡ побѣди́теле под̾и́гшихъ, и҆лѝ крале́й нѣ́кихъ, вѣ́твьми древе́съ присноцвѣтꙋ́щихъ въ побѣ́дныхъ провожде́нїихъ почита́ти, и҆ ѡ҆бводи́ли клꙋ́бъ. Гада́тельнѣйше же зна́меноваше жребе́цъ сꙋ́щыѧ ны̀ ѿ ꙗ҆зы́къ лю́ди, на не́мже всѣ́дъ Хрⷭ҇то́съ, и҆ преночи́въ, ѡ҆долѣ́тель и҆ побѣди́тель, Цр҃ь же всеѧ̀ землѝ нарече́сѧ. Ѡ҆ се́мъ пра́здницѣ и҆ прⷪ҇ро́къ глаго́лаше Заха́рїа: Ра́дꙋйсѧ ѕѣлѡ̀ дщѝ Сїѡ́нова, сѐ Цр҃ь тво́й грѧде́тъ тебѣ̀ кро́токъ, и҆ всѣ́дъ на под̾ѧре́мника, и҆ жребца̀ ѻ҆слѧ̀ сы́на под̾ѧре́мнича. И҆ Дв҃дъ па́ки ѡ҆ дѣ́техъ: И҆з̾ ᲂу҆́стъ младе́нецъ, и҆ ссꙋ́щихъ соверши́лъ є҆сѝ хвалꙋ̀. Но крѡда́мъ, речѐ, Хрⷭ҇тꙋ̀, потрясе́сѧ ве́сь І҆ерл҃имъ: и҆ во смꙋще́нїе наро́ди, ѿ а҆рхїере́й поꙋче́ни бы́вше, смотрѧ́хꙋ є҆го̀ ᲂу҆би́ти: то́йже таѧ́шесѧ крꙑ́ѧсѧ и҆ ꙗ҆влѧ́ѧсѧ, при́тчами глаго́лаше и҆̀мъ. Неизрече́ннымъ твои́мъ млⷣрдїемъ Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е на́шъ, побѣди́тели ны̀ безслове́сныхъ страсте́й сотворѝ, и҆ твою̀ свѣ́тлꙋю на сме́рть побѣ́дꙋ, ꙗ҆́сное же и҆ живоно́сное Воскр҃нїе ви́дѣти сподо́би, и҆ поми́лꙋй на́съ, ны́нѣ и҆ при́снѡ, и҆ во вѣ́ки вѣкѡ́въ, а҆ми́нь.
items.english_text: ...victory by palms, that is, branches; for among the Hebrews a tender branch is called *vaia*. For it was the custom to honor those who achieved victories or certain kings with branches of evergreen trees in triumphal processions, and they surrounded the assembly. More enigmatically, the foal prefigured us, the people from among the Gentiles, upon whom Christ mounted and, having sojourned, became Victor and Conqueror, and was proclaimed King of the whole earth. Concerning this feast the Prophet Zechariah also spoke: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; behold, thy King comes unto thee, meek, and sitting upon a beast of burden and a young colt, the foal of an ass. And David again concerning the children: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast Thou perfected praise. But when Christ entered, He saith, all Jerusalem was shaken; and the multitudes in turmoil, having been incited by the chief priests, sought to kill Him; but He concealed Himself, hiding and appearing, and spoke unto them in parables. By Thine ineffable compassion, O Christ our God, make us victors over irrational passions, and make us worthy to behold Thy radiant victory over death and Thine illuminated and life-bearing Resurrection, and have mercy on us, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.

items.slavonic_text: Съ ва́їемъ тѧ̀ Хрⷭ҇тѐ, вѣ́твьми похваля́хꙋ мно́жества, бл҃гослове́нъ прише́дый Цр҃ь вѣкѡ́въ, вопїѧ́хꙋ же: препѣ́тый Гдⷭ҇и Бж҃е ѻ҆тє́цъ, бл҃гослове́нъ є҆сѝ.
items.english_text: The innocent multitude, nature yet in infancy, hymned Thee in a manner befitting God, O King of Israel and of the angels: O all-hymned Lord, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS

items.day_or_date: Synaxarion:*[^44]
items.slavonic_text: Весели́сѧ І҆ерл҃име, торжествꙋ́йте лю́бѧщїи Сїѡ́на: црⷭ҇твꙋѧй бо во вѣ́ки Гдⷭ҇ь си́лъ прїи́де, да бл҃гоговѣ́етъ всѧ̀ землѧ̀ ѿ лица̀ є҆гѡ̀, и҆ да вопїе́тъ: бл҃гослови́те всѧ̑ дѣла̀ Гдⷭ҇нѧ Гдⷭ҇а.
items.english_text: With palms and branches the multitudes praised Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Blessed is He that is come, the King of the ages! O all-hymned Lord, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

provenance.verbatim_source: With palms and branches the multitudes praised Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Blessed is He that is come, the King of the ages! O all-hymned Lord, God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion:*[^44]
items.slavonic_text: На жребѧ̀ мла́до всѣ́дъ Цр҃ь тво́й Сїѡ́не, предста̀ Хрⷭ҇то́съ: безслове́снꙋю бо і҆́дѡльскꙋю пре́лесть разрꙋши́ти, неᲂу҆держа́нное стремле́нїе ᲂу҆ста́вити, всѣ́хъ ꙗ҆зы́къ прїи́де, во є҆́же пѣ́ти: всѧ̑ дѣла̀ по́йте Гдⷭ҇а.
items.english_text: *Ode 8. Heirmos:* Be glad, O Jerusalem! Keep feast, ye that love Zion! For the Lord of hosts, Who reigns unto the ages, is come; let all the earth stand in awe before His face, and cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Be glad, O Jerusalem! Keep feast, ye that love Zion! For the Lord of hosts, Who reigns unto the ages, is come; let all the earth stand in awe before His face, and cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK

items.slavonic_text: Бг҃ъ тво́й, ра́дꙋйсѧ Сїѡ́не ѕѣлѡ̀, воцр҃и́сѧ во вѣ́ки Хрⷭ҇то́съ, се́й, ꙗ҆́коже пи́сано є҆́сть, кро́ткїй и҆ спаса́ѧй, пра́ведный И҆зба́витель на́шъ, прїи́де на жребѧ́ти, ко́нское свирѣ́пство ᲂу҆би́ти врагѡ́въ, не вопїю́щихъ: бл҃гослови́те всѧ̑ дѣла̀ Гдⷭ҇нѧ Гдⷭ҇а.

items.english_text: Mounted upon a young foal, thy King, O Zion, Christ, hath appeared; for He is come to destroy the irrational deception of idols and to stay the unrestrained rush of all the Gentiles, that they may sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь ѳ҃. І҆рмо́съ:
items.english_text: Thy God, rejoice greatly, O Zion, Christ, reigns unto the ages! He, as it is written, meek and saving, our righteous Deliverer, is come upon a foal, to put to death the furious horse-rage of the enemies who cry not: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

provenance.verbatim_source: Thy God, rejoice greatly, O Zion, Christ, reigns unto the ages! He, as it is written, meek and saving, our righteous Deliverer, is come upon a foal, to put to death the furious horse-rage of the enemies who cry not: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

items.slavonic_text: Бг҃ъ Гдⷭ҇ь, и҆ ꙗ҆ви́сѧ на́мъ, соста́вите пра́здникъ, и҆ веселя́щесѧ прїиди́те, возвели́чимъ Хрⷭ҇та̀, съ ва́їами и҆ вѣ́твьми пѣ́сньми зовꙋ́ще: бл҃гослове́нъ грѧды́й во и҆́мѧ Гдⷭ҇а Сп҃са на́шегѡ.

items.english_text: The law-transgressing congregation of the disobedient is deprived of divine ramparts, since they made the house of prayer of God a den of thieves, casting off from their heart the Deliverer, unto Whom we cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

items.slavonic_text: Мно́жество наро́да Гдⷭ҇и, постила́хꙋ по пꙋтѝ ри̑зы своѧ̑: дрꙋзі́и же рѣ́захꙋ вѣ́тки ѿ древе́съ, и҆ ноша́хꙋ, пред̾идꙋ́щїи же и҆ послѣ́дствꙋющїи зовя́хꙋ глаго́люще: ѡ҆са́нна Сн҃ꙋ Дв҃довꙋ, бл҃гослове́нъ є҆сѝ прише́дый, и҆ па́ки грѧды́й во и҆́мѧ Гдⷭ҇не.
items.english_text: *Sticheron 1:* A multitude of the people, O Lord, spread their garments in the way; while others cut branches from the trees, and carried them; and they that went before and they that followed after cried aloud, saying: Hosanna to the Son of David! items.slavonic_text: Хотѧ́щꙋ тебѣ̀ вни́ти во ст҃ы́й гра́дъ Гдⷭ҇и, вѣ́тки садо́въ лю́дїе ноша́хꙋ, тебѐ пою́ще всѣ́хъ Влⷣкꙋ, и҆ зрѧ́ще тѧ̀ на жребѧ́ти сѣдѧ́ща, ꙗ҆́коже на Херꙋві́мѣхъ зрѧ́хꙋ, сегѡ̀ ра́ди си́це вопїя́хꙋ: ѡ҆са́нна въ вы́шнихъ, бл҃гослове́нъ є҆сѝ прише́дый, и҆ па́ки грѧды́й во и҆́мѧ Гдⷭ҇не.
items.english_text: *Sticheron 2:* When Thou wast pleased to enter into the holy city, O Lord, the people carried branches of gardens, singing unto Thee, the Master of all; and beholding Thee sitting upon a foal even as upon the Cherubim they beheld Thee, for this cause they cried aloud thus: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed art Thou Who art come, and art coming again in the name of the Lord!

items.slavonic_text: И҆зыди́те ꙗ҆зы́цы, и҆зыди́те и҆ лю́дїе, и҆ ви́дите дне́сь Цр҃ѧ̀ нбⷭ҇наго, ꙗ҆́кѡ на прⷭ҇то́лѣ высо́цѣ, на жребѧ́ти хꙋдѣ̀ ко І҆ерл҃имъ входѧ́ща. Ро́де І҆ꙋде́йскїй невѣ́рный и҆ прелюбодѣ́йный, прїидѝ и҆ ви́ждь, Е҆го́же ви́дѣ И҆са́їа во пло́ти на́съ ра́ди прїитѝ и҆мꙋ́ща, ка́кѡ ᲂу҆невѣ́щиваетъ себѣ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ цѣломꙋ́дренный но́вый Сїѡ́нъ, и҆ ѿлага́етъ ѡ҆сꙋжде́ннꙋю со́нмищꙋ: ꙗ҆́кѡ въ нета́иномъ же бра́цѣ и҆ нескве́рномъ, нескве́рнїи стеко́шасѧ бл҃гохва́лѧще, неискꙋсоѕло́бнїи дѣ́ти, съ ни́миже и҆ мы̀ пою́ще возопїе́мъ пѣ́снь а҆́гг҃льскꙋю: ѡ҆са́нна въ вы́шнихъ, И҆мꙋ́щемꙋ ве́лїю ми́лость.
items.english_text: *Sticheron 3:* Come forth, ye Gentiles! Come forth also, ye peoples, and behold this day the Heavenly King, as upon a lofty throne, entering into Jerusalem upon a lowly foal! O faithless and adulterous Jewish generation, come and see Him Whom Isaiah beheld about to come in the flesh for our sake, how He betroths unto Himself the chaste New Zion, and casts off the condemned synagogue; for as unto an open and undefiled bridal banquet, the undefiled and innocent children ran together with praised acclaim, with whom we also singing cry aloud the angelic hymn: Hosanna in the highest to Him that hath great mercy!

items.english_text: *Sticheron 4:* Giving assurance of the general resurrection before Thy voluntary Passion for the strengthening of all, O Christ God, Thou didst raise dead Lazarus who was four days in the tomb in Bethany by Thy sovereign power; and unto the blind Thou didst grant sight as the Giver of light, O Savior; and Thou didst enter into the holy city with Thy disciples, sitting upon the foal of an ass, fulfilling the prophetic preachings, even as One borne upon the Cherubim; and the Hebrew children went out to meet Thee with branches and palms; therefore we also, carrying branches of olives and palms, cry unto Thee with thanksgiving: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord!

items.slavonic_text: Пре́жде шестѝ дне́й Па́схи, прїи́де І҆и҃съ въ Виѳа́нїю, и҆ пристꙋпи́ша къ немꙋ̀ ᲂу҆чени́цы є҆гѡ̀, глаго́люще є҆мꙋ̀: Гдⷭ҇и, гдѣ̀ хо́щеши ᲂу҆гото́ваемъ тѝ ꙗ҆́сти Па́схꙋ; Ѻ҆́нъ же посла̀ и҆̀хъ, и҆ди́те въ пре́днюю ве́сь, и҆ ѡ҆брѧ́щете чл҃вѣ́ка скꙋ́дельникъ воды̀ носѧ́ща, послѣ́дꙋйте є҆мꙋ̀, и҆ до́мꙋ влады́цѣ рцы́те: ᲊчи́тель гл҃етъ, ᲂу҆ тебѐ сотворю̀ Па́схꙋ со ᲂу҆ченикѝ мои́ми.
items.english_text: Six days before Pascha, Jesus came unto Bethany, and His disciples came unto Him, saying unto Him: Lord, where wilt Thou that we prepare for Thee to eat the Passover? And He sent them: Go ye into the village opposite, and ye shall find a man bearing an earthen jar of water; follow him, and say unto the master of the house: The Teacher saith: With thee will I keep the Passover with My disciples.

items.english_text: *Sticheron 2:* A fearful thing it is to fall into the hands of the living God [Heb. 10:31]. He is the Judge of the thoughts and intents of the heart [Heb. 4:12]; let no one enter tempting the undefiled faith; but in meekness and fear let us draw near unto Christ, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need [Heb. 4:16].

items.english_text: *Sticheron 3:* O wicked and adulterous synagogue, that hast not preserved faith unto thy Husband, why holdest thou the covenant whereof thou wast not the heiress? Why boastest thou of the Father, having rejected the Son? Thou didst not receive the Prophets who foretold the Son; be ashamed at least before thine own children, who cry out thus: Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord!

items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь а҃, гла́съ и҃. І҆рмо́съ: Сокрꙋши́вшемꙋ бра̑ни мы́шцею свое́ю, и҆ прове́дшемꙋ І҆и҃лѧ сквозѣ̀ Чермно́е мо́ре, пои́мъ є҆мꙋ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ И҆зба́вителю на́шемꙋ Бг҃ꙋ: ꙗ҆́кѡ просла́висѧ.
items.english_text: *We say Small Compline, whereon we sing the tri-ode of lord Andrew of Crete. The heirmos twice. The troparia, as many as there be. And the final heirmos by both choirs together. In like manner do we also on the remaining evenings of Great Week, at Compline.*[^51]

items.slavonic_text: І҆ѡ́сифово цѣломꙋ́дрїе подража́вше вѣ́рнїи, разꙋ́момъ почте́мъ чⷭ҇ты́мъ чл҃вѣ́ческое слове́сное сꙋщество̀, всѧ́кимъ хране́нїемъ пожи́вше добродѣ́телїю дѣ́йствительною.
items.english_text: *Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos:* Unto Him Who broke wars with His arm, and led Israel through the Red Sea, let us sing unto Him, as unto our Redeemer God, for He is glorified!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: До́брыхъ недѣ́ланїе оу҆подо́бисѧ смоко́вницѣ: сегѡ̀ оу҆́бѡ оу҆клони́мсѧ, да не и҆́зсхнемъ ꙗ҆́коже ѻ҆на̀ тогда̀, собо́рище ли́ствїемъ покрыва́ющеесѧ преднаписа́ющаѧ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Having imitated the chastity of Joseph, ye faithful, let us with a pure mind honor the rational human nature, having lived in all watchfulness by active virtue.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Ѡ҆́бразъ Влⷣчень подне́съ І҆ѡ́сифъ, въ ро́въ вве́рженъ быва́етъ, продае́тсѧ ѿ срѡ́дникъ, всѧ̑ терпи́тъ приснопа́мѧтный, во ѡ҆́бразъ пои́стиннѣ Хрⷭ҇то́въ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* The non-working of good deeds is likened unto the fig tree; therefore let us turn away from this, lest we wither away as it did then, prefiguring the assembly that covered itself with leaves.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Смоко́вницы безпло́дствїѧ оу҆боя́вшесѧ бра́тїе, разꙋмѣ́имъ ѡ҆́бразъ, да не и҆́зсхнемъ ꙗ҆́коже ѻ҆на̀ тогда̀, є҆гда̀ возвраща́ѧсѧ Чл҃вѣколю́бецъ прїи́де къ не́й а҆́лчѧ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Bearing the Master's image, Joseph is cast into a pit, is sold by his kinsmen, and all things the ever-memorable one endures, truly as a type of Christ.

provenance.verbatim_source:

Bearing the Master's image, Joseph is cast into a pit, is sold by his kinsmen, and all things the ever-memorable one endures, truly as a type of Christ.

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE

items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: І҆и҃съ за ми́ръ тща́сѧ пострада́ти во́лею, и҆́детъ со оу҆чени́ки свои́ми ко гра́дꙋ І҆ерл҃имъ къ во́льнѣй Стрⷭ҇ти, ю҆́же прїи́де пострада́ти.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Fearing the barrenness of the fig tree, brethren, let us understand the figure, lest we wither away as it did then, when returning the Lover of mankind came unto it hungering.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Fearing the barrenness of the fig tree, brethren, let us understand the figure, lest we wither away as it did then, when returning the Lover of mankind came unto it hungering.

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE

items.slavonic_text: Прибли́жившесѧ Гдⷭ҇ни всѧ̀ тща́щемсѧ пострада́ти, гото́ви бꙋ́демъ на ѡ҆плева́нїе, на порꙋга̑нїѧ, и҆ на оу҆ничиже́нїѧ: ꙗ҆́кѡ да пречⷭ҇тыми є҆гѡ̀ Стрⷭ҇тьмѝ спросла́вимсѧ вѣ́рнїи.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Jesus, striving to suffer voluntarily for the world, goes with His disciples unto the city of Jerusalem unto the voluntary Passion, which He is come to suffer.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Стрⷭ҇тьмѝ стра̑сти и҆сцѣлѧ́етъ Пострада́вый ѡ҆ на́съ: хотѧ́ бо произво́дитъ, на на́ше сꙋщество̀ человѣ́ческое, животво́рнаѧ своѧ̑ страда̑нїѧ, да мы̀ спасе́мсѧ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* As all things of the Lord draw near which He is eager to suffer, let us be ready for spitting, for reproaches, and for humiliations, that by His all-pure Sufferings we may be glorified together with Him, ye faithful.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва: Трⷪ҇ицꙋ безнача́льнꙋ прославлѧ́ю, трїѝ ст҃а̀ пою̀, трїѝ соприсносꙋ̑щна во Е҆ди́номъ Сꙋществѣ̀ проповѣ́даю: є҆ди́нъ бо во Ѻ҆ц҃ѣ̀, Сн҃ѣ, и҆ Дс҃ѣ, славосло́витсѧ Бг҃ъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* By His Sufferings He Who suffered for us heals our passions; for willingly He directs His life-creating sufferings upon our human nature, that we may be saved.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
By His Sufferings He Who suffered for us heals our passions; for willingly He directs His life-creating sufferings upon our human nature, that we may be saved.

items.slavonic_text: Сѣда́ленъ, гла́съ д҃. Подо́бенъ: Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ: Смоко́вницы ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїе да не предвари́тъ тѧ̀: но бл҃га̑ѧ плоды̀ потщи́сѧ се́рдца гро́здами дꙋшѐ, Творцꙋ̀ твоемꙋ̀ Хрⷭ҇тꙋ̀ возвестѝ, въ покаѧ́нїи є҆мꙋ̀ приносѧ́щи.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* The Trinity unoriginate I glorify, three holies I sing, three co-ever-existing in One Essence I proclaim; for as One in Father, Son, and Spirit, God is glorified.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
The Trinity unoriginate I glorify, three holies I sing, three co-ever-existing in One Essence I proclaim; for as One in Father, Son, and Spirit, God is glorified.

items.english_text: The rod of Moses and the rod of Aaron showed forth a strange transformation and a dispensation beyond understanding; but thy womb, O Mother of God, renews a new Birth.

items.english_text: *Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):* Let not the condemnation of the fig tree anticipate thee; but strive, O my soul, to make known good fruits with the clusters of the heart unto Christ thy Creator, offering them unto Him in repentance.

items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь и҃. І҆рмо́съ: На горѣ̀ ст҃ѣ́й просла́вльшагосѧ, и҆ въ кꙋпинѣ̀ ѻ҆гне́мъ Приснодѣ́вы Мѡѷсе́ови та́йнꙋ ꙗ҆́вльшаго, Гдⷭ҇а по́йте, и҆ превозноси́те во всѧ̑ вѣ́ки.
items.english_text: *Ode 8. Heirmos:* Unto Him Who was glorified on the holy mountain, and by fire in the bush revealed unto Moses the mystery of the Ever-Virgin, sing unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all for ever!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Цѣломꙋ́дрїемъ оу҆краси́вше житїѐ, и҆ мꙋ́дростїю сохрани́вше вѣ́рꙋ, пра́вды пра́вы взы́щемъ, да къ мꙋ́жествѣ спослѣ́дꙋюще, Хрⷭ҇то́ви сраспне́мсѧ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Having adorned our life with chastity, and having preserved the faith with wisdom, let us seek uprightness of righteousness, that following after courage, we may be crucified together with Christ.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Having adorned our life with chastity, and having preserved the faith with wisdom, let us seek uprightness of righteousness, that following after courage, we may be crucified together with Christ.

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: Дрꙋгꙋ́ю Е҆́вꙋ ѡ҆брѣ́тъ Е҆гѵ́птѧныню, не побѣди́сѧ къ неподо́бномꙋ дѣѧ́нїю, патрїа́рхъ І҆ѡ́сифъ, но ста̀ ꙗ҆́коже нѣ́кїй а҆дама́нтъ, ѿ страсте́й не ꙗ҆́тъ грѣхо́вныхъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Finding a second Eve in the Egyptian woman, the patriarch Joseph was not overcome unto an unfitting deed, but stood like an adamant, not seized by sinful passions.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Finding a second Eve in the Egyptian woman, the patriarch Joseph was not overcome unto an unfitting deed, but stood like an adamant, not seized by sinful passions.

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: Преходѧ̀ жите́йскаѧ ше́ствїѧ Сп҃се мо́й, взалка́лъ є҆сѝ во́лею, сп҃се́нїѧ всѣ́хъ жела́ѧ: сегѡ́ бо взалка́лъ є҆сѝ, ѡ҆браще́нїѧ ѿ тебѐ ꙋ҆дале́нныхъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Passing through the journeys of this life, O my Savior, Thou didst hunger voluntarily, desiring the salvation of all; for of this didst Thou hunger: the conversion of those distanced from Thee.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Passing through the journeys of this life, O my Savior, Thou didst hunger voluntarily, desiring the salvation of all; for of this didst Thou hunger: the conversion of those distanced from Thee.

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: Пра́ѻц҃ъ вкꙋси́въ ѿ дре́ва, ꙗ҆́кѡ позна́сѧ на́гъ и҆ посра́мленъ, ли́ствїе смоко́вное взе́мъ препоѧ́сасѧ: собо́рище бо ѡ҆бнаже́нное Хрⷭ҇та̀ проѡбража́шесѧ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* The forefather, having tasted of the tree, when he knew himself naked and put to shame, took fig leaves and girded himself; for the stripped synagogue prefigured Christ.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
The forefather, having tasted of the tree, when he knew himself naked and put to shame, took fig leaves and girded himself; for the stripped synagogue prefigured Christ.

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: Гото́висѧ дꙋшѐ пре́жде и҆схо́да, оу҆стро́й себѐ ко ѻ҆́номꋋ житїю̀: и҆ Хрⷭ҇тꙋ̀, тебѐ ра́ди пострада́ти тща́щемꙋсѧ, да тѧ̀ просла́витъ, потщи́сѧ спострада́ти, и҆ сраспѧ́тисѧ, и҆ оу҆мре́ти.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Prepare thyself, O my soul, before the departure; order thyself unto that other life; and unto Christ, Who for thy sake is eager to suffer that He may glorify thee, strive to suffer together, and to be crucified together, and to die.

items.english_text: As a Monad in Essence I sing of Thee, as a Trinity in Persons I honor Thee, O Father, and Son, and All-Holy Spirit; the unoriginate dominion of Thy Kingdom I glorify unto the ages.

items.slavonic_text: Чꙋ́жде є҆́сть нечести́вымъ цѣломꙋ́дрїе, и҆ стра́нно пра́ведникѡмъ законопрестꙋпле́нїе: І҆ѡ́сифъ же вели́кїй оу҆клони́сѧ грѣха̀, и҆ цѣломꙋ́дрїѧ бы́сть ѡ҆́бразъ, и҆ подо́бїе пои́стиннꙋ Хрⷭ҇то́во.
items.english_text: The Mother of God prays Thee, O Christ; the assembly of Thine Apostles prays Thee: grant Thy peace unto Thy world, and lavishly bestow Thy tender mercies upon us unto the ages.

items.english_text: *Troparion:* Good order is alien to lawbreakers, and good understanding is strange to the faithless; and the Jews rejected these things through lawlessness, therefore they also alone inherited the curse, even as the fig tree.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: Взалка̀ чл҃вѣ́ческагѡ сп҃се́нїѧ, Хлѣ́бъ сы́й жи́зни, Хрⷭ҇то́съ и҆ Бг҃ъ мо́й, тѣ́мже смоко́вницꙋ предвари́въ, безпло́дное собо́рище, ли́ствїемъ ѡ҆кра́сившꙋю зако́ннѡ, ꙗ҆́кѡ ви́дѣ, прокля́тъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Christ, my God, Who is the Bread of life, hungered for the salvation of mankind; therefore, having anticipated the fig tree—the barren synagogue adorned legally with leaves—when He beheld it, He cursed it.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF PALMS, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: Зако́нное непло́дїе прокля́лъ є҆сѝ, ꙗ҆́кѡ ли́ствїе процвѣта́ющее писмено́вный ра́зꙋмъ, плодо́въ же дѣ́лъ не и҆мꙋ́щее за беззако́нїе: на́съ же всѣ́хъ бл҃года́ти сынѡ́въ, Сп҃се, бл҃гословѝ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou didst curse the barrenness of the Law, as leaves budding the letter's meaning, yet having no fruits of deeds because of lawlessness; but bless us all, the sons of grace, O Savior.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Же́злъ оу҆́бѡ Мѡѷсе́овъ дре́вле въ ѕмїю̀, А҆арѡ́новъ же же́злъ въ зе́лїе преложи́сѧ, и҆ процвѣтѐ ли́ствїе: непло́дное же и҆зсо́хшее собо́рище законопрестꙋ́пное, къ непло́днꙋю преложи́сѧ смоко́вницꙋ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* The rod of Moses of old was changed into a serpent, and the rod of Aaron was changed into foliage and budded leaves; but the law-transgressing, dried-up, barren assembly was changed into the barren fig tree.

items.slavonic_text: Гото́ви І҆ꙋде́є сщ҃е́нники твоѧ̑, и҆ оу҆стро́й рꙋ́цѣ къ бг҃оꙋбі́йствꙋ: сѐ бо прїи́де кро́ткїй и҆ молчали́вый на Стрⷭ҇ть, А҆́гнецъ сы́й и҆ Па́стырь на́шъ, Хрⷭ҇то́съ Цр҃ь І҆и҃левъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Prepare thy priests, O Judah, and set thine hands to the slaying of God; for behold, the meek and quiet One comes unto the Passion, Who is the Lamb and our Shepherd, Christ, King of Israel.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Прїимѝ І҆ꙋде́е Цр҃ѧ̀, сѐ бо на Стрⷭ҇ть прихо́дитъ во́лею, да постра́ждетъ и҆ сп҃се́тъ зовꙋ́щыѧ непреста́ннѡ: бл҃гослове́нъ грѧды́й спастѝ крⷭ҇то́мъ человѣ́ка.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Receive thy King, O Judah; for behold, He comes voluntarily unto the Passion, that He may suffer and save those who cry out unceasingly: Blessed is He that comes to save man by the Cross!

items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ: Прихо́димъ къ моли́твѣ Бцⷣе: твоѧ̑ моли́твами и҆ а҆́п҃лъ твои́хъ, ѻ҆́бщники ны̀ сотворѝ Влⷣко, бл҃ги́хъ твои́хъ, и҆ свѣ́тлости сподо́би Сп҃се, Воскресе́нїѧ твоегѡ̀.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* It is alien to the lawless to glorify Thee, the unoriginate Essence, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, uncreated Almighty power, whereby the whole world is upheld by the beckoning of Thy divine majesty.

items.slavonic_text: И҆ па́ки і҆рмо́съ то́йже: Чꙋ́жде мт҃ремъ: Та́же и҆ про́чее ѡ҆бы́чнѡ. И҆ ѿпꙋ́стъ. Вѣ́домо бꙋ́ди, ꙗ҆́кѡ въ сїю̀ ст҃ꙋ́ю вели́кꙋю Седми́цꙋ є҆ди́ною соверша́емъ ѱалти́рь, и҆ глаго́лемъ на оу҆́тренни каѳі́смы трѝ, и҆ на часѣ́хъ, г҃-мъ, и҆ ѕ҃-мъ, двѣ̀. И҆ соверша́ютсѧ въ сре́дꙋ. Въ вели́кꙋю же Сꙋббѡ́тꙋ стихосло́вѧтсѧ Непоро́чны, къ вече́рнѧхъ же глаго́лемъ ѡ҆бы́чнѡ: Ко Гдⷭ҇ꙋ внегда̀ скорбѣ́ти мѝ:
items.english_text: We draw near unto prayer, O Mother of God: by thy prayers and those of Thine Apostles, make us partakers, O Master, of Thy good things, and count us worthy, O Savior, of the brightness of Thy Resurrection.

provenance.verbatim_source: We draw near unto prayer, O Mother of God: by thy prayers and those of Thine Apostles, make us partakers, O Master, of Thy good things, and count us worthy, O Savior, of the brightness of Thy Resurrection.

items.day_or_date: ON GREAT AND HOLY MONDAY
items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, то́йже. По г҃-мъ стихосло́вїи сѣда́ленъ, гла́съ и҃. Подо́бенъ: Премꙋ́дрости: Стрⷭ҇те́й Гдⷭ҇нихъ нача́тки, настоя́щїй де́нь свѣтоно́ситъ, прїиди́те оу҆́бѡ празднолю́бцы, оу҆срѧ́щимъ пѣ́ньми: Созда́тель бо грѧде́тъ крⷭ҇тъ прїѧ́ти, и҆спыта̑нїѧ и҆ ра́ны, Пїла́томъ сꙋди́мъ, тѣ́мже и҆ ѿ раба̀ оу҆да́ренъ бы́въ по главѣ̀, всѧ̑ терпи́тъ, да спасе́тъ чл҃вѣ́ка, сегѡ̀ ра́ди возопїи́мъ є҆мꙋ̀: чл҃вѣколю́бче Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е, прегрѣше́нїй да́рꙋй ѡ҆ставле́нїе покланѧ́ющымсѧ вѣ́рою пречⷭ҇тымъ Стрⷭ҇те́мъ твои̑мъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Behold, the Bridegroom comes at midnight, and blessed is the servant whom He shall find watching; but unworthy is he again whom He shall find heedless; beware therefore, O my soul, lest thou be weighed down with sleep, lest thou be given over unto death, and be shut out from the Kingdom; but rouse thyself, crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us! *Thrice.*

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Behold, the Bridegroom comes at midnight, and blessed is the servant whom He shall find watching; but unworthy is he again whom He shall find heedless; beware therefore, O my soul, lest thou be weighed down with sleep, lest thou be given over unto death, and be shut out from the Kingdom; but rouse thyself, crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us! *Thrice.*

items.day_or_date: ON GREAT AND HOLY MONDAY
items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, то́йже.
items.english_text: The present day causes the venerable Sufferings to shine forth upon the world like perfect luminaries; for Christ comes to suffer in goodness, He Who holds all things in the palm of His hand, and is pleased to be stretched upon the Tree that He may save man.

provenance.verbatim_source: The present day causes the venerable Sufferings to shine forth upon the world like perfect luminaries; for Christ comes to suffer in goodness, He Who holds all things in the palm of His hand, and is pleased to be stretched upon the Tree that He may save man.

items.day_or_date: ON GREAT AND HOLY MONDAY
items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, то́йже.
items.english_text: O Invisible Judge, how wast Thou seen in the flesh, and goest to be slain by lawless men, condemning our condemnation by Thy Passion? Therefore sending up praise, majesty, and glory unto Thy dominion, O Word, we offer it with one accord.

provenance.verbatim_source: O Invisible Judge, how wast Thou seen in the flesh, and goest to be slain by lawless men, condemning our condemnation by Thy Passion? Therefore sending up praise, majesty, and glory unto Thy dominion, O Word, we offer it with one accord.

items.section: After the 3rd Kathisma Psalmody, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word of God" (Премꙋ́дрости)
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON GREAT AND HOLY MONDAY
items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, то́йже.
items.english_text: The present day brings light as the beginning of the Lord's Sufferings; come, therefore, ye lovers of feasts, let us go out to meet them with hymns; for the Creator comes to receive the Cross, interrogations, and wounds, judged by Pilate; therefore being struck on the head by a servant, He endures all things, that He may save man; for this cause let us cry aloud unto Him: O Lover of mankind, Christ God, grant remission of transgressions unto them that worship with faith Thine all-pure Sufferings!

provenance.verbatim_source: The present day brings light as the beginning of the Lord's Sufferings; come, therefore, ye lovers of feasts, let us go out to meet them with hymns; for the Creator comes to receive the Cross, interrogations, and wounds, judged by Pilate; therefore being struck on the head by a servant, He endures all things, that He may save man; for this cause let us cry aloud unto Him: O Lover of mankind, Christ God, grant remission of transgressions unto them that worship with faith Thine all-pure Sufferings!

items.slavonic_text: И҆ а҆́бїе пое́мъ чте́нїе въ толкова́нїи Е҆ѵⷢ҇лїа є҆́же ѿ Матѳе́а. И҆ Сло́во І҆ѡа́нна Златоꙋ́стагѡ ѡ҆ и҆зсо́хшей смоко́вницѣ, є҆мꙋ́же нача́ло: Ꙗ҆́коже оу҆́бѡ ви́да: И҆ Сло́во Дамаски́ново ѡ҆ и҆зсо́хшей смоко́вницѣ: и҆ ѡ҆ при́тчи виногра́да. Та́же, И҆ ѡ҆ сподо́битися на́мъ: Е҆ѵⷢ҇лїе ѿ Матѳе́а, зача́ло п҃д, без̾ престꙋ́пки: Во вре́мѧ ѻ҆́но, возвра́щсѧ І҆и҃съ во гра́дъ, взалка̀: Коне́цъ, въ зача́лѣ п҃и-мъ: И҆ да́стся ꙗ҆зы́кꙋ творѧ́щемꙋ плоды̀ є҆гѡ̀. Посе́мъ ѱало́мъ н҃. Та́же: Спасѝ Бж҃е лю́ди твоѧ̑: Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй в҃i. Трипѣ́снецъ, творе́нїе господи́на Космы̀, є҆гѡ́же краестро́чїе: Тῇ δευτέρᾳ, си́речь: ко вторы́й де́нь, є҆́же є҆́сть понедѣ́льникъ. І҆рмо́съ по два́жды, тропарѝ на ѐi. Припѣ́въ: Сла́ва тебѣ̀ Бж҃е на́шъ, сла́ва тебѣ̀. (Се́й во всю̀ седми́цꙋ). Послѣ́дїй і҆рмо́съ, ѻ҆́ба ли́ка вкꙋ́пѣ:
items.english_text: *And immediately we read a reading in the Commentary on the Gospel according to Matthew.*[^55]

items.slavonic_text: Гла́съ в҃. Пѣ́снь а҃. І҆рмо́съ: Т Непроходи́мое волнѧ́щееся мо́ре, бж҃їимъ свои́мъ велѣ́нїемъ и҆зсꙋши́вшемꋋ, и҆ пѣшеше́ствовати сквозѣ̀ ѐ пѣ́шѣстїѧ лю́ди наста́вльшемꋋ, Гдⷭ҇ви пои́мъ, сла́внѡ бо просла́висѧ.
items.english_text: *And the Homily of John Chrysostom on the withering of the fig tree, the beginning whereof is: "Even as the appearance..."*[^56]

items.slavonic_text: И Неизрече́нное Сло́ва Бж҃їя схожде́нїе, є҆́же Хрⷭ҇то́съ то́йжде є҆́сть Бг҃ъ и҆ чл҃вѣ́къ, є҆́же Бг҃ъ невосхище́нїемъ бы́ти непщева́въ, внегда̀ воѡбража́тися рабо́мъ, показꙋ́етъ оу҆ченико́мъ, сла́внѡ бо просла́висѧ.

items.slavonic_text: І҆́косъ: На рыда́нїе ны́нѣ приложи́мъ рыда́нїе, и҆ и҆злїе́мъ сле́зы со І҆а́кѡвомъ, пла́чꙋщеся І҆ѡ́сифа приснопа́мѧтнагѡ и҆ цѣломꙋ́дреннагѡ, порабоще́ннагѡ оу҆́бѡ тѣ́ломъ, дꙋ́шꙋ же непорабоще́нꙋ соблю́дшагѡ, и҆ Е҆гѵ́птомъ всѣ́мъ црⷭ҇твовавшагѡ: Бг҃ъ бо подае́тъ рабо́мъ свои̑мъ вѣне́цъ нетлѣ́нный.
items.english_text: *The Tri-ode, the composition of lord Cosmas, the acrostic whereof is: Τῇ δευτέρᾳ, that is: "On the second day," which is Monday. The heirmos twice, the troparia unto 12.*[^58]

items.slavonic_text: Во ст҃ы́й и҆ вели́кїй Понедѣ́льникъ па́мѧть твори́мъ бл҃же́ннагѡ І҆ѡ́сифа прекра́снагѡ, и҆ и҆зсо́хшїя смоко́вницы: зане́же нача́ло ѿсю́дꙋ прїе́млютъ ст҃ы̑я Стрⷭ҇ти Гдⷭ҇а на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭ҇та̀:
items.english_text: Unto Him Who by His divine command dried up the impassable surging sea, and guided the pedestrian people to march on foot through it, let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified!

items.slavonic_text: І҆ѡ́сифа же во ѡ҆́бразъ сегѡ̀ пе́рвѣе прїе́млется. Се́й оу҆́бѡ сы́нъ послѣ́днїй бя́ше патрїа́рха І҆а́кѡва, ѿ Рахи́ли є҆мꙋ̀ рожде́нный, ѿ свои́хъ же бра́тїй позави́дѣнъ бы́въ нѣ́кихъ ра́ди во снѣ̀ видѣ́нїй. Пре́жде оу҆́бѡ ко и҆скопа́нїе ро́ва скрыва́ется: и҆ ѻ҆тцꙋ̀ є҆гѡ̀ ѿ дѣте́й пре́лестїю ѡ҆крокавле́нною ри́зою оу҆крада́ется, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѿ ѕвѣ́рей ꙗ҆де́нъ бы́сть. Та́же на три́десѧтыхъ сре́бреницѣхъ про́данъ быва́етъ І҆смаи́лтѡмъ, и҆̀же па́ки продаю́тъ є҆го̀ Пентефрі́ю, нача́льникꙋ скопце́й царя̀ є҆гѵ́петскагѡ фараѡ́на. Неи́стовствовавшей же госпожѣ̀ є҆гѡ̀ на цѣломꙋ́дрїе ю҆́ноши, поне́же беззако́нїя содѣ́яти не восхотѣ̀, ри́зꙋ ѡ҆ста́вль ѿбѣжѐ: ѻ҆на́ же гди́нꙋ свое́мꋋ ѡ҆болга́етъ є҆го̀, и҆ оу҆́зы и҆ темни́ца сегѡ̀ прїе́млетъ. Та́же разрѣше́нїемъ снѡ́въ и҆зводи́тся, и҆ царю̀ ꙗ҆вля́ется, и҆ гди́нъ всеѧ̀ землѝ є҆гѵ́петскїя поставля́ется. Па́ки же пшеницода́тельствомъ бра́тїямъ ꙗ҆вле́нъ быва́етъ, и҆ всѧ́ческагѡ своего̀ живота̀ до́брѣ препровожде́нїя, во Е҆гѵ́птѣ оу҆мира́етъ, вели́кїй во цѣломꙋ́дрїи при и҆нѣ́хъ є҆гѡ̀ до́брыхъ познава́емый. Ѡ҆́бразъ же се́й Хрⷭ҇то́въ: занѐ и҆ Хрⷭ҇то́съ ѿ є҆диноплеме́нныхъ І҆ꙋде́й зави́стнꙋемь быва́етъ, и҆ ѿ оу҆чени́ка на три́десѧти сре́бреницѣхъ продае́тся, и҆ ко мра́чный и҆ те́мный ро́въ гро́ба, заключа́ется, и҆ ѿтꙋ́дꙋ самовла́стнѡ восторги́вся, црⷭ҇твꙋетъ над̾ є҆гѵ́птомъ: ꙗ҆́кѡ на всѧ́кїй грѣ́хъ, и҆ до конца̀ сегѡ̀ побѣжда́етъ, мі́ромъ же всѣ́мъ ѡ҆облада́етъ, и҆ чл҃вѣколю́бнѡ и҆скꙋпꙋ́етъ на́съ та́инственнымъ пшеницода́тельствомъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ са́мъ себѐ за на́съ да́вый, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ пита́етъ на́съ нбⷭ҇нымъ хлѣ́бомъ, свое́ю живоно́сною Пло́тїю. По семꙋ̀ оу҆́бѡ словесѝ, прекра́сный І҆ѡ́сифъ ны́нѣ прїе́млется.
items.english_text: ...And Joseph is first taken as a type of this. For he was the youngest son of the patriarch Jacob, born to him of Rachel, envied by his own brethren on account of certain dreams. First he was hidden in an excavated pit, and stolen from his father by his children with a deceitfully blood-stained coat, as though he had been devoured by beasts. Then he was sold for thirty pieces of silver unto the Ishmaelites, who in turn sold him unto Potiphar, chief of the eunuchs of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. And when his mistress raged against the chastity of the youth, because he would not commit lawlessness, he left his garment and fled; but she slandered him unto her master, and bonds and prison received him. Then by the interpretation of dreams he was brought out, and presented unto the king, and appointed ruler over all the land of Egypt. And again by the distribution of corn he was made known unto his brethren, and having spent all his life well, he died in Egypt, known as great in chastity alongside his other virtues. And he is a type of Christ: for Christ also is envied by the Jews of His own tribe, and sold by His disciple for thirty pieces of silver, and shut up in the dark and gloomy pit of the tomb; and bursting forth thence by His own sovereign power, He reigns over Egypt—that is, over every sin, and vanquishes it unto the end—and rules over the whole world, and as the Lover of mankind redeems us by the mystical distribution of corn, since He gave Himself for us, and feeds us with heavenly bread, His life-bearing Flesh. In accordance with this discourse, therefore, Joseph the All-Comely is commemorated this day.

items.slavonic_text: Здѣ́ же и҆ ѡ҆ и҆зсо́хшей смоко́вницѣ па́мѧть твори́мъ: зане́же бж҃е́ственнїи є҆ѵⷢ҇ли́сти, си́рѣчь, Матѳе́й и҆ Ма́рко, по повѣ́сти ѡ҆ ва́їахъ прино́сятъ: Во оу҆́трїе же и҆зше́дшымъ и҆̀мъ ѿ Виѳа́нїи, взалка̀. Дрꙋгі́й же: Оу҆́трꙋ же возвра́щся ко гра́дъ, гла́етъ, взалка̀, и҆ ви́дѣвъ смоко́вницꙋ ли́ствїе то́кма и҆мꙋ́щꙋю, не бѣ́ бо вре́мя смо́квамъ, прїи́де къ не́й, и҆ є҆лма̀, плода̀ не ѡ҆брѣ́те на не́й, речѐ: Да не ктомꙋ̀ пло́дъ ѿ тебѐ бꙋ́детъ во вѣ́ки: и҆ и҆́зсше а҆́бїе смоко́вница. Смоко́вница оу҆́бѡ є҆́сть, со́нмище І҆ꙋде́йское, на не́мже плода̀ подо́бнагѡ Сп҃съ не ѡ҆брѣ́тъ, то́чїю сѣнѣ́ющее зако́на, и҆ сїѐ ѿѧ́тъ ѿ ни́хъ, пра́здное всѧ́чески содѣ́лавъ. А҆́ще ли же кто̀ рече́тъ: почто̀ бездꙋ́шное дре́во сꙋ́хо бы́сть, кля́твꙋ взе́мшее не согрѣши́вшее; да нака́жетъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ І҆ꙋде́е ви́дѧще Хрⷭ҇та̀ при́снѡ всѣ̑хъ бл҃годѣ́тельствующа, никомꙋ́же ключи́мое ско́рбно содѣва́юща, непрека́хꙋ, ꙗ҆́кѡ си́лꙋ и҆́матъ то́чїю бл҃годѣ́тельствовати, злотвори́ти же, нѝ. Человѣколю́бивъ же Влⷣка сы́й, не восхотѣ̀ на человѣ́цѣ сїѐ показа́ти, и҆ семꙋ̀ бы́ти: да оу҆́бѡ оу҆вѣ́ритъ неблагода́рныя лю́ди, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆́матъ си́лꙋ и҆ къ мще́нїю дово́льнꙋю: ꙗ҆́кѡ бла́гъ же не хо́щетъ, на бездꙋ́шномъ и҆ нечꙋ́вственномъ є҆стествѣ̀ мще́нїе содѣва́етъ. Вкꙋ́пѣ же нѣ́кое и҆ неизглаго́ланное сло́во є҆́сть, ѿ ста́рецъ премꙋ́дрыхъ къ на́мъ прише́дшее. Ꙗ҆́коже глаго́летъ І҆сі́дѡръ Пилосиѡ́тъ: ꙗ҆́кѡ дре́во престꙋпле́нїя сїѐ бы́сть, є҆гѡ́же и҆ ли́ствїе къ покро́вꙋ престꙋ́пльшии оу҆потреби́ша, тѣ́мже и҆ прокля́тся ѿ Хрⷭ҇та̀ человѣколю́бнѡ, поне́же тогда̀ сїѐ не пострада̀, ктомꙋ̀ плода̀ не принестѝ вино́вна грѣхꙋ̀. И҆ ꙗ҆́коже грѣ́хъ смо́кви оу҆подобля́ется, бл҃гохва́льнѡ: и҆́матъ бо оу҆слажда́ющее сла́сти, прилѣпля́емое грѣха̀, и҆ ѡ҆жесточава́ющее послѣдѝ, и҆ поплютка́ющее со́вѣстїю. Ѡ҆ба́че ѿ сїи́хъ смоко́внична по́вѣсть здѣ̀ оу҆чрежде́нїя ра́ди положи́ся, ꙗ҆́коже І҆ѡ́сифа ра́ди за є҆́же носи́ти ѡ҆́бразъ Хрⷭ҇то́въ. Є҆́сть же смоко́вница всѧ́ка дꙋша̀, всѧ́кагѡ дꙋхо́внагѡ плода̀ неприча́стна: къ не́йже оу҆́трѡ, по настоя́щей а҆́бїе жи́зни, не ѡ҆брѣ́тыи Гдⷭ҇ь поко́я оу҆ нея̀, оу҆сꙋша́етъ ю҆̀ кля́твою, и҆ къ вѣ́чный посыла́етъ ѻ҆́гнь, и҆ сто́лпъ нѣ́кїй стои́тъ оу҆сꙋше́нный, оу҆страша́ѧй не дѣ́лающихъ приклада́емагѡ добродѣ́телей плода̀.
items.english_text: Here also we make commemoration of the withered fig tree: for the divine Evangelists, namely Matthew and Mark, record after the narrative concerning the palms: "On the morrow, when they were come from Bethany, He hungered" [Mark 11:12]. And the other says: "Now in the morning, as He returned into the city, He hungered; and seeing a fig tree having only leaves, for the time of figs was not yet, He came unto it, and when He found no fruit thereon, He said: Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever; and presently the fig tree withered away" [Matt. 21:18-19]. The fig tree is the Jewish synagogue, wherein the Savior found not fitting fruit, but only the shadow of the Law; and this He took away from them, making it utterly void. But if anyone say: For what reason did an inanimate tree become dry, taking a curse having not sinned? Let him know that the Jews, seeing Christ ever doing good unto all and causing no one any grief, objected that He had power only to do good, but not to do evil. And the Master, being the Lover of mankind, was not pleased to show this upon a man, lest it so happen; therefore, that He might convince the ungrateful people that He hath also sufficient power for vengeance, yet as the Good One desires it not, upon an inanimate and insensate nature He works vengeance. Together with this, there is also a certain ineffable saying that hath come down unto us from the most wise elders, even as Isidore of Pelusium says:[^60] that this was the tree of transgression, whose leaves the transgressors used for a covering; therefore also it was cursed by Christ as the Lover of mankind, since it did not suffer then, that it might no longer bear fruit that was guilty of sin. And that sin is likened unto a fig is praiseworthy: for it hath that which sweetens with pleasure, the stickiness of sin, and which hardens afterwards and torments the conscience. Nevertheless, from these things the narrative of the fig tree is set forth here for moral instruction, even as for Joseph because he bore the type of Christ. For every soul is a fig tree that is destitute of every spiritual fruit; unto which in the morning, immediately after the present life, the Lord finding no rest therein, dries it up with a curse, and sends it into eternal fire; and it stands as a withered pillar, terrifying them that bring not forth the fitting fruit of virtues.

Heirmos [Acrostic: E]:* The unwearied fire, nourished in boundless fuel, was terrified by the devout youths, whose undefiled body was conformed unto the soul, and drew back; and as the flame dried up before the ever-living One, an everlasting hymn was sung: All ye works of the Lord, sing unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all for ever!

items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, гла́съ то́йже: Гдⷭ҇и, грѧды́й къ страда́нїю, твоя̑ оу҆твержда́лъ оу҆чени́ки, глаго́лалъ є҆сѝ, ѻ҆со́бь прїе́мъ и҆́хъ: ка́кѡ глаго́лъ мои́хъ не по́мните, ꙗ҆́же пре́жде реко́хъ ва́мъ: ꙗ҆́кѡ всѧ́комꋋ прⷪ҇ро́кꙋ нѣ́сть пи́сано, то́кмѡ во І҆ерл҃имѣ оу҆бїе́нꙋ бы́ти; Ны́нѣ оу҆́бѡ вре́мя наста́етъ, є҆́же реко́хъ ва́мъ: сѐ бо предаю́ся, рꙋка́ма грѣ́шныхъ порꙋ́ганъ бы́ти, и҆̀же и҆ крⷭ҇тꙋ́ мя пригвозди́вше, и҆ погребе́нїю преда́вше, ѡ҆ме́рзена вмѣня́тъ ꙗ҆́кѡ ме́ртва, ѻ҆ба́че дерза́йте: тридне́венъ бо воста́нꙋ, въ ра́дость вѣ́рныхъ, и҆ жи́знь вѣ́чнꙋю.
items.english_text: Thy bridal chamber I behold adorned, O my Savior, and I have no garment that I may enter therein; enlighten the vesture of my soul, O Giver of light, and save me!

provenance.verbatim_source: Thy bridal chamber I behold adorned, O my Savior, and I have no garment that I may enter therein; enlighten the vesture of my soul, O Giver of light, and save me!

items.english_text: *Sticheron 1:* The Lord, going unto the voluntary Passion, said unto the Apostles on the way: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be betrayed, even as it is written concerning Him [Matt. 20:18]. Come therefore, we also, with cleansed thoughts, let us journey with Him, and let us be crucified together, and let us put to death for His sake the pleasures of this life, that we may also live with Him, and hear Him crying aloud: No longer unto the earthly Jerusalem, in order to suffer; but I ascend unto My Father, and your Father, and unto My God, and your God [John 20:17], and I will raise you up together into the Jerusalem above, into the Heavenly Kingdom! *Twice.*

Now therefore the time is come which I told you: for behold, I am betrayed to be mocked by the hands of sinners, who having both nailed Me to the Cross and delivered Me to burial, shall reckon Me abhorred as dead; nevertheless, take courage, for on the third day I will arise unto the joy of the faithful and life everlasting!

items.slavonic_text: Та́же, Бл҃го є҆́сть: и҆ про́чая по ѡ҆бы́чаю съ покло́ны. Та́же Ѿпꙋ́стъ: Гряды́й Гдⷭ҇ь на во́льнꙋю Стрⷭ҇ть, на́шегѡ ра́ди сп҃се́нїя, Хрⷭ҇то́съ и҆́стинный: Се́й же Ѿпꙋ́стъ глаго́лется во вто́рникъ и҆ въ сре́дꙋ. Вѣ́домо же бꙋ́ди, ꙗ҆́кѡ на а҃-мъ часѣ̀ и҆ ѳ҃-мъ, ѱалти́рь не глаго́лемъ въ вели́кꙋю Седми́цꙋ: но то́чїю глаго́лются триѱа́лмы, по ѡ҆бы́чаю. Тре́тїй же ча́съ и҆ шесты́й пое́мъ со ѱалти́ремъ. Чте́тся же и҆ ЧЕТВЕРОЕВГГЕЛЇЕ, въ понедѣ́льникъ, во вто́рникъ и҆ въ сре́дꙋ соверша́ется.
items.english_text: *Sticheron 3:* Fearing the rebuke of the fig tree withered for barrenness, brethren, let us bring forth worthy fruits of repentance unto Christ, Who bestows great mercy upon us.

items.slavonic_text: При часѣ̀ г҃-мъ днѐ, оу҆даря́етъ параекклисїа́рхъ въ би́ло, ꙗ҆́коже є҆́сть ѡ҆бы́чай. И҆ со́бравшемся въ це́рковь, ПОЕ́МЪ Г҃-Й ЧА́СЪ, съ каѳі́смою: и҆ тво́рѧще ѡ҆бы́чныѧ покло́ны. Та́же тропа́рь: Гдⷭ҇и и҆́же прест҃а́го твоегѡ̀ Дх҃а: и҆ Бцⷣе ты̀ є҆сѝ лоза̀: покло́ны г҃. И҆ а҆́бїе оу҆краше́нъ а҆налѡ́гїю, положа́тъ на не́мъ верхꙋ̀ ст҃о́е ЧЕТВЕРОЕВꙁГГЕ́ЛЇЕ и҆ двѣма̀ лампа́дома возже́ннома. Всѣ̑мъ же стоя́щымъ ѿкрове́нными глава́ми. Сщ҃е́нникъ же кади́тъ хра́мъ ве́сь, и҆ бра́тїю. А҆ на ѕ҃-мъ часѣ̀ кади́тъ то́кмѡ Е҆ѵⷢ҇лїе. На ѳ҃-мъ часѣ̀ Е҆ѵⷢ҇лїе кади́тъ, и҆ хра́мъ ве́сь, и҆ бра́тїю: И҆ та́кѡ чте́тъ Е҆ѵⷢ҇лїе. items.english_text: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was in the midst of the captivity by the river Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God. On the fifth day of the month, this was the fifth year of the captivity of king Jehoiachin, the word of the Lord came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was upon me. And I looked, and behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was round about it, and out of the midst thereof as the color of amber, out of the midst of the fire, and brightness was in it. Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures; and this was their appearance: they had the likeness of a man. And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. And their legs were straight, and their feet were winged, and sparkled like the color of burnished brass, and their wings were swift. And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and their faces and their wings were joined one to another across the four; their faces turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward. As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side; and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle. And their faces and their wings were stretched upward on the four; two wings of every one were joined one to another, and two covered their bodies above; and they went every one straight forward: whither the spirit was to go, they went; and they turned not as they went. And in the midst of the living creatures was an appearance like burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of torches turning back and forth in the midst of the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning. And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning. Now as I beheld, behold, one wheel upon the earth by the four living creatures. The appearance of the wheels and their workmanship was like unto the appearance of beryl, and they four had one likeness; and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel. When they went, they went upon their four sides; and they turned not when they went. As for their rings, they had both height; and I beheld them, and the rings of all four were full of eyes round about. And when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them; and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up. Whithersoever the cloud was to go, there was also the spirit to go; the living creatures went, and the wheels were lifted up with them; for the spirit of life was in the wheels.

items.slavonic_text: дне́хъ, си́рѣчь, въ понедѣ́льникъ, во вто́рникъ, въ сре́дꙋ: И҆ соверша́ется въ сре́дꙋ на ѳ҃-мъ часѣ̀. Быва́ютъ же ѿ Лꙋкѝ чте́нїя трѝ. Про́чая же по два̀. Вкꙋ́пѣ всѣ́хъ чте́нїй де́вять, и҆ ка́пше ничто́же. Девя́тый же ча́съ тре́хъ дне́й стїхосло́вїа не и҆́мать, ꙗ҆́коже рече́ся. Но по триѱа́лмїи пое́тся ѿ оу҆чи- не́ннагѡ мона́ха: И҆́же въ девя́тый ча́съ: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ: И҆́же на́съ ра́ди рожде́йся ѿ Дѣ́вы: И҆ быва́етъ чте́- нїе въ Четвероева́нгелїи: По не́мже глаго́лемъ: Не преда́ждь на́съ до конца̀: Трисвѧто́е съ покло́ны. По Ѻ҆́ч҃е на́шъ: Конда́къ днѐ. Въ црⷭ҇твїи твое́мъ: И҆ про́чее послѣ́дованїе, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆бы́чно. Глаго́лемъ же и҆ конда́къ днѐ. Приготовля́емъ же и҆ вече́рню.
items.english_text: *The Ninth Hour of these three days has no chanting of the Psalter, as has been said. But after the three Psalms, the appointed monk sings: "O Thou Who at the Ninth Hour;" "Glory... Both now... Thou Who for our sake wast born of the Virgin." And the reading from the Four Gospels takes place. After which we say: "Deliver us not up utterly unto the end;" the Trisagion with prostrations. After "Our Father:" the Kontakion of the day; "In Thy Kingdom," and the rest of the sequence, as is customary. We say also the Kontakion of the day; and we prepare also for Vespers.*[^67]

items.slavonic_text: Гла́съ е҃: Дости́гше вѣ́рнїи спаси́тельнꙋю Стрⷭ҇ть Хрⷭ҇та̀ Бг҃а, неизрече́нное є҆гѡ̀ долготерпѣ́нїе просла́вимъ: ꙗ҆́кѡ да бл҃гоꙋтро́бїемъ свои́мъ совоздви́гнетъ и҆ на́съ оу҆мерщвле́нныхъ грѣхо́мъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ бл҃гъ и҆ чл҃вѣколю́бецъ. Два́жды.
items.english_text: The Lord, going unto His voluntary Passion, said unto the Apostles on the way: "Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered up, as it is written concerning Him." Come therefore, and let us also, with minds purified, travel with Him, and be crucified with Him, and be mortified for His sake unto the pleasures of this life, that we may also live with Him, and hear Him crying aloud: "No longer do I ascend unto the earthly Jerusalem to suffer, but I ascend unto My Father and your Father, and unto My God and your God; and I will exalt you together with Myself into the Jerusalem on high, into the Heavenly Kingdom." *(Twice)*

items.slavonic_text: Гдⷭ҇и, къ та́инствꙋ неизглаго́ланномꋋ твоегѡ̀ смотре́нїя, не довлѣ́ющи сыновѡ́въ Зеведе́овыхъ ма́ти, проша́ше тя̀, вре́меннагѡ црⷭ҇тва по́чести дарова́тися ча́дѡмъ є҆я̀: но вмѣ́стѡ тоя̀, ча́шꙋ сме́рти ѡ҆бѣщава́лъ є҆сѝ пи́ти дрꙋгѡ́мъ твои̑мъ: ю҆́же ча́шꙋ пре́жде си́хъ пи́ти са́мъ глаго́лалъ є҆сѝ, грѣхѡ́въ ѡ҆чище́нїе, тѣ́мже тебѣ̀ вопїе́мъ: спасе́нїе дꙋ́шъ на́шихъ, сла́ва тебѣ̀. Два́жды.
items.english_text: Having attained the saving Passion of Christ God, O ye faithful, let us glorify His ineffable longsuffering, that by His tender mercy He may raise up together also us who have been slain by sin, for He is good and the Lover of mankind. *(Twice)*

items.english_text: O Lord, going unto Thy suffering, Thou didst establish Thy disciples, and taking them aside, didst say: "How do you not remember My words, which I spoke unto you before: that it is written of every prophet that he should be slain nowhere except in Jerusalem? Now therefore the time is at hand, concerning which I told you; for behold, I am delivered up into the hands of sinners to be mocked, who also having nailed Me to the Cross and given Me over to burial, shall account Me an abomination as one dead. Nevertheless, take courage; for on the third day I shall rise, unto the joy of the faithful and life everlasting." *(Twice)*

items.english_text: O Lord, the mother of the sons of Zebedee, not comprehending the ineffable mystery of Thy dispensation, asked of Thee that the honors of a temporal kingdom might be granted unto her children. But instead of this, Thou didst promise Thy friends that they should drink the cup of death, which cup Thou didst say that Thou Thyself wouldest drink before them, for the cleansing of sins. Therefore we cry unto Thee: O Salvation of our souls, glory be to Thee! *(Twice)*

items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, гла́съ то́йже: Вторꙋ́ю Е҆́вꙋ Е҆гѵ́птѧныню ѡ҆брѣ́тъ ѕмі́й глаго́лы, тща́шеся ласка́ньми запя́ти І҆ѡ́сифа, но то́й ѡ҆ста́вивъ ри́зꙋ, бѣжа̀ грѣха̀: и҆ на́гъ не стыдя́шеся, ꙗ҆́коже первозда́нный пре́жде преслꙋша́нїя, тогѡ̀ мл҃твами, Хрⷭ҇тѐ, поми́лꙋй на́съ.
items.english_text: The serpent, finding in the Egyptian woman a second Eve, sought through flattery to supplant Joseph; but he, leaving his garment behind, fled from sin, and being naked was not ashamed, even as the first-formed man before the transgression. By his intercessions, O Christ, have mercy on us!

items.slavonic_text: И҆схо́да чте́нїе, глава̀ а҃: Сїя̑ и҆мена̀ сынѡ́въ І҆и҃левыхъ, входя́щихъ во Е҆гѵ́петъ вкꙋ́пѣ со І҆а́кѡвомъ ѻ҆тце́мъ и҆́хъ, кі́йждо со всѣ́мъ до́момъ свои́мъ внидо́ша: Рꙋви́мъ, Сѷмеѡ́нъ, Левíй, І҆ꙋ́да, І҆ссаха́ръ, Завꙋлѡ́нъ, и҆ Венїами́нъ, Да́нъ, и҆ Нефѳали́мъ, Га́дъ и҆ А҆си́ръ: І҆ѡ́сифъ же бя́ше во Е҆гѵ́птѣ. Бя́ше же всѣ́хъ дꙋ́шъ, и҆зше́дшихъ и҆з̾ І҆а́кѡва, се́дмьдесятъ пя́ть. Оу҆́мре же І҆ѡ́сифъ, и҆ вся̀ бра́тїя є҆гѡ̀, и҆ ве́сь ро́дъ ѻ҆́ный. Сы́нове же І҆и҃левы возрасто́ша, и҆ оу҆мно́жишася, и҆ мно́зи бы́ша, и҆ оу҆крѣпи́шася ѕѣлѡ̀ ѕѣлѡ̀: оу҆мно́жи же и҆́хъ земля̀. Воста́ же ца́рь и҆́нъ во Е҆гѵ́птѣ, и҆́же не зна́ше І҆ѡ́сифа. Рече́ же ꙗ҆зы́кꙋ своемꋋ: сѐ ро́дъ сынѡ́въ І҆и҃левыхъ вели́кое мно́жество, и҆ оу҆крѣпля́ется па́че на́съ. Прїиди́те оу҆́бѡ, прехи́тримъ и҆́хъ, да не когда̀ оу҆мно́жатся: и҆ є҆гда̀ а҆́ще приключи́тся на́мъ бра́нь, приложа́тся и҆ сїи́ къ сꙋпоста́тѡмъ, и҆ ѡ҆долѣ́вше на́мъ, и҆зы́дꙋтъ и҆з̾ землѝ (на́шеѧ.) И҆ приста́ви над̾ ни́ми приста́вники дѣ́лъ, да ѡ҆ѕло́бятъ и҆́хъ въ дѣ́лѣхъ: и҆ созда́ша гра́ды тве́рды фараѡ́нꙋ, Пиѳѡ̀, и҆ Рамессѝ, и҆ ѽ҆́нъ, и҆́же є҆́сть И҆лїо́поль. Поели́кꙋ же и҆́хъ смиря́хꙋ, толи́кѡ мно́жайшїи быва́хꙋ, и҆ оу҆крѣпля́хꙋся ѕѣлѡ̀ ѕѣлѡ̀, и҆ гнꙋша́хꙋся Е҆гѵ́птяне сынмѝ І҆и҃левыми: И҆ наси́лїе твора́хꙋ Е҆гѵ́птяне сынѡ́мъ І҆и҃левымъ нꙋ́ждею. И҆ болѣ́зненнꙋ тѣ́мъ жи́знь твора́хꙋ въ дѣ́лѣхъ жесто́кихъ, бре́нїемъ, и҆ плїнѳодѣ́ланїемъ, и҆ всѣ́ми дѣлы̀, ꙗ҆́же въ поля́хъ, по всѣ́хъ дѣ́лѣхъ, и҆́миже порабоща́хꙋ и҆́хъ съ нꙋ́ждею. И҆ речѐ ца́рь Е҆гѵ́петскїй ба́бамъ Е҆вре́йскимъ: є҆ди́ной и҆́хъ и҆́мя Сепфѡ́ра, и҆ и҆́мя второ́й Фꙋ́а. И҆ речѐ (и҆̀мъ:) Е҆гда̀ ба́бите Е҆вре́анынямъ, и҆ сꙋ́ть къ рожде́нїю, а҆́ще оу҆́бѡ мꙋ́жескїй по́лъ бꙋ́детъ, оу҆бива́йте є҆го̀: а҆́ще же же́нскїй, снабдѣва́йте є҆го̀. Оу҆боя́шася же ба́бы Бг҃а, и҆ не сотвори́ша, ꙗ҆́коже повелѣ̀ и҆̀мъ ца́рь Е҆гѵ́петскїй, и҆ живля́хꙋ мꙋ́жескїй по́лъ. Призва́ же ца́рь Е҆гѵ́петскїй ба́бы, и҆ речѐ и҆̀мъ: что̀ ꙗ҆́кѡ сотвори́сте ве́щь сїю̀, и҆ ѡ҆живля́ете мꙋ́жескїй по́лъ; Реко́ша же ба́бы фараѡ́нꙋ: не ꙗ҆́кѡ жены̀ Е҆гѵ́птяныни, та́кѡ и҆ жены̀ Е҆вре́аныни: ражда́ютъ бо пре́жде не́же вни́ти къ ни̑мъ ба́камъ, и҆ ражда́хꙋ. Бла́го же твора́ше Бг҃ъ ба́бамъ, и҆ мно́жахꙋся лю́дїе, и҆ оу҆крѣпля́хꙋся ѕѣлѡ̀.

items.slavonic_text: И҆схо́да чте́нїе, глава̀ а҃: Сїя̑ и҆мена̀ сынѡ́въ І҆и҃левыхъ, входя́щихъ во Е҆гѵ́петъ вкꙋ́пѣ со І҆а́кѡвомъ ѻ҆тце́мъ и҆́хъ, кі́йждо со всѣ́мъ до́момъ свои́мъ внидо́ша: Рꙋви́мъ, Сѷмеѡ́нъ, Левíй, І҆ꙋ́да, І҆ссаха́ръ, Завꙋлѡ́нъ, и҆ Венїами́нъ, Да́нъ, и҆ Нефѳали́мъ, Га́дъ и҆ А҆си́ръ: І҆ѡ́сифъ же бя́ше во Е҆гѵ́птѣ. Бя́ше же всѣ́хъ дꙋ́шъ, и҆зше́дшихъ и҆з̾ І҆а́кѡва, се́дмьдесятъ пя́ть. Оу҆́мре же І҆ѡ́сифъ, и҆ вся̀ бра́тїя є҆гѡ̀, и҆ ве́сь ро́дъ ѻ҆́ный. Сы́нове же І҆и҃левы возрасто́ша, и҆ оу҆мно́жишася, и҆ мно́зи бы́ша, и҆ оу҆крѣпи́шася ѕѣлѡ̀ ѕѣлѡ̀: оу҆мно́жи же и҆́хъ земля̀. Воста́ же ца́рь и҆́нъ во Е҆гѵ́птѣ, и҆́же не зна́ше І҆ѡ́сифа. Рече́ же ꙗ҆зы́кꙋ своемꋋ: сѐ ро́дъ сынѡ́въ І҆и҃левыхъ вели́кое мно́жество, и҆ оу҆крѣпля́ется па́че на́съ. Прїиди́те оу҆́бѡ, прехи́тримъ и҆́хъ, да не когда̀ оу҆мно́жатся: и҆ є҆гда̀ а҆́ще приключи́тся на́мъ бра́нь, приложа́тся и҆ сїи́ къ сꙋпоста́тѡмъ, и҆ ѡ҆долѣ́вше на́мъ, и҆зы́дꙋтъ и҆з̾ землѝ (на́шеѧ.) И҆ приста́ви над̾ ни́ми приста́вники дѣ́лъ, да ѡ҆ѕло́бятъ и҆́хъ въ дѣ́лѣхъ: и҆ созда́ша гра́ды тве́рды фараѡ́нꙋ, Пиѳѡ̀, и҆ Рамессѝ, и҆ ѽ҆́нъ, и҆́же є҆́сть И҆лїо́поль. Поели́кꙋ же и҆́хъ смиря́хꙋ, толи́кѡ мно́жайшїи быва́хꙋ, и҆ оу҆крѣпля́хꙋся ѕѣлѡ̀ ѕѣлѡ̀, и҆ гнꙋша́хꙋся Е҆гѵ́птяне сынмѝ І҆и҃левыми: И҆ наси́лїе твора́хꙋ Е҆гѵ́птяне сынѡ́мъ І҆и҃левымъ нꙋ́ждею. И҆ болѣ́зненнꙋ тѣ́мъ жи́знь твора́хꙋ въ дѣ́лѣхъ жесто́кихъ, бре́нїемъ, и҆ плїнѳодѣ́ланїемъ, и҆ всѣ́ми дѣлы̀, ꙗ҆́же въ поля́хъ, по всѣ́хъ дѣ́лѣхъ, и҆́миже порабоща́хꙋ и҆́хъ съ нꙋ́ждею. И҆ речѐ ца́рь Е҆гѵ́петскїй ба́бамъ Е҆вре́йскимъ: є҆ди́ной и҆́хъ и҆́мя Сепфѡ́ра, и҆ и҆́мя второ́й Фꙋ́а. И҆ речѐ (и҆̀мъ:) Е҆гда̀ ба́бите Е҆вре́анынямъ, и҆ сꙋ́ть къ рожде́нїю, а҆́ще оу҆́бѡ мꙋ́жескїй по́лъ бꙋ́детъ, оу҆бива́йте є҆го̀: а҆́ще же же́нскїй, снабдѣва́йте є҆го̀. Оу҆боя́шася же ба́бы Бг҃а, и҆ не сотвори́ша, ꙗ҆́коже повелѣ̀ и҆̀мъ ца́рь Е҆гѵ́петскїй, и҆ живля́хꙋ мꙋ́жескїй по́лъ. Призва́ же ца́рь Е҆гѵ́петскїй ба́бы, и҆ речѐ и҆̀мъ: что̀ ꙗ҆́кѡ сотвори́сте ве́щь сїю̀, и҆ ѡ҆живля́ете мꙋ́жескїй по́лъ; Реко́ша же ба́бы фараѡ́нꙋ: не ꙗ҆́кѡ жены̀ Е҆гѵ́птяныни, та́кѡ и҆ жены̀ Е҆вре́аныни: ражда́ютъ бо пре́жде не́же вни́ти къ ни̑мъ ба́камъ, и҆ ражда́хꙋ. Бла́го же твора́ше Бг҃ъ ба́бамъ, и҆ мно́жахꙋся лю́дїе, и҆ оу҆крѣпля́хꙋся ѕѣлѡ̀.
items.english_text: Now these are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt together with Jacob their father; every one entered with all his house: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin, Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. But Joseph was in Egypt. And all the souls that came out of Jacob were seventy and five. And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation. And the children of Israel increased, and multiplied, and became numerous, and grew exceedingly strong; and the land multiplied them. Now there arose another king in Egypt, who knew not Joseph. And he said unto his people: "Behold, the race of the children of Israel is a great multitude, and is stronger than we. Come therefore, let us deal craftily with them, lest they multiply; and if war should happen to fall upon us, they also will join themselves unto our adversaries, and having overcome us, they will go forth out of our land." And he set over them taskmasters, that they might afflict them in their works. And they built strong cities for Pharaoh: Pithom, and Raamses, and On, which is Heliopolis.[^70] But the more they afflicted them, so much the more numerous they became, and grew exceedingly strong; and the Egyptians abhorred the children of Israel. And the Egyptians compelled the children of Israel with violence. And they made their life bitter with hard labors, in mortar, and in brick-making, and in all labors in the fields, in all their works wherein they enslaved them with violence. And the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the second Puah; and he said unto them: "When you act as midwives to the Hebrew women, and they are at the birth, if it be a male child, kill him; but if it be a female, preserve her." But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but preserved the male children alive. And the king of Egypt called the midwives, and said unto them: "Why is it that you have done this thing, and preserved the male children alive?" And the midwives said unto Pharaoh: "Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they give birth before the midwives come in unto them, and they were delivered." And God dealt well with the midwives; and the people multiplied, and grew exceedingly strong.

items.slavonic_text: [Орнаментальная разделительная виньетка]
items.english_text: There was a certain man in the land of Ausitis [Uz], whose name was Job; and that man was true, blameless, righteous, and godly, departing from every evil matter. And there were born unto him seven sons, and three daughters. And his cattle were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses feeding, and exceedingly many servants; and great works were his upon the earth; and that man was the noblest of all that were in the east of the sun. And his sons went and feasted one with another every day, taking with them also their three sisters to eat and drink with them. And when the days of the feast were finished, Job sent and purified them, rising up early in the morning; and he offered sacrifices for them according to their number, and one calf for sin for their souls; for Job said: "Lest perhaps my sons have sinned, and thought evil against God in their mind." Thus therefore did Job all the days. And it came to pass on this day, that behold, the Angels of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and the devil came also with them. And the Lord said unto the devil: "Whence comest thou?" And the devil answered the Lord, and said: "Having gone round about the earth, and walked under heaven, here I am." And the Lord said unto him: "Hast thou considered in thy mind My servant Job? For there is none like him upon the earth, a man blameless, true, godly, departing from every evil matter." And the devil answered and said before the Lord: "Doth Job honor the Lord for nought? Hast not Thou hedged about his outward things, and the inward parts of his house, and all that he hath on every side round about? The works of his hands Thou hast blessed, and his cattle Thou hast multiplied upon the earth. But put forth Thine hand, and touch all that he hath: surely he will bless Thee to Thy face!" Then said the Lord unto the devil: "Behold, all that he hath I give into thy hand, but upon himself touch thou not." And the devil went forth from the presence of the Lord.

items.slavonic_text: На трапе́зѣ же, ꙗ҆ди́мъ сꙋхоꙗде́нїе, и҆ си̑мъ оу҆доволѧ́емся. И҆ ꙗ҆́коже въ пе́рвꙋю недѣ́лю ст҃а́гѡ сегѡ̀ поста̀: си́це и҆ въ сїя̑ дни̑, въ вели́кїй Понедѣ́льникъ, во вто́рникъ и҆ въ сре́дꙋ пости́тися подоба́етъ. Вѣ́дати бо подоба́етъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ шесты́й вели́кїй Собо́ръ повелѣ̀, спаси́тельныя Стрⷭ҇ти дни̑ въ постѣ̀, и҆ мл҃твѣ, и҆ оу҆миле́нїи се́рдца сотворя́ти вѣ́рнымъ: къ полꙋ́нощи же вели́кїя Сꙋббѡ́ты ѡ҆ставля́ти по́стъ, бж҃е́ственнымъ Є҆ѵаггели́стѡмъ Матѳе́ю и҆ Лꙋцѣ̀, ѻ҆́вомꋋ оу҆́бѡ по́здѣ къ сꙋббѡ́тѣ глаго́ланїемъ: ѻ҆́вомꋋ же оу҆́тромъ глꙋбо́кимъ, медля́емое на́мъ но́щи написо́ющымъ.
items.english_text: *At the table, we eat dry food, and with this we are satisfied. And even as in the first week of this holy fast, so also in these days, on Great Monday, on Tuesday, and on Wednesday, it is fitting to fast.*[^72]

items.english_text: *For it is fitting to know that the Sixth Great Council commanded the faithful to pass the days of the saving Passion in fasting, prayer, and contrition of heart; and to cease the fast towards midnight of Great Saturday, the divine Evangelists Matthew and Luke describing the night that delays us, the one speaking of late on the Sabbath, and the other of the deep dawn.*[^73]

items.slavonic_text: По́йдемъ со Хрⷭ҇то́мъ къ горѣ̀ Є҆леѡ́нетстѣй, та́йнѡ со а҆пⷭ҇лы соводвори́мся є҆мꙋ̀. Разꙋмѣ́й смире́нное моѐ се́рдце, что́ є҆́сть же́рновная при́тча, ѡ҆ не́йже пре́жде речѐ Хрⷭ҇то́съ, и҆ и҆стрезви́ся про́чее. Гото́ви сама̀ себѐ, ѽ дꙋшѐ моя̀, ко и҆схо́дꙋ: прише́ствїе приближа́ется невмоли́магѡ Сꙋдїѝ.
items.english_text: *Ode 2, Tone 8. Heirmos:* Attend, O heaven, and I will speak, and will hymn Christ, Who was born of the Virgin for our salvation.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: И҆́нъ. Гла́съ то́йже. І҆рмо́съ: Ви́дите, ви́дите, ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́зъ є҆́смь Бг҃ъ, дре́вле І҆и҃ля сквозѣ̀ Чермно́е мо́ре проведы́й, и҆ пита́вый, и҆ спасы́й, и҆ ѿ го́рькїя рабо́ты свободи́вый фараѡ́новы.
items.english_text: Let us go with Christ unto the Mount of Olives, and let us mystically take up our abode with the Apostles beside Him.

provenance.verbatim_source: Let us go with Christ unto the Mount of Olives, and let us mystically take up our abode with the Apostles beside Him.

items.english_text: Understand, O my humble heart, what is the parable of the millstones, concerning which Christ spoke before, and henceforth become sober.[^75]

items.english_text: See, see that I am God, Who of old led Israel through the Red Sea, and fed, and saved him, and delivered him from the bitter bondage of Pharaoh.

items.english_text: See, see that I am God, Who before the existence of all things, and before the creation of earth and heaven, knows all things; and Who am entirely in the Father, and bear all things within Myself.

items.slavonic_text: Сло́вомъ соста́вихъ нб҃о вкꙋ́пѣ и҆ зе́млю: со Ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ во вѣ́цѣхъ, и҆ сло́вомъ ношꙋ̀ вся̑, ꙗ҆́кѡ Сло́во, Мꙋ́дрость, и҆ Си́ла, и҆ Ѻ҆́бразъ, и҆ содѣ́йствителенъ, и҆ равнодѣ́теленъ. Кто̀ времена̀ положѝ; кто̀ вѣ́ки соблюда́й; кто̀ вся̑ оу҆предвѣ́дый, и҆ совоздвиза́яй, ра́звѣ Безнача́льный при́снѡ сы́й со Ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ, ꙗ҆́коже заря̀ со свѣ́тѣ; Ѡ҆ безмѣ́рнагѡ твоегѡ̀ человѣколю́бїя І҆и҃се! сказа́лъ бо є҆сѝ на́мъ сконча́нїя свы́ше вре́мя, скры́въ ча́съ, оу҆жа́сныхъ же свѣ́тлѡ ѡ҆́бразы є҆гѡ̀. Вся̑ вѣ́си, вся̑ зна́еши І҆и҃се, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆мѣ́яй всѐ въ себѣ̀ Ѻ҆́чее состоя́нїе бж҃е́ственнѣ, и҆ всего̀ Дх҃а взае́мна нося́й въ себѣ̀, соприсносꙋ́щнаго Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ̀. Влⷣко Гдⷭ҇и, вѣкѡ́въ Тво́рче, сподо́би и҆ на́съ свяще́нный ѻ҆́ный тогда̀ гла́съ оу҆слы́шати, зовꙋ́щїй и҆збра́нныя Ѻ҆тца̀ въ Црⷭ҇тво нбⷭ҇ное.
items.english_text: Who appointed the times? Who preserves the ages? Who foreknew and raises up all things together, save the Unoriginate One Who is ever with the Father, like the radiance with the light?

items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва: Безнача́льная, несозда́нная Трⷪ҇це, нераздѣ́льная Е҆ди́нице, тро́е сꙋ́щая и҆ є҆ди́но, Ѻ҆́ч҃е, Сн҃е и҆ Дх҃е, є҆ди́ный Бж҃е, прїимѝ пѣ́нїе ѿ бре́нныхъ ꙗ҆зы́къ, ꙗ҆́коже ѿ оу҆́стъ пла́менныхъ.
items.english_text: O the measureless loving-kindness of Thee, O Jesus! For Thou didst tell us from on high the time of the consummation, while hiding the hour, yet brightly revealing the images of its terrors.

provenance.verbatim_source: O the measureless loving-kindness of Thee, O Jesus! For Thou didst tell us from on high the time of the consummation, while hiding the hour, yet brightly revealing the images of its terrors.

items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ: Бг҃оро́диченъ: Селе́нїе ст҃о́е ꙗ҆ви́лася є҆сѝ Дѣ́во Бж҃їе: въ тя́ бо нбⷭ҇ный Цр҃ь всели́вся пло́тїю, про́йде кра́сный, человѣ́ка въ себѣ̀ воѡбрази́въ бж҃е́ственнѣ.
items.english_text: All things Thou knowest, all things Thou discernest, O Jesus, as possessing in Thyself the entire Fatherly subsistence divinely, and bearing in Thyself the whole Spirit mutually, Who is co-eternal with the Father.

provenance.verbatim_source: All things Thou knowest, all things Thou discernest, O Jesus, as possessing in Thyself the entire Fatherly subsistence divinely, and bearing in Thyself the whole Spirit mutually, Who is co-eternal with the Father.

items.slavonic_text: Сѣда́ленъ, гла́съ в҃. Подо́бенъ: Милосе́рдїя сꙋ́щи: Милосе́рдїемъ дви́жимь Хрⷭ҇тѐ, во́лею преды́деши страда́ти Бл҃годѣ́телю, хотя́й страсте́й на́съ и҆зба́вити, и҆ є҆́же во а҆́дѣ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїя: тѣ́мже честна̑я твоя̑ воспѣва́емъ Страда́нїя, и҆ сла́вимъ Сп҃се кра́йнее твоѐ всѐ схожде́нїе.
items.english_text: O Master and Lord, Creator of the ages, account also us worthy then to hear that sacred voice, calling the chosen of the Father into the Heavenly Kingdom.

items.slavonic_text: Вся́кѡ слы́шала є҆сѝ дꙋшѐ, ка́кѡ Хрⷭ҇то́съ бж҃е́ственнымъ оу҆чени́кѡмъ свои̑мъ провозглаша́ше, глаго́ля сконча́нїе: разꙋмѣ́вши же тво́й коне́цъ, оу҆гото́вися про́чее: вре́мя и҆схо́да прїи́де. Позна́ла є҆сѝ непло́дная дꙋшѐ, лꙋка́вагѡ раба̀ при́тчꙋ, бо́йся и҆ не небрезѝ ѡ҆ дарова́нїи, є҆го́же прїя́ла є҆сѝ, да не сокры́еши въ зе́млю, но да кꙋ́плю дѣ́еши. Да оу҆ясни́тся свѣща̀, да преизлїе́тся се́й и҆ є҆ле́й, ꙗ҆́коже дѣ́вамъ тогда̀ сострада́нїе, да оу҆кра́сиши дꙋшѐ моя̀ черто́гъ Хрⷭ҇то́въ тогда̀ ѿве́рстый. Въ сꙋббѡ́тꙋ бѣ́гство и҆ въ зимѣ̀ гла̀ Оу҆чи́тель, седма́гѡ вѣ́рю предгада́тельствꙋетъ настоя́щагѡ вѣ́ка, въ не́мже на́йдетъ ꙗ҆́кѡ зима̀ кончи́на. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ско́рость мо́лнїи преходя́щая, та́кѡ тогда̀ бꙋ́детъ стра́шное ѻ҆́ное Влⷣки твоегѡ̀ прише́ствїе, дꙋшѐ моя̀: слы́шала є҆сѝ, гото́ва про́чее бы́ти потщи́ся. Є҆гда̀ прїи́детъ Сꙋдїя̀ съ ты́сящами тогда̀ и҆ тма́ми а҆́гг҃льскихъ чинѡ́въ и҆ си́лъ, кі́й стра́хъ дꙋшѐ моя̀, кі́й тре́петъ; оу҆вы̀ мнѣ̀, наги̑мъ стоя́щымъ всѣ̑мъ.
items.english_text: O Unoriginate, Uncreated Trinity, Undivided Unity, existing threefold and one, O Father, Son, and Spirit, the one God: receive the hymnody from clay tongues, even as from flaming lips.

provenance.verbatim_source: O Unoriginate, Uncreated Trinity, Undivided Unity, existing threefold and one, O Father, Son, and Spirit, the one God: receive the hymnody from clay tongues, even as from flaming lips.

items.english_text: A holy habitation hast thou shown thyself to be, O Virgin of God: for in thee the Heavenly King dwelt in the flesh, and came forth all-fair, having divinely fashioned man in Himself.

Да оу҆ясни́тся свѣща̀, да преизлїе́тся се́й и҆ є҆ле́й, ꙗ҆́коже дѣ́вамъ тогда̀ сострада́нїе, да оу҆кра́сиши дꙋшѐ моя̀ черто́гъ Хрⷭ҇то́въ тогда̀ ѿве́рстый. Въ сꙋббѡ́тꙋ бѣ́гство и҆ въ зимѣ̀ гла̀ Оу҆чи́тель, седма́гѡ вѣ́рю предгада́тельствꙋетъ настоя́щагѡ вѣ́ка, въ не́мже на́йдетъ ꙗ҆́кѡ зима̀ кончи́на. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ско́рость мо́лнїи преходя́щая, та́кѡ тогда̀ бꙋ́детъ стра́шное ѻ҆́ное Влⷣки твоегѡ̀ прише́ствїе, дꙋшѐ моя̀: слы́шала є҆сѝ, гото́ва про́чее бы́ти потщи́ся. Є҆гда̀ прїи́детъ Сꙋдїя̀ съ ты́сящами тогда̀ и҆ тма́ми а҆́гг҃льскихъ чинѡ́въ и҆ си́лъ, кі́й стра́хъ дꙋшѐ моя̀, кі́й тре́петъ; оу҆вы̀ мнѣ̀, наги̑мъ стоя́щымъ всѣ̑мъ.
items.english_text: Thou hast known, O barren soul, the parable of the wicked servant; fear, and neglect not the gift which thou hast received, that thou hide it not in the earth, but trade therewith.

provenance.verbatim_source: Thou hast known, O barren soul, the parable of the wicked servant; fear, and neglect not the gift which thou hast received, that thou hide it not in the earth, but trade therewith.

items.english_text: When the Judge shall come with thousands then and ten thousands of angelic ranks and powers, what fear, O my soul, what trembling! Woe is me, when all shall stand naked!

items.office: ON HOLY AND GREAT MONDAY, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON HOLY AND GREAT MONDAY, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: Бл҃гослови́мъ Ѻ҆ц҃а̀, и҆ Сн҃а, и҆ ст҃а́го Дх҃а, Гдⷭ҇а. Є҆ди́нъ Бг҃ъ оу҆́бѡ Трⷪ҇ца, ни Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ̀ и҆згꙋби́вшꙋ въ сво́йство, нижѐ Сн҃ꙋ премѣни́вшꙋся во и҆схожде́нїе, но сво́йственная, и҆ своѐ, свѣ́тъ, Бг҃а, трѝ сла́влю во вѣ́ки.
items.english_text: God is one, even the Trinity: neither hath the Father lost His proper characteristic, nor hath the Son been changed into procession, but possessing Their proper attributes, and Their own, as Light and God, Three do I glorify unto the ages.

provenance.verbatim_source: God is one, even the Trinity: neither hath the Father lost His proper characteristic, nor hath the Son been changed into procession, but possessing Their proper attributes, and Their own, as Light and God, Three do I glorify unto the ages.

items.office: ON HOLY AND GREAT MONDAY, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON HOLY AND GREAT MONDAY, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: Хва́лимъ, бл҃гослови́мъ, покланя́емся Гдⷭ҇ви, пою́ще и҆ превознося́ще во вся̑ вѣ́ки. Та́же І҆рмо́съ: А҆́гг҃ли и҆ нб҃са̀ на прⷭ҇то́лѣ: Пѣ́снь ѳ҃. І҆рмо́съ: Проꙗвле́нное на горѣ̀ законополо́жникꙋ во ѻ҆гнѝ и҆ кꙋпинѣ̀, Ржⷭ҇тво̀ Приснодѣ́вы, въ на́ше вѣ́рныхъ сп҃се́нїе, пѣ́ньми немо́лчными велича́емъ.
items.english_text: By the intercessions of the Mother of God, O God, receive our prayer, and send down Thy mercies richly upon all, and grant Thy peace unto Thy people.

provenance.verbatim_source: By the intercessions of the Mother of God, O God, receive our prayer, and send down Thy mercies richly upon all, and grant Thy peace unto Thy people.

items.office: ON HOLY AND GREAT MONDAY, AT COMPLINE
items.season_or_tone: PART I: GREAT AND HOLY PASCHA AND BRIGHT WEEK
items.day_or_date: ON HOLY AND GREAT MONDAY, AT COMPLINE
items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ, Бг҃оро́диченъ: Прїимѝ Мт҃рь твою̀ Хрⷭ҇тѐ къ моли́твѣ, да мл҃твами є҆я̀ оу҆мири́ши мі́ръ, и҆ оу҆тверди́ши црⷭ҇твїя ски́птры, и҆ Цр҃кви твоя̑ совокꙋпи́ши во є҆ди́но.
items.english_text: *Ode 9. Heirmos:* The Nativity of the Ever-Virgin, prefigured on the mountain unto the Lawgiver in fire and the bush, for the salvation of us the faithful, with unceasing hymns do we magnify.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Nativity of the Ever-Virgin, prefigured on the mountain unto the Lawgiver in fire and the bush, for the salvation of us the faithful, with unceasing hymns do we magnify.

items.slavonic_text: І҆рмо́съ ѳ҃-я пѣ́сни: Проꙗвле́нное на горѣ̀: за Досто́йно: И҆ покло́нъ до землѝ. Трист҃о́е. И҆ по Ѻ҆́ч҃е на́шъ: Конда́къ днѐ. Та́же, Гдⷭ҇и си́лъ съ на́ми бꙋ́ди: И҆ про́чее ѡ҆бы́чное. И҆ ѿпꙋ́стъ.
items.english_text: Thou hast heard, O my soul, the Judge foretelling and teaching thee the time of the consummation: prepare the works that pertain unto departure, lest as one untested thou be rejected of God.

provenance.verbatim_source: Thou hast heard, O my soul, the Judge foretelling and teaching thee the time of the consummation: prepare the works that pertain unto departure, lest as one untested thou be rejected of God.

items.slavonic_text: А҆λληлꙋ́їа, на гла́съ и҃. Тропа́рь три́жды: Сѐ Жени́хъ гряде́тъ: пи́санъ въ Понедѣ́льникъ вели́кїй, ли́стъ л҃з. И҆ ѡ҆бы́чное стїхосло́вїе. По а҃-мъ стїхосло́вїи сѣда́ленъ, гла́съ д҃. Подо́бенъ: Вознесы́йся на крⷭ҇тъ: Жениха̀ бра́тїе возлю́бимъ, свѣщы̑ своя̑ оу҆краси́мъ, въ добродѣ́телехъ сїя́юще и҆ вѣ́рѣ пра́вой: да ꙗ҆́кѡ мꙋ̑дрыя Гдⷭ҇ни дѣ̑вы гото́ви вни́демъ съ ни́мъ на бра́ки: Жени́хъ бо да́ры, ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ всѣ̑мъ подае́тъ, нетлѣ́нный вѣне́цъ. Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, то́йже.
items.english_text: Brethren, let us love the Bridegroom, let us adorn our lamps, shining with virtues and right faith, that like the wise virgins of the Lord we may be ready to enter with Him into the marriage banquet; for the Bridegroom, as God, grants unto all an incorruptible crown as His gift.

items.slavonic_text: Та́же, И҆ ѡ҆ сподо́битися на́мъ: Е҆ѵⷢ҇лїе ѿ Матѳе́а, зача́ло ч҃ без̾ престꙋ́пки: Во вре́мя ѻ҆́но, совѣ́тъ прїе́мше всѝ фарисе́е на І҆и҃са, ꙗ҆́кѡ да ѡ҆больстя́тъ є҆го̀ сло́вомъ: Коне́цъ въ зача́лѣ ч҃ѕ-мъ: Бл҃гослове́нъ гряды́й во и҆́мя Гдⷭ҇не. Пое́мъ, ѱало́мъ н҃. Та́же, Спасѝ Бж҃е лю́ди твоя̑: Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй, в҃і. По се́мъ є҆ктенїа̀ ма́лая.
items.english_text: O Savior, the priests and scribes, having maliciously gathered an unlawful council against Thee through envy, moved Judas unto betrayal; therefore shamelessly he went forth, saying against Thee unto the lawless people: "What will you give me," says he, "and I will deliver Him into your hands?" From this condemnation deliver our souls, O Lord!

items.english_text: Judas in his mind becomes a lover of money; he rises up hostilely against the Master; he takes counsel and studies betrayal; he falls from the light, receiving darkness; he agrees upon the price, and sells Him Who is Priceless; therefore also hanging, the recompense for what he wrought, does the wretch find, and a bitter death, having betrayed Thee, the Lord. From his portion deliver us, O Christ God, granting forgiveness of transgressions unto those who celebrate Thy most pure Passion in faith.

items.slavonic_text: Та́же КОНДА́КЪ, гла́съ в҃. Подо́бенъ: Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀: Ча́съ дꙋшѐ конца̀ помы́сливши, и҆ посѣче́нїя смоко́вницы оу҆боя́вшися, да́нный тебѣ̀ тала́нтъ трудолю́бнѡ дѣ́лай ѻ҆кая́нная, бо́дрствꙋющи и҆ зовꙋ́щи: да не пребꙋ́демъ внѣ̀ черто́га Хрⷭ҇то́ва.
items.english_text: Having considered the hour of the end, O my soul, and having feared the cutting down of the fig tree, diligently cultivate the talent that was given unto thee, O wretched one, being watchful and crying aloud: "Let us not remain outside the bridal chamber of Christ!"

items.slavonic_text: І҆́косъ: Что̀ оу҆ныва́еши дꙋшѐ моя̀ ѻ҆кая́нная; что̀ мечта́еши безвре́меннѡ попече́нїя неполе́зная; что̀ оу҆пражня́ешися къ мимотекꙋ́щымъ; послѣ́днѣйшїй ча́съ є҆́сть ѿтолѣ̀, и҆ разлꙋчи́тися и҆́мамы ѿ сꙋ́щихъ здѣ̀. До́ндеже вре́мя и҆́маши, возни́кни зовꙋ́щи: согрѣши́хъ тѝ, Сп҃се мо́й, не посѣцы̀ менѐ, ꙗ҆́коже непло́днꙋю смоко́вницꙋ, но ꙗ҆́кѡ бл҃гоꙋтро́бенъ Гдⷭ҇и, оу҆ще́дри со стра́хомъ зовꙋ́щꙋю: да не пребꙋ́демъ внѣ̀ черто́га Хрⷭ҇то́ва.
items.english_text: *Ikos:* Why dost thou despond, O my wretched soul? Why dost thou imagine unseasonably unprofitable anxieties? Why art thou occupied with passing things? The final hour is at hand from henceforth, and we are to be parted from the things that are here. While thou hast time, arise and cry aloud: "I have sinned against Thee, O my Savior; cut me not down like the barren fig tree, but as Thou art tender-hearted, O Lord, have compassion on me who cry with fear: Let us not remain outside the bridal chamber of Christ!"

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ikos:*
Why dost thou despond, O my wretched soul? Why dost thou imagine unseasonably unprofitable anxieties? Why art thou occupied with passing things? The final hour is at hand from henceforth, and we are to be parted from the things that are here. While thou hast time, arise and cry aloud: "I have sinned against Thee, O my Savior; cut me not down like the barren fig tree, but as Thou art tender-hearted, O Lord, have compassion on me who cry with fear: Let us not remain outside the bridal chamber of Christ!"

items.day_or_date: Synaxarion.*[^78]
items.slavonic_text: Лѣ́ность дале́че на́съ ѿве́ржимъ, и҆ свѣ́тлыми свѣща́ми безсме́ртнаго Жениха̀ Хрⷭ҇та̀ пѣ́нїемъ оу҆сря́щимъ, бл҃гослови́те, вопїю́ще, дѣла̀ Гдⷭ҇ня Гдⷭ҇а.
items.english_text: On Holy and Great Tuesday, we make commemoration of the Parable of the Ten Virgins. For such parables the Lord, going up to Jerusalem and journeying unto His Passion, spoke unto His disciples, and there are parables which He extended also unto the Jews. The Parable of the Ten Virgins, turning it unto almsgiving, He spoke, at the same time teaching that all should be prepared before the end. For He told them much concerning virginity, and concerning eunuchs; and virginity hath great glory, for it is truly great. But lest anyone, fulfilling this work, should neglect other virtues, and especially almsgiving, whereby the lamp of virginity is enlightened, the Holy Gospel introduces this parable. And five it calls wise, as having joined with virginity also the abundant and rich oil of almsgiving; but five it calls foolish, as they also indeed possessed virginity, but had an incomparable lack of almsgiving. On this account they are called foolish, because having accomplished the greater, they neglected the lesser, and differed in nothing from harlots: for the latter indeed were overcome by the flesh, but the former by possessions. And the night of this present life passing away, all the virgins slumbered, that is to say, they died: for sleep is called death. And while they were sleeping, a cry arose at midnight; and those indeed who had brought oil in abundance, the doors being opened, entered with the Bridegroom; but the foolish, having an insufficient supply of oil, sought it after their sleep. But the wise, though wishing to give, were unable, and before entering answered, saying: "Lest perhaps there should not be enough for us and you, go you to them that sell, that is to say, to the poor, and buy; but with difficulty, for after death this is impossible." Which also Abraham shows concerning the rich man and Lazarus, saying: "There is an impassable gulf, so that they cannot cross over from hence thither." But the foolish, having come unenlightened, cry aloud thus, knocking at the gate: "Lord, Lord, open unto us!" But the Lord Himself through Himself gives that dread answer: "Depart," saying, "I know you not; for how will you see the Bridegroom, not having the bridal gift, even almsgiving itself?" On account of this figure, therefore, the Parable of the Ten Virgins was appointed by the God-bearing Fathers to be placed here, instructing us ever to watch and to be prepared for the meeting of the true Bridegroom, by good works, and especially by almsgiving; because the day and hour of the end are unknown: even as through Joseph we acquire chastity, and through the fig tree we ever bring forth spiritual fruit. For he who accomplishes one single and greatest deed, but neglects others, and especially almsgiving, shall not enter with Christ into eternal rest, but returns back put to shame. For nothing is more mournful, and more full of disgrace, than virginity overcome by possessions.[^79] But, O Christ the Bridegroom, unite us with the wise virgins, and number us with Thy chosen flock, and have mercy on us. Amen.
