items.slavonic_text: Ѱало́мъ ч҃: Живы́й въ по́мощи Вы́шнѧгѡ, въ кро́вѣ Бг҃а нбⷭ҇нагѡ водвори́тсѧ. Рече́тъ Гдⷭ҇ви: застꙋ́пникъ мо́й є҆сѝ, и҆ прибѣ́жище моѐ, Бг҃ъ мо́й, и҆ ᲂу҆пова́ю на него̀. Ꙗ҆́кѡ то́й и҆зба́витъ тѧ̀ ѿ сѣ́ти ло́вчи, и҆ ѿ словесѐ мѧте́жна. Плещма̀ свои́ма ѡ҆сѣни́тъ тѧ̀, и҆ подъ крилѣ̀ є҆гѡ̀ надѣ́ешисѧ: ѻ҆рꙋ́жїемъ ѡ҆бы́детъ тѧ̀ и҆́стина є҆гѡ̀. Не ᲂу҆бои́шисѧ ѿ стра́ха нощна́гѡ, ѿ стрѣлы̀ летѧ́щїѧ во днѝ: Ѿ ве́щи во тмѣ̀ преходѧ́щїѧ, ѿ срѧ́ща и҆ бѣ́са полꙋ́деннагѡ. Паде́тъ ѿ страны̀ твоеѧ̀ ты́сѧща, и҆ тма̀ ѡ҆деснꙋ́ю тебѐ, къ тебѣ́ же не прибли́житсѧ. Ѻ҆ба́че ѻ҆чи́ма твои́ма смо́триши, и҆ воздаѧ́нїе грѣ́шникѡвъ ᲂу҆́зриши. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ты̀ Гдⷭ҇и, ᲂу҆пова́нїе моѐ, вы́шнѧго положи́лъ є҆сѝ прибѣ́жище твоѐ. Не прїи́детъ къ тебѣ̀ ѕло̀, и҆ ра́на не прибли́житсѧ тѣлесѝ твоемꙋ̀. Ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́гг҃лѡмъ свои̑мъ заповѣ́сть
items.english_text: Save me, O God, by Thy name, and judge me by Thy strength. Hear my prayer, O God; give ear to the words of my mouth. For strangers are risen up against me, and mighty men have sought after my soul; they have not set God before them. For behold, God is my helper, and the Lord is the protector of my soul. He shall turn evils back upon mine enemies; destroy them in Thy truth. Willingly will I sacrifice unto Thee; I will confess Thy name, O Lord, for it is good. For Thou hast delivered me out of all tribulation, and mine eye hath looked down upon mine enemies.

items.english_text: Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man; rescue me from the unrighteous man. Who have devised iniquities in their heart; all the day long did they prepare wars. They have sharpened their tongue like a serpent; the poison of asps is under their lips. Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner; rescue me from unrighteous men, who have purposed to trip up my steps. The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords have they spread for a net for my feet; they have set stumbling-blocks for me near the path. I said unto the Lord: "Thou art my God; give ear, O Lord, to the voice of my supplication." O Lord, O Lord, the strength of my salvation, Thou hast overshadowed my head in the day of battle. Deliver me not, O Lord, from my desire unto the sinner; they have plotted against me: forsake me not, lest they should be exalted. As for the head of them that compass me about, the labor of their lips shall cover them. Coals of fire shall fall upon them; Thou shalt cast them down into afflictions, and they shall not stand. A man full of tongue shall not prosper upon the earth; evils shall hunt the unrighteous man unto destruction. I know that the Lord will maintain the cause of the afflicted, and vengeance for the poor. Surely the righteous shall confess Thy name, and the upright shall dwell with Thy presence.

items.english_text: He that dwells in the help of the Most High shall abide in the shelter of the God of heaven. He shall say unto the Lord: "Thou art my protector and my refuge, my God, and in Him will I hope." For He shall deliver thee from the snare of the hunters, and from the troubling word. With His shoulders shall He overshadow thee, and under His wings shalt thou hope; His truth shall compass thee with a shield. Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror of the night, nor for the arrow that flies by day; nor for the thing that walks in darkness, nor for the mishap and the noonday demon. A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand, but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold, and see the reward of sinners. For Thou, O Lord, art my hope; Thou hast made the Most High thy refuge. There shall no evil come unto thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling. For He shall give His angels charge...

На рꙋка́хъ во́змꙋтъ тѧ̀, да не когда̀ преткне́ши ѡ҆ ка́мень но́гꙋ твою̀: На а҆спі́да и҆ васілі́ска настꙋ́пиши, и҆ попере́ши льва̀ и҆ ѕмі́ѧ. Ꙗ҆́кѡ на мѧ̀ ᲂу҆пова̀, и҆ и҆зба́влю и҆̀, покры́ю и҆̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ позна̀ и҆́мѧ моѐ. Воззове́тъ ко мнѣ̀, и҆ ᲂу҆слы́шꙋ є҆го̀: съ ни́мъ є҆́смь въ ско́рби, и҆змꙋ̀ є҆го̀, и҆ просла́влю є҆го̀: Долгото́ю дне́й и҆спо́лню є҆го̀, и҆ ꙗ҆влю̀ є҆мꙋ̀ спасе́нїе моѐ.
items.english_text: ...concerning thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. On their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone. Upon the asp and the basilisk shalt thou tread, and the lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under foot. Because he hath hoped in Me, I will deliver him; I will protect him, because he hath known My name. He shall cry unto Me, and I will hear him; I am with him in tribulation; I will deliver him, and glorify him. With length of days will I satisfy him, and show him My salvation.

items.slavonic_text: Спасе́нїе содѣ́лалъ є҆сѝ посредѣ̀ землѝ Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е, на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ пречтⷭ҇тиїи рꙋ́цѣ твоѝ просте́рлъ є҆сѝ, собира́ѧ всѧ̑ ꙗ҆зы́ки, зовꙋ́щыѧ: Гдⷭ҇и, сла́ва тебѣ̀.
items.english_text: Thou hast wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God; upon the Cross Thou didst stretch out Thy most pure hands, gathering together all the nations who cry: "O Lord, glory to Thee!"

items.english_text: Because we have no boldness on account of our manifold sins, do thou, O Virgin Theotokos, implore Him Who was born of thee, for the supplication of a Mother avails much unto the good pleasure of the Master; despise not the prayers of sinners, O all-pure one, for He is merciful, and able to save, Who also willed to suffer for us.

items.slavonic_text: Сїѧ̑ глаго́летъ Гдⷭ҇ь І҆ꙋде́ѡмъ: лю́дїе моѝ, что̀ сотвори́хъ ва́мъ; и҆лѝ чи́мъ ва́мъ стꙋжи́хъ; слѣпцы̀ ва́ши просвѣти́хъ, прокажє́нныѧ ѡ҆чи́стихъ, мꙋ́жа сꙋ́ща на ѻ҆дрѣ̀ и҆спра́вихъ: лю́дїе моѝ, что̀ сотвори́хъ ва́мъ; и҆лѝ что̀ мнѣ̀ возда́сте; за ма́ннꙋ же́лчь, за во́дꙋ ѻ҆́цетъ: за є҆́же люби́ти мѧ̀, ко крⷭ҇тꙋ́ мѧ пригвозди́сте: ктомꙋ̀ не терплю̀ про́чее, призовꙋ̀ моѧ̑ ꙗ҆зы́ки, и҆ ті́и мѧ̀ просла́вѧтъ со Ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ и҆ Дх҃омъ, и҆ а҆́зъ и҆̀мъ да́рꙋю живо́тъ вѣ́чный.
items.english_text: Thus saith the Lord unto the Jews: "O My people, what have I done unto you, or wherein have I grieved you? I gave light to your blind, I cleansed your lepers, I set upright the man that lay upon a bed. O My people, what have I done unto you, or what have ye repaid Me? In return for the manna, gall; in return for the water, vinegar; instead of loving Me, ye nailed Me to the Cross. No longer do I endure; henceforth will I call My nations, and they shall glorify Me with the Father and the Spirit, and I will grant them eternal life."

items.english_text: Ye lawgivers of Israel, Jews and Pharisees, the apostolic choir cries aloud unto you: "Behold the Temple which ye destroyed; behold the Lamb Whom ye crucified and delivered unto the tomb, but by His own power He arose! Deceive not yourselves, O Jews; for He it is that saved in the sea, and fed in the wilderness; He is the Life, and the Light, and the Peace of the world!"

items.slavonic_text: Та́кѡ глаго́летъ Гдⷭ҇ь: сѐ ᲂу҆разꙋмѣ́етъ Ѽтрокъ мо́й, и҆ вознесе́тсѧ, и҆ просла́витсѧ ѕѣлѡ̀. Ꙗ҆́коже ᲂу҆жа́снꙋтсѧ ѡ҆ тебѣ̀ мно́зи, та́кѡ ѡ҆безсла́витсѧ ѿ человѣ̑къ ви́дъ тво́й, и҆ сла́ва твоѧ̀ ѿ сынѡ́въ человѣ́ческихъ. Та́кѡ ᲂу҆дивѧ́тсѧ ꙗ҆зы́цы мно́зи ѡ҆ не́мъ, и҆ заградѧ́тъ ца́рїе ᲂу҆ста̀ своѧ̑: ꙗ҆́кѡ, и҆̀мже не возвѣсти́сѧ ѡ҆ не́мъ, ᲂу҆́зрѧтъ, и҆ и҆̀же не слы́шаша, ᲂу҆разꙋмѣ́ютъ. Гдⷭ҇и, кто̀ вѣ́рова слꙋ́хꙋ на́шемꙋ; и҆ мы́шца Гдⷭ҇нѧ комꙋ̀ ѿкры́сѧ; Возвѣсти́хомъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ Ѽтроча̀ пред̾ ни́мъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ ко́рень въ землѝ жа́ждꙋщей, нѣ́сть ви́да є҆мꙋ̀, нижѐ сла́вы: и҆ ви́дѣхомъ є҆го̀, и҆ не и҆ма́ше ви́да, ни добро́ты: Но ви́дъ є҆гѡ̀ безче́стенъ, ᲂу҆ма́ленъ па́че всѣ́хъ сынѡ́въ человѣ́ческихъ: человѣ́къ въ ꙗ҆́звѣ сы́й, и҆ вѣ́дый терпѣ́ти болѣ́знь, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѿврати́сѧ лицѐ є҆гѡ̀, безче́стно бы́сть, и҆ не вмѣни́сѧ. Се́й грѣхѝ на́шѧ но́ситъ, и҆ ѡ҆ на́съ болѣ́знꙋетъ, и҆ мы̀ вмѣни́хомъ є҆го̀ бы́ти въ трꙋдѣ̀, и҆ въ ꙗ҆́звѣ ѿ Бг҃а, и҆ во ѡ҆ѕлобле́нїи. То́й же ꙗ҆́звенъ бы́сть за грѣхѝ на́шѧ, и҆ мꙋ́ченъ бы́сть за беззакѡ́нїѧ на̑ша, наказа́нїе ми́ра на́шегѡ на не́мъ, ꙗ҆́звою є҆гѡ̀ мы̀ и҆сцѣлѣ́хомъ. Всѝ ꙗ҆́кѡ ѻ҆́вцы заблꙋди́хомъ: человѣ́къ ѿ пꙋтѝ своегѡ̀ заблꙋдѝ, и҆ Гдⷭ҇ь предадѐ є҆го̀ грѣ̑хъ ра́ди на́шихъ. И҆ то́й, занѐ ѡ҆ѕло́бленъ бы́сть, не ѿверза́етъ ᲂу҆́стъ свои́хъ: ꙗ҆́кѡ ѻ҆вча̀ на заколе́нїе веде́сѧ, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ А҆́гнецъ пред̾ стригꙋ́щимъ є҆го̀ безгла́сенъ, та́кѡ не ѿверза́етъ ᲂу҆́стъ свои́хъ. Во смире́нїи є҆гѡ̀ сꙋ́дъ є҆гѡ̀ взѧ́тсѧ: ро́дъ же є҆гѡ̀ кто̀ и҆сповѣ́сть; ꙗ҆́кѡ взе́млетсѧ ѿ землѝ живо́тъ є҆гѡ̀, ра́ди беззако́нїй люде́й мои́хъ веде́сѧ на сме́рть. И҆ да́мъ лꙋка̑выѧ вмѣ́стѡ погребе́нїѧ є҆гѡ̀, и҆ бога́тыѧ вмѣ́стѡ сме́рти є҆гѡ̀: ꙗ҆́кѡ беззако́нїа не сотворѝ, нижѐ ѡ҆брѣ́тесѧ ле́сть во ᲂу҆стнѣ́хъ є҆гѡ̀. И҆ Гдⷭ҇ь хо́щетъ ѡ҆чи́стити є҆го̀ ѿ ꙗ҆́звы: а҆́ще да́стсѧ ѡ҆ грѣсѣ̀, дꙋша̀ ва́ша ᲂу҆́зритъ сѣ́мѧ долгоживо́тное. И҆ хо́щетъ Гдⷭ҇ь рꙋко́ю свое́ю ѿѧ́ти болѣ́знь ѿ дꙋшѝ є҆гѡ̀, ꙗ҆ви́ти є҆мꙋ̀ свѣ́тъ, и҆ созда́ти ра́зꙋмомъ, ѡ҆правда́ти пра́веднаго бла́гѡ слꙋжа́ща мнѡ́гимъ: и҆ грѣхѝ и҆́хъ то́й понесе́тъ. Сегѡ̀ ра́ди то́й наслѣ́дитъ мнѡ́гихъ, и҆ крѣ́пкихъ раздѣли́тъ ко́рысти: занѐ предана̀ бы́сть на сме́рть дꙋша̀ є҆гѡ̀, и҆ со беззако́нными вмѣни́сѧ, и҆ то́й грѣхѝ мнѡ́гихъ вознесѐ, и҆ за беззакѡ́нїѧ и҆́хъ пре́данъ бы́сть. Возвесели́сѧ непло́ды неражда́ющаѧ, возгласѝ и҆ возопі́й нечревоболи́вшаѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ мно́га ча̑да пꙋсты́ѧ па́че, не́жели и҆мꙋ́щїѧ мꙋ́жа.
items.english_text: Thus saith the Lord: "Behold, My Servant shall understand, and He shall be exalted and glorified exceedingly. As many shall be astonished at Thee, so shall Thy countenance be without glory among men, and Thy glory among the sons of men. So shall many nations marvel at Him, and kings shall shut their mouths; for they to whom it was not told concerning Him shall see, and they that have not heard shall understand. Lord, who hath believed our report? And to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed? We have proclaimed Him as a Child before Him, as a root in a thirsty land; He hath no form nor glory: and we beheld Him, and He had no form nor beauty: but His form was ignominious, despised more than all the sons of men; a Man in suffering, and knowing how to bear sickness, for His face was turned away, He was despised, and was not esteemed. He bears our sins, and suffers for us, yet we esteemed Him to be in toil, and in smiting from God, and in affliction. But He was wounded for our sins, and tormented for our iniquities; the chastisement of our peace was upon Him, and by His stripe we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; each man hath wandered from his way, and the Lord hath delivered Him for our sins. And He, because of His affliction, opens not His mouth; as a sheep He was led to the slaughter, and as a Lamb before His shearer is dumb, so opens He not His mouth. In His humiliation His judgment was taken away; and who shall declare His generation? For His life is taken from the earth, because of the iniquities of My people was He led unto death. And I will give the wicked in return for His burial, and the rich in return for His death; for He did no iniquity, neither was deceit found in His mouth. And the Lord wills to cleanse Him from the stripe: if He give His soul for sin, your soul shall see a long-lived seed. And the Lord wills by His hand to take away sickness from His soul, to show Him light, and to form Him with understanding, to justify the Righteous One Who servs many well; and He shall bear their sins. Therefore shall He inherit many, and shall divide the spoils of the strong; because His soul was delivered unto death, and He was numbered among the lawless, and He bare the sins of many, and was delivered for their iniquities. Rejoice, thou barren woman that barest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not; for many more are the children of the desolate than of her that hath a husband."

items.slavonic_text: Бра́тїе, ст҃ѧ́й и҆ ѡ҆свѧща́емїи ѿ Є҆ди́нагѡ всѝ: Е҆ѧ́же ра́ди вины̀ не стыди́тсѧ бра́тїю нарица́ти и҆̀хъ, гл҃ѧ: Возвѣщꙋ̀ и҆́мѧ твоѐ бра́тїи мое́й, посредѣ̀ цр҃кве воспою́ тѧ. И҆ па́ки: А҆́зъ бꙋ́дꙋ надѣ́ѧсѧ на́нь, и҆ па́ки: Сѐ а҆́зъ и҆ дѣ́ти, ꙗ҆̀же мѝ да́лъ є҆́сть Бг҃ъ. Поне́же ᲂу҆́бѡ дѣ́ти приѡбщи́шасѧ пло́ти и҆ кро́ви, и҆ то́й прїи́скреннѣ приѡбщи́сѧ тѣ́хже, да сме́ртїю ᲂу҆праздни́тъ и҆мꙋ́щаго держа́вꙋ сме́рти, си́рѣчь дїа́вола: И҆ и҆зба́витъ си́хъ, є҆ли́цы стра́хомъ сме́рти чрез̾ всѐ житїѐ пови́нни бѣ́ша рабо́тѣ. Не ѿ а҆́гг҃лъ ᲂу҆́бѡ когда̀ прїе́млетъ, но ѿ сѣ́мене А҆враа́мова прїе́млетъ. Ѿню́джє до́лженъ бѣ̀ по всемꙋ̀ подо́битисѧ бра́тїи, да ми́лостивъ бꙋ́детъ и҆ вѣ́ренъ первосщ҃е́нникъ въ тѣ́хъ, ꙗ҆̀же къ Бг҃ꙋ, ко є҆́же ѡ҆чи́стити грѣхѝ людскі̑ѧ. Въ не́мже бо пострада̀, са́мъ и҆скꙋше́нъ бы́въ, мо́жетъ и҆ и҆скꙋша́ємымъ помощѝ.
items.english_text: Brethren, both He that sanctifies and they who are sanctified are all of One; for which cause He is not ashamed to call them brethren, saying: "I will declare Thy name unto My brethren, in the midst of the Church will I hymn Thee." And again: "I will put My trust in Him." And again: "Behold I and the children whom God hath given Me." Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, He also Himself likewise took part of the same; that through death He might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil; and deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage. For truly He takes not hold of angels, but He takes hold of the seed of Abraham. Therefore in all things it behooved Him to be made like unto His brethren, that He might be a merciful and faithful High Priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people. For in that He Himself hath suffered, being tempted, He is able to succor them that are tempted.

items.slavonic_text: Во вре́мѧ ѻ҆́но, ведо́хꙋ съ І҆и҃сомъ и҆ и҆́на два̀ ѕлодѣ̑ѧ, съ ни́мъ ᲂу҆би́ти. И҆ є҆гда̀ прїидо́ша на мѣ́сто нарица́емое ло́бное, тꙋ̀ распѧ́ша є҆го̀, и҆ ѕлодѣ̑ѧ, ѻ҆ва́го ᲂу҆́бѡ ѡ҆деснꙋ́ю, а҆ дрꙋга́го ѡ҆шꙋ́юю. І҆и҃съ же глаго́лаше: Ѻ҆́ч҃е, ѡ҆стꙋстѝ и҆̀мъ: не вѣ́дѧтъ бо, что̀ творя́тъ. Раздѣлѧ́юще же ри̑зы є҆гѡ̀, мета́хꙋ жре́бїѧ. И҆ стоѧ́хꙋ лю́дїе зрѧ́ще, рꙋга́хꙋсѧ же и҆ кнѧ̑зи съ ни́ми, глаго́люще: и҆́ныѧ спасѐ, да спасе́тъ и҆ себѐ, а҆́ще то́й є҆́сть Хрⷭ҇то́съ Бж҃їй и҆збра́нный. Рꙋга́хꙋсѧ же є҆мꙋ̀ и҆ во́ини, пристꙋпа́юще и҆ ѻ҆́цетъ принося́ще є҆мꙋ̀, и҆ глаго́лахꙋ: а҆́ще ты̀ є҆сѝ Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́йскъ, спаси́сѧ са́мъ. Бѣ́ же и҆ написа́нїе напи́сано над̾ ни́мъ писмены̀ Е҆́ллинскими и҆ ри́мскими и҆ є҆вре́йскими: Се́й є҆́сть Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́йскъ. Є҆ди́нъ же ѿ ѡ҆бѣ́шеною ѕлодѣ́ю хꙋ́лѧше є҆го̀, глаго́ла: а҆́ще ты̀ є҆сѝ Хрⷭ҇то́съ, спасѝ себѐ и҆ на́ю. Ѿвѣща́въ же дрꙋгі́й преща́ше є҆мꙋ̀, глаго́лѧ: ни лѝ ты̀ бои́шисѧ Бг҃а, ꙗ҆́кѡ въ то́мже ѡ҆сꙋжде́нъ є҆сѝ; И҆ мы̀ ᲂу҆́бѡ въ пра́вдꙋ: досто́йнаѧ бо по дѣлѡ́мъ на́ю воспрїе́млева: се́й же ни є҆ди́нагѡ ѕла̀ сотворѝ. И҆ глаго́лаше І҆и҃сови: помѧни́ мѧ Гдⷭ҇и, є҆гда̀ прїи́деши во Ца́рствїи сѝ. И҆ речѐ є҆мꙋ̀ І҆и҃съ: а҆ми́нь глаго́лю тебѣ̀, дне́сь со мно́ю бꙋ́деши въ раѝ. Бѣ́ же ча́съ ꙗ҆́кѡ шесты́й, и҆ тма̀ бы́сть по все́й землѝ до часа̀ девѧ́тагѡ. И҆ помє́рче со́лнце, и҆ завѣ́са церко́внаѧ раздра́сѧ посредѣ̀. И҆ возгла́шь гла́сомъ ве́лїимъ І҆и҃съ, речѐ: Ѻ҆́ч҃е, въ рꙋ́цѣ твоѝ предаю̀ Дꙋ́хъ мо́й! и҆ сїѧ̑ ре́къ и҆́здше. Ви́дѣвъ же со́тникъ бы́вшее, просла́ви Бг҃а, глаго́ла: вои́стиннꙋ, человѣ́къ се́й пра́веденъ бѣ̀. И҆ всѝ прише́дшїи наро́ди на позо́ръ се́й, ви́дѧще быва́ющаѧ, бїю́ще пе́рси своѧ̑ возвраща́хꙋсѧ. Стоѧ́хꙋ же всѝ зна́емїи є҆гѡ̀ и҆здале́ча, и҆ жєны̀ спослѣ́дствовавшыѧ є҆мꙋ̀ ѿ Галиле́и, зрѧ́щѧ сїѧ̑.
items.english_text: At that time, there were also two other malefactors led with Jesus to be put to death. And when they were come to the place which is called Calvary, there they crucified Him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left. Then said Jesus: "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do." And parting His garments, they cast lots. And the people stood beholding; and the rulers also with them derided Him, saying: "He saved others; let Him save Himself, if He be Christ, the chosen of God." And the soldiers also mocked Him, coming to Him, and offering Him vinegar, and saying: "If Thou be the King of the Jews, save Thyself." And a superscription also was written over Him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS. And one of the malefactors who were hanged reviled Him, saying: "If Thou be the Christ, save Thyself and us." But the other answering rebuked him, saying: "Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation? And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this Man hath done nothing amiss." And he said unto Jesus: "Lord, remember me when Thou comest into Thy kingdom." And Jesus said unto him: "Amen I say unto thee, today shalt thou be with Me in Paradise." And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour. And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst. And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, He said: "Father, into Thy hands I commend My Spirit!" and having said thus, He gave up the ghost. Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying: "Truly this was a righteous Man." And all the people that came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts, and returned. And all His acquaintance, and the women that followed Him from Galilee, stood afar off, beholding these things.

items.slavonic_text: Бж҃е и҆ Гдⷭ҇и си́лъ, и҆ всеѧ̀ тва́ри Содѣ́телю, и҆́же за милосе́рдїе безприкла́дныѧ ми́лости твоеѧ̀, є҆диноро́днаго Сн҃а твоего̀, Гдⷭ҇а на́шего І҆и҃са Хрⷭ҇та̀ низпосла́вый на спасе́нїе ро́да на́шегѡ: и҆ честны́мъ є҆гѡ̀ крⷭ҇то́мъ, рꙋкописа́нїе грѣ̑хъ на́шихъ растерза́вый, и҆ побѣди́вый тѣ́мъ нача̑ла и҆ вла̑сти тмы̀: Са́мъ Влⷣко чл҃вѣколю́бче, прїимѝ и҆ на́съ грѣ́шныхъ бл҃годарє́ственныѧ сїѧ̑ и҆ моле́бныѧ мл҃твы, и҆ и҆зба́ви на́съ ѿ всѧ́кагѡ всепа́гꙋбнагѡ и҆ мра́чнагѡ прегрѣше́нїѧ, и҆ всѣ́хъ ѡ҆ѕло́бити на́съ и҆́щꙋщихъ, ви́димыхъ и҆ неви́димыхъ вра̑гъ, пригвоздѝ стра́хꙋ твоемꙋ̀ плѡ́ти на́шѧ, и҆ не ᲂу҆клонѝ серде́цъ на́шихъ въ словеса̀, и҆лѝ помышлє́нїѧ лꙋка́вствїѧ: но любо́вїю твое́ю ᲂу҆ѧзвѝ дꙋ́шы на́шѧ: да къ тебѣ̀ всегда̀ взира́юще, и҆ є҆́же ѿ тебѐ свѣ́томъ наставля́еми, тебѐ непристꙋ́пнаго и҆ присносꙋ́щнаго зрѧ́ще свѣ́та, непреста́нное тебѣ̀ и҆сповѣ́данїе, и҆ бл҃годарє́нїе возсыла́емъ безнача́льномꙋ Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ̀, со є҆диноро́днымъ твои́мъ Сн҃омъ, и҆ всест҃ы́мъ, и҆ бл҃ги́мъ и҆ животворѧ́щимъ твои́мъ Дх҃омъ, ны́нѣ и҆ при́снѡ, и҆ во вѣ́ки вѣкѡ́въ, а҆ми́нь.
items.english_text: O God and Lord of hosts, and Maker of all creation, Who through the tender compassion of Thine incomparable mercy didst send down Thine Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, for the salvation of our race, and through His precious Cross didst tear up the handwriting of our sins, and thereby didst triumph over the principalities and powers of darkness: Do Thou Thyself, O Master and Lover of mankind, accept also these our thanksgiving and suppliant prayers, and deliver us from every all-destructive and dark transgression, and from all them that seek to harm us, both visible and invisible enemies. Nail down our flesh to Thy fear, and incline not our hearts unto words or thoughts of wickedness, but wound our souls with Thy love; that ever looking unto Thee, and guided by the light that comes from Thee, beholding Thee the unapproachable and everlasting Light, we may send up unceasing confession and thanksgiving unto Thee, the unoriginate Father, with Thine Only-begotten Son, and Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.

items.slavonic_text: Спаси́ мѧ Бж҃е, ꙗ҆́кѡ внидо́ша во́ды до дꙋшѝ моеѧ̀. Оу҆глѧбо́хъ въ ти́нѣнїи глꙋбины̀ и҆ нѣ́сть постоѧ́нїа. Прїидо́хъ во глꙋбины̀ морскїѧ, и҆ бꙋ́рѧ потопи́ мѧ. Оу҆трꙋди́хсѧ зовы́й, и҆змолчѐ горта́нь мо́й, и҆счезо́стѣ ѻ҆́чи моѝ, ѿ є҆́же ᲂу҆пова́ти мѝ на Бг҃а моего̀. Оу҆мно́жишасѧ па́че вла́съ главы̀ моеѧ̀ ненави́дѧщїи мѧ̀ тꙋ́не: ᲂу҆крѣпи́шасѧ вразѝ моѝ и҆згонѧ́щїи мѧ̀ непра́веднѡ, ꙗ҆̀же не восхища́хъ, тогда̀ воздаѧ́хъ. Бж҃е, ты̀ ᲂу҆вѣ́дѣлъ є҆сѝ безꙋ́мїе моѐ, и҆ прегрѣше́нїѧ моѧ̑ ѿ тебѐ не ᲂу҆таи́шасѧ. Да не постыдѧ́тсѧ ѡ҆ мнѣ̀ терпѧ́щїи тебѐ Гдⷭ҇и, Гдⷭ҇и си́лъ: нижѐ да посра́мѧтсѧ ѡ҆ мнѣ̀ и҆́щꙋщїи тебѐ Бж҃е І҆и҃левъ. Ꙗ҆́кѡ тебѐ ра́ди претерпѣ́хъ поноше́нїе, покры̀ срамота̀ лицѐ моѐ. Чꙋ́ждь бы́хъ бра́тїи мое́й, и҆ стра́ненъ сыновѡ́мъ ма́тере моеѧ̀. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ре́вность до́мꙋ твоегѡ̀ снѣде́ мѧ, и҆ поношє́нїѧ поноша́ющихъ тѝ нападо́ша на мѧ̀. И҆ покры́хъ посто́мъ дꙋ́шꙋ мою̀, и҆ бы́сть въ поноше́нїе мнѣ̀. И҆ положи́хъ ѡ҆дѣѧ́нїе моѐ вре́тище, и҆ бы́хъ и҆̀мъ въ при́тчꙋ. Ѡ҆ мнѣ̀ размышлѧ́хꙋ сѣдѧ́щїи во вратѣ́хъ, и҆ ѡ҆ мнѣ̀ поѧ́хꙋ пїю́щїи вїно̀. А҆́зъ же мл҃твою мое́ю къ тебѣ̀ Бж҃е, вре́мѧ бл҃говоле́нїѧ. Бж҃е, во мно́жествѣ ми́лости твоеѧ̀ ᲂу҆слы́ши мѧ̀, во и҆́стинѣ спасе́нїѧ твоегѡ̀. Спаси́ мѧ ѿ брѣ́нїѧ, да не ᲂу҆глѧ́бнꙋ, да и҆зба́влюсѧ ѿ ненави́дѧщихъ мѧ̀, и҆ ѿ глꙋбо́кихъ во́дъ. Да не потопи́тъ менѐ бꙋ́рѧ во́днаѧ, нижѐ да пожре́тъ менѐ глꙋбина̀, нижѐ сведетъ ѡ҆ мнѣ̀ рове́нникъ ᲂу҆́стъ свои́хъ. Оу҆слы́ши мѧ̀ Гдⷭ҇и, ꙗ҆́кѡ бл҃га мт҃ь твоѧ̀, по мно́жествꙋ щедро́тъ твои́хъ при́зри на мѧ̀. Не ѿвратѝ лица̀ твоегѡ̀ ѿ Ѽтрока твоегѡ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ скорблю̀, ско́рѡ ᲂу҆слы́ши мѧ̀. Вонмѝ дꙋшѝ мое́й, и҆ и҆зба́ви ю҆̀: вра̑гъ мои́хъ ра́ди и҆зба́ви мѧ̀. Ты́ бо вѣ́си поноше́нїе моѐ, и҆ стꙋ́дъ мо́й, и҆ срамотꙋ̀ мою̀, пред̾ тобо́ю всѝ ѡ҆скорблѧ́ющїи мѧ̀. Поноше́нїе ча́ѧше дꙋша̀ моѧ̀ и҆ стра́сть, и҆ жда́хъ соскорбѧ́щагѡ, и҆ не бѣ̀, и҆ ᲂу҆тѣша́ющихъ, и҆ не ѡ҆брѣто́хъ. И҆ да́ша въ снѣ́дь мою̀ же́лчь, и҆ въ жа́ждꙋ мою̀ напои́ша мѧ̀ ѻ҆́цта. Да бꙋ́детъ трапе́за и҆́хъ пред̾ ни́ми въ сѣ́ть, и҆ въ воздаѧ́нїе и҆ въ собла́знъ. Да помрача́тсѧ ѻ҆́чи и҆́хъ, є҆́же не ви́дѣти, и҆ хребе́тъ и҆́хъ вы́нꙋ слѧцы̀. Проле́й на нѧ̀ гнѣ́въ тво́й, и҆ ꙗ҆́рость гнѣ́ва твоегѡ̀ да пости́гнетъ и҆́хъ. Да бꙋ́детъ дво́ръ и҆́хъ пꙋ́стъ, и҆ въ жили́щахъ и҆́хъ да не бꙋ́детъ живы́й. Занѐ є҆го́же ты̀ порази́лъ є҆сѝ, ті́и погна́ша, и҆ къ болѣ́зни ꙗ҆́звъ мои́хъ приложи́ша. Приложѝ беззако́нїе къ беззако́нїю и҆́хъ, и҆ да не вни́дꙋтъ въ пра́вдꙋ твою̀. Да потребя́тсѧ ѿ кни́ги живы́хъ, и҆ съ пра́ведными да не напи́шꙋтсѧ. Ни́щъ и҆ болѧ́й є҆́смь а҆́зъ, спасе́нїе твоѐ Бж҃е да прїи́метъ мѧ̀. Восхвалю̀ и҆́мѧ Бг҃а моегѡ̀ съ пѣ́нїю, возвели́чꙋ є҆го̀ во хвале́нїи. И҆ ᲂу҆го́дно бꙋ́детъ Бг҃ꙋ па́че тельца̀ ю҆́на, ро́ги и҆зносѧ́ща и҆ па́знѡкти. Да ᲂу҆́зрѧтъ ни́щїи, и҆ возвеселѧ́тсѧ, взыщи́те Бг҃а, и҆ жива̀ бꙋ́детъ дꙋша̀ ва́ша. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ᲂу҆слы́ша ᲂу҆бо́гїѧ Гдⷭ҇ь, и҆ ѡ҆ко́ванныѧ своѧ̑ не ᲂу҆ничижѝ. Да восхва́лѧтъ є҆го̀ нб҃са̀ и҆ землѧ̀, мо́ре, и҆ всѧ̑ живꙋ́щаѧ въ не́мъ. Ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ спасе́тъ Сїѡ́на, и҆ сози́жд-
items.english_text: Save me, O God, for the waters are come in unto my soul. I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing; I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me. I am weary of my crying, my throat is dried; mine eyes fail while I wait for my God. They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head; they that would destroy me, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty; then I restored that which I took not away. O God, Thou knowest my foolishness, and my faults are not hid from Thee. Let not them that wait on Thee, O Lord God of hosts, be ashamed for my sake; let not those that seek Thee be confounded for my sake, O God of Israel. Because for Thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face. I am become a stranger unto my brethren, and an alien unto my mother's children. For the zeal of Thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached Thee are fallen upon me. And I covered my soul with fasting, and that was turned to my reproach. I made sackcloth also my garment, and I became a proverb to them. They that sit in the gate spoke against me, and I was the song of the drunkards. But as for me, my prayer is unto Thee, O Lord, in an acceptable time; O God, in the multitude of Thy mercy hear me, in the truth of Thy salvation. Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink; let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters. Let not the waterflood overflow me, neither let the deep swallow me up, and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me. Hear me, O Lord, for Thy loving-kindness is good; turn unto me according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies. And hide not Thy face from Thy servant, for I am in trouble; hear me speedily. Draw nigh unto my soul, and redeem it; deliver me because of mine enemies. For Thou hast known my reproach, and my shame, and my dishonor; mine adversaries are all before Thee. Reproach hath broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness; and I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none. They gave me also gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. Let their table become a snare before them, and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap. Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not, and make their loins continually to shake. Pour out Thine indignation upon them, and let Thy wrathful anger take hold of them. Let their habitation be desolate, and let none dwell in their tents. For they persecute Him Whom Thou hast smitten, and they talk to the grief of those whom Thou hast wounded. Add iniquity unto their iniquity, and let them not come into Thy righteousness. Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous. But as for me, I am poor and sorrowful; let Thy salvation, O God, set me up on high. I will praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify Him with thanksgiving. This also shall please the Lord better than an ox or bullock that hath horns and hoofs. The humble shall see this, and be glad; and your heart shall live that seek God. For the Lord hears the poor, and despiss not His prisoners. Let the heaven and earth praise Him, the seas, and everything that moves therein. For God will save Zion, and will build...

items.slavonic_text: Бж҃е, въ по́мощь мою̀ вонмѝ: Гдⷭ҇и, помощи́ ми потщи́сѧ. Да постыдѧ́тсѧ и҆ посра́мѧтсѧ и҆́щꙋщїи дꙋ́шꙋ мою̀, да возвратя́тсѧ вспѧ́ть, и҆ постыдѧ́тсѧ, хотя́щїи мѝ ѕла̑ѧ. Да возвратя́тсѧ а҆́бїе стыдѧ́щесѧ, глаго́лющїи мѝ: бл҃гоже бл҃гоже. Да возра́дꙋютсѧ и҆ возвеселѧ́тсѧ ѡ҆ тебѣ̀ всѝ и҆́щꙋщїи тебѐ Бж҃е, и҆ да гл҃ютъ вы́нꙋ: да возвели́читсѧ Гдⷭ҇ь, любѧ́щїи спасе́нїе твоѐ. А҆́зъ же ни́щъ є҆́смь и҆ ᲂу҆бо́гъ. Бж҃е помози́ ми, помо́щникъ мо́й, и҆ и҆зба́витель мо́й є҆сѝ ты̀, Гдⷭ҇и не закоснѝ.
items.english_text: O God, make speed to save me; O Lord, make haste to help me. Let them be ashamed and confounded that seek after my soul; let them be turned backward and put to confusion that desire my hurt. Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame that say: "Aha, aha!" Let all those that seek Thee rejoice and be glad in Thee; and let such as love Thy salvation say continually: "Let the Lord be magnified!" But I am poor and needy; make haste unto me, O God: Thou art my help and my deliverer; O Lord, make no tarrying.

items.slavonic_text: Приклонѝ Гдⷭ҇и ᲂу҆́хо твоѐ, и҆ ᲂу҆слы́ши мѧ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ ни́щъ и҆ ᲂу҆бо́гъ є҆́смь а҆́зъ. Сохранѝ дꙋ́шꙋ мою̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ преподо́бенъ є҆́смь: спасѝ раба̀ твоего̀ Бж҃е мо́й, ᲂу҆пова́ющаго на тѧ̀. Поми́лꙋй мѧ̀ Гдⷭ҇и, ꙗ҆́кѡ къ тебѣ̀ воззовꙋ̀ ве́сь де́нь. Возвеселѝ дꙋ́шꙋ раба̀ твоегѡ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ къ тебѣ̀ взѧ́хъ дꙋ́шꙋ мою̀. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ты̀ Гдⷭ҇и бл҃гъ и҆ кро́токъ, и҆ многомл҃тивъ всѣ̑мъ призыва́ющымъ тѧ̀. Внꙋшѝ Гдⷭ҇и мл҃твꙋ мою̀, и҆ вонмѝ гла́сꙋ моле́нїа моегѡ̀. Въ де́нь ско́рби моеѧ̀ воззва́хъ къ тебѣ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ ᲂу҆слы́шалъ мѧ̀ є҆сѝ. Нѣ́сть подо́бенъ тебѣ̀ въ бо́зѣхъ Гдⷭ҇и, и҆ нѣ́сть по дѣлѡ́мъ твои̑мъ. Всѝ ꙗ҆зы́цы, є҆ли́ки сотвори́лъ є҆сѝ, прїи́дꙋтъ, и҆ покло́нѧтсѧ пред̾ тобо́ю Гдⷭ҇и, и҆ просла́вѧтъ и҆́мѧ твоѐ: ꙗ҆́кѡ ве́лїй є҆сѝ ты̀, и҆ творѧ́й чꙋдеса̀, ты̀ є҆сѝ Бг҃ъ є҆ди́нъ. Наста́ви мѧ̀ Гдⷭ҇и на пꙋ́ть тво́й, и҆ пойдꙋ̀ во и҆́стинѣ твое́й: да возвесели́тсѧ се́рдце моѐ боѧ́тисѧ и҆́мене твоегѡ̀. И҆сповѣ́мсѧ тебѣ̀ Гдⷭ҇и Бж҃е мо́й всѣ́мъ се́рдцемъ мои́мъ, и҆ просла́влю и҆́мѧ твоѐ въ вѣ́къ. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ми́лость твоѧ̀ ве́лїѧ на мнѣ̀, и҆ и҆зба́вилъ є҆сѝ дꙋ́шꙋ мою̀ ѿ а҆́да преисподнѣ́йшагѡ. Бж҃е, законопрестꙋ́пницы воста́ша на мѧ̀, и҆ со́нмъ держа́вныхъ взыска́ша дꙋ́шꙋ мою̀, и҆ не предложи́ша тебѐ пред̾ собо́ю. И҆ ты̀ Гдⷭ҇и Бж҃е мо́й ще́дрый и҆ ми́лостивый, долготерпѣли́вый и҆ многомл҃тивый, и҆ и҆́стинный. При́зри на мѧ̀ и҆ поми́лꙋй мѧ̀, да́ждь держа́вꙋ твою̀ Ѽтрокꙋ твоемꙋ̀, и҆ спасѝ сы́на рабы̀ твоеѧ̀. Сотворѝ со мно́ю знаме́нїе ко бла́гꙋ, и҆ да ви́дѧтъ ненави́дѧщїи мѧ̀, и҆ постыдѧ́тсѧ: ꙗ҆́кѡ ты̀ Гдⷭ҇и помо́глъ мѝ, и҆ ᲂу҆тѣ́шилъ мѧ̀ є҆сѝ.
items.english_text: Bow down Thine ear, O Lord, hear me, for I am poor and needy. Preserve my soul, for I am holy; O Thou my God, save Thy servant that trusts in Thee. Be merciful unto me, O Lord, for I cry unto Thee all the day long. Rejoice the soul of Thy servant, for unto Thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul. For Thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive, and plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon Thee. Give ear, O Lord, unto my prayer, and attend to the voice of my supplications. In the day of my trouble I will call upon Thee, for Thou wilt answer me. Among the gods there is none like unto Thee, O Lord, neither are there any works like unto Thy works. All nations whom Thou hast made shall come and worship before Thee, O Lord, and shall glorify Thy name. For Thou art great, and doest marvelous things; Thou art God alone. Teach me Thy way, O Lord; I will walk in Thy truth; unite my heart to fear Thy name. I will praise Thee, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify Thy name for evermore. For great is Thy mercy toward me, and Thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell. O God, the proud are risen against me, and the assemblies of violent men have sought after my soul, and have not set Thee before them. But Thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, long-suffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth. O turn unto me, and have mercy upon me; give Thy strength unto Thy servant, and save the son of Thine handmaid. Show me a token for good, that they who hate me may see it, and be ashamed; because Thou, Lord, hast holpen me, and comforted me.

items.slavonic_text: Ви́дѧ разбо́йникъ Нача́льника жи́зни на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ ви́сѧща, глаго́лаше: а҆́ще не бы̀ Бг҃ъ бы́лъ вопло́щьсѧ, и҆́же съ на́ми распны́йсѧ, не бы̀ со́лнце лꙋчы̑ [своѧ̑] потаи́ло, нижѐ бы землѧ̀ трепе́щꙋщи трѧсла́сѧ: но всѧ̑ терпѧ́й, помѧни́ мѧ Гдⷭ҇и во Црⷭ҇твїи твое́мъ.
items.english_text: Seeing the Author of life hanging upon the Cross, the thief said: "If He that is crucified with us were not God incarnate, the sun would not have hidden its rays, nor would the earth have shaken with trembling; but O Thou Who endurest all things, remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom!"

items.slavonic_text: И҆́же на́съ ра́ди Рожде́йсѧ ѿ Дв҃ы, и҆ распѧ́тїе претерпѣ́въ Бл҃гі́й, и҆спрове́ргїй сме́ртїю сме́рть, и҆ Воскресе́нїе ꙗ҆вле́й, ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ, не пре́зри ꙗ҆̀же созда́лъ є҆сѝ рꙋко́ю твое́ю, ꙗ҆вѝ человѣколю́бїе твоѐ Ми́лостиве: прїимѝ ро́ждшꙋю тѧ̀ Бцⷣꙋ молѧ́щꙋюсѧ за ны̀, и҆ спасѝ Сп҃се на́шъ лю́ди ѿча́янныѧ.
items.english_text: O Good One, Who for our sake wast born of a Virgin, and didst endure crucifixion, trampling down death by death, and revealing the Resurrection as God: despise not those whom Thou hast fashioned with Thine own hand; show forth Thy loving-kindness, O Merciful One; accept the Theotokos who bare Thee, interceding for us, and save, O our Savior, a despairing people.

items.slavonic_text: Оу҆́жасъ бѣ̀ ви́дѣти, нб҃сѐ и҆ землѝ Творца̀ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ ви́сѧща, со́лнце поме́ркшее, де́нь же па́ки въ но́щь прело́жшїйсѧ, и҆ зе́млю и҆з̾ гро́бѡвъ возсыла́ющꙋ тѣлеса̀ ме́ртвыхъ: съ ни́миже покланѧ́емсѧ тебѣ̀, спасѝ на́съ. Два́жды.
items.english_text: A terror it was to behold the Creator of heaven and earth hanging upon the Cross, the sun darkened, the day turning back into night, and the earth sending forth from the tombs the bodies of the dead; with them we worship Thee: save us!

items.slavonic_text: Є҆гда̀ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ пригвозди́ша беззако́ннїи Гдⷭ҇а сла́вы, вопїѧ́ше къ ни̑мъ: чи́мъ ва́съ ѡ҆скорби́хъ; и҆лѝ ѡ҆ че́мъ прогнѣ́вахъ; пре́жде менѐ кто̀ ва́съ и҆зба́ви ѿ ско́рби; и҆ ны́нѣ что̀ мнѣ̀ воздаетѐ; ѕла̑ѧ за бл҃га̑ѧ: за сто́лпъ ѻ҆́гненный, на крⷭ҇тѣ́ мѧ пригвозди́сте: за ѡ҆́блакъ, гро́бъ мнѣ̀ и҆скопа́сте: за ма́ннꙋ, же́лчь мнѣ̀ принесо́сте: за во́дꙋ, ѻ҆́цтомъ мѧ̀ напои́сте: про́чее призовꙋ̀ ꙗ҆зы́ки, и҆ ті́и мѧ̀ просла́вѧтъ со Ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ и҆ со ст҃ы́мъ Дх҃омъ.
items.english_text: When the lawless nailed the Lord of glory to the Cross, He cried unto them: "Wherein have I grieved you, or wherein have I provoked you to anger? Before Me, who delivered you from affliction? And now, what do ye repay Me? Evil for good! In return for the pillar of fire, ye nailed Me to the Cross; in return for the cloud, ye dug a tomb for Me; in return for the manna, ye brought Me gall; in return for the water, ye gave Me vinegar to drink! Henceforth will I call the nations, and they shall glorify Me with the Father and with the Holy Spirit!"

items.slavonic_text: Дне́сь ви́ситъ на Дре́вѣ, и҆́же на вода́хъ зе́млю Повѣ́сивый: вѣнце́мъ ѿ те́рнїа ѡ҆блага́етсѧ, и҆́же а҆́гг҃лѡвъ Цр҃ь, въ ло́жнꙋю багрѧни́цꙋ ѡ҆блачи́тсѧ, Ѡ҆дѣва́ѧй нб҃о ѡ҆́блаки: заꙋше́нїе прїѧ́тъ, и҆́же во І҆орда́нѣ Свободи́вый А҆да́ма, гвоздьмѝ пригвозди́сѧ Жени́хъ церко́вный: копіе́мъ прободе́сѧ Сы́нъ Дв҃ыа. Покланѧ́емсѧ Стрⷭ҇те́мъ твои̑мъ Хрⷭ҇тѐ. Покланѧ́емсѧ Стрⷭ҇те́мъ твои̑мъ Хрⷭ҇тѐ. Покланѧ́емсѧ Стрⷭ҇те́мъ твои̑мъ Хрⷭ҇тѐ, покажѝ на́мъ и҆ сла́вное твоѐ Воскрⷭ҇нїе.
items.english_text: Today He Who hung the earth upon the waters is hung upon the Tree; He Who is King of the angels is girt with a crown of thorns; He Who covers the heaven with clouds is arrayed in mock purple; He Who set Adam free in the Jordan receives buffeting; the Bridegroom of the Church is transfixed with nails; the Son of the Virgin is pierced with a lance. We venerate Thy Sufferings, O Christ! We venerate Thy Sufferings, O Christ! We venerate Thy Sufferings, O Christ: show us also Thy glorious Resurrection!

items.slavonic_text: Бра́тїе, и҆мꙋ́ще дерзнове́нїе, входи́ти во Ст҃а̑ѧ Кро́вїю І҆и҃съ Хрⷭ҇то́вою, пꙋте́мъ но́вымъ и҆ живы́мъ. Е҆го́же ѡ҆бнови́лъ є҆́сть на́мъ завѣ́сою, си́рѣчь Пло́тїю свое́ю: И҆ І҆ере́а вели́ка над̾ до́момъ Бж҃їимъ: да пристꙋпа́емъ со и҆́стиннымъ се́рдцемъ ко и҆звѣще́нїи вѣ́ры, ѡ҆кропле́ни се́рдцы ѿ со́вѣсти лꙋка́выѧ, и҆ и҆змове́ни тѣлесы̀ водо́ю чи́стою: да держи́мъ и҆сповѣ́данїе ᲂу҆пова́нїѧ нескло́нное: вѣ́ренъ бо є҆́сть Ѿвѣща́вый: и҆ да разꙋмѣва́емъ дрꙋг̾дрꙋ́га къ поощре́нїю любвѐ, и҆ до́брыхъ дѣ́лъ, не ѡ҆ставлѧ́юще собра́нїа своегѡ̀, ꙗ҆́коже є҆́сть нѣ́кторымъ ѻ҆бы́чай, но дрꙋг̾дрꙋ́га ᲂу҆тѣша́юще: и҆ толи́кѡ па́че, є҆ли́кѡ ви́дите приближа́ющїйсѧ де́нь [сꙋ́дный]. Во́лею бо согрѣша́ющымъ на́мъ по прїѧ́тїи ра́зꙋма и҆́стины, ктомꙋ̀ ѡ҆ грѣсѣ́хъ не ѡ҆брѣта́етсѧ же́ртва: стра́шное же нѣ́кое ча́ѧнїе сꙋда̀, и҆ ѻ҆гнѧ̀ ре́вность, поя́сти хотя́щагѡ сопроти́вныхъ. items.english_text: Brethren, having boldness to enter into the Holiest by the Blood of Jesus Christ, by a new and living way, which He hath consecrated for us through the veil, that is to say, His flesh; and having a Great Priest over the house of God: let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water; let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering; for He is faithful that promised; and let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is, but exhorting one another; and so much the more, as ye see the [judgment] day approaching. For if we sin willfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more sacrifice for sins, but a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the Blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace? For we know Him that hath said: "Vengeance belongs unto Me, I will recompense, saith the Lord." And again: "The Lord shall judge His people." It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

items.slavonic_text: Е҆ѵагⷢ҇лїе ѿ І҆ѡа́нна, зача́ло ѯ҃а. ѿ. ѯ҃а:
items.english_text: At that time, they led Jesus from Caiaphas unto the hall of judgment; and it was early; and they themselves went not into the judgment hall, lest they should be defiled, but that they might eat the passover. Pilate then went out unto them, and said: "What accusation bring ye against this Man?" They answered and said unto him: "If He were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered Him up unto thee." Then said Pilate unto them: "Take ye Him, and judge Him according to your law." The Jews therefore said unto him: "It is not lawful for us to put any man to death." That the saying of Jesus might be fulfilled, which He spoke, signifying what death He should die. Then Pilate entered into the judgment hall again, and called Jesus, and said unto Him: "Art Thou the King of the Jews?" Jesus answered him: "Sayest thou this thing of thyself, or did others tell it thee of Me?" Pilate answered: "Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests have delivered Thee unto me: what hast Thou done?" Jesus answered: "My kingdom is not of this world: if My kingdom were of this world, then would My servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is My kingdom not from hence." Pilate therefore said unto Him: "Art Thou a King then?" Jesus answered: "Thou sayest that I am a King. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth hears My voice." Pilate saith unto Him: "What is truth?" And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them: "I find in Him no fault at all. But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?" Then cried they all again, saying: "Not this Man, but Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a robber. Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged Him. And the soldiers plaited a crown of thorns, and put it on His head, and they put on Him a purple robe, and said: "Hail, King of the Jews!" and they smote Him on the cheeks. Pilate therefore went forth again, and saith unto them: "Behold, I bring Him forth to you, that ye may know that I find no fault in Him." Then came Jesus forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them: "Behold the Man!" When the chief priests therefore and officers saw Him, they cried out, saying: "Crucify Him, crucify Him!" Pilate saith unto them: "Take ye Him, and crucify Him: for I find no fault in Him." The Jews answered him: "We have a law, and by our law He ought to die, because He made Himself the Son of God." When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he was the more afraid; and went again into the judgment hall, and saith unto Jesus: "Whence art Thou?" But Jesus gave him no answer. Then saith Pilate unto Him: "Speakest Thou not unto me? Knowest Thou not that I have power to crucify Thee, and have power to release Thee?" Jesus answered: "Thou couldest have no power at all against Me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered Me unto thee hath the greater sin." And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release Him; but the Jews cried out, saying: "If thou let this Man go, thou art not Caesar's friend: whosoever makes himself a king speaks against Caesar." When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha. And it was the Preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour; and he saith unto the Jews: "Behold your King!" But they cried out: "Away with Him, away with Him, crucify Him!" Pilate saith unto them: "Shall I crucify your King?" The chief priests answered: "We have no king but Caesar." Then delivered he Him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led Him away. And He bearing His Cross went forth into a place called the Place of a Skull, which is called in the Hebrew Golgotha; where they crucified Him, and two other with Him, on either side one...

items.slavonic_text: средѣ́ же І҆и҃са. Написа́ же и҆ ті́тла Пїла́тъ, и҆ положѝ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀. Бѣ́ же напи́сано: І҆и҃съ Назѡре́йнинъ Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́йскїй. Сего́ же ті́тла мно́зи что́ша ѿ І҆ꙋде́й: ꙗ҆́кѡ бли́зъ бѣ̀ мѣ́сто гра́да, и҆́дѣже пропѧ́ша І҆и҃са: и҆ бѣ̀ напи́сано Е҆вре́йски, Гре́чески, Ри́мски. Глаго́лахꙋ же Пїла́тꙋ а҆рхїере́е і҆ꙋде́йстїи: не пишѝ: Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́йскїй, но ꙗ҆́кѡ са́мъ речѐ: Цр҃ь є҆́смь І҆ꙋде́йскїй. Ѿвѣща̀ Пїла́тъ: є҆́же писа́хъ, писа́хъ. Во́ини же, є҆гда̀ пропѧ́ша І҆и҃са, прїѧ́ша ри̑зы є҆гѡ̀, и҆ сотвори́ша четы́ри ча́сти, коемꙋ́ждо во́инꙋ ча́сть, и҆ хїтѡ́нъ. Бѣ́ же хїтѡ́нъ не шве́нъ, свы́ше и҆стка́нъ ве́сь. Рѣ́ша же къ себѣ̀: не предере́мъ є҆гѡ̀, но ме́тнемъ жре́бїѧ ѡ҆ не́мъ, комꙋ̀ бꙋ́детъ: да сбꙋ́детсѧ писа́нїе, глаго́лющее: раздѣли́ша ри̑зы моѧ̑ себѣ̀, и҆ ѡ҆ і҆маті́смѣ мое́й мета́ша жре́бїѧ. Во́ини ᲂу҆́бѡ сїѧ̑ сотвори́ша. Стоѧ́хꙋ же при крⷭ҇тѣ̀ І҆и҃совѣ Ма́ти є҆гѡ̀, и҆ сестра̀ Мт҃ре є҆гѡ̀, Марі́а Клеѡ́пова, и҆ Марі́а Магдали́на. І҆и҃съ же ви́дѣвъ Ма́терь, и҆ ᲂу҆чени́ка стоѧ́ща, є҆го́же люблѧ́ше, глаго́ла Ма́тери свое́й: Же́но, сѐ сы́нъ тво́й. Пото́мъ глаго́ла ᲂу҆чени́кꙋ: сѐ Ма́ти твоѧ̀. И҆ ѿ тогѡ̀ часа̀ поя́тъ ю҆̀ ᲂу҆чени́къ къ своѧ̑ си. По се́мъ вѣ́дый І҆и҃съ, ꙗ҆́кѡ всѧ̑ ᲂу҆жѐ соверши́шасѧ, да сбꙋ́детсѧ писа́нїе, глаго́ла: жа́ждꙋ. Сосꙋ́дъ же стоѧ́ше по́лнъ ѻ҆́цта: ѻ҆ни́ же и҆спо́лнивше гꙋ́бꙋ ѻ҆́цта, и҆ на тро́сть вонзе́нше, придѣ́ша къ ᲂу҆стна́мъ є҆гѡ̀. Є҆гда́ же прїѧ́тъ ѻ҆́цетъ І҆и҃съ, речѐ: соверши́шасѧ. И҆ прекло́нь главꙋ̀, предадѐ Дꙋ́хъ. І҆ꙋде́е же, поне́же Пѧто́къ бѣ̀, да не ѡ҆ста́нꙋтъ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ тѣлеса̀ въ сꙋббѡ́тꙋ: бѣ́ бо вели́къ де́нь тоѧ̀ сꙋббѡ́ты, моли́ша Пїла́та, да пребїю́тъ го́лєни и҆́хъ, и҆ во́змꙋтъ. Прїидо́ша же во́ини, и҆ пе́рвомꙋ ᲂу҆́бѡ преби́ша го́лєни, и҆ дрꙋго́мꙋ распѧ́томꙋ съ ни́мъ. На І҆и҃са же прише́дше, ꙗ҆́кѡ ви́дѣша є҆го̀ ᲂу҆жѐ ᲂу҆ме́рша, не преби́ша є҆мꙋ̀ голе́нїй: но є҆ди́нъ ѿ во́инъ копіе́мъ ре́бра є҆мꙋ̀ прободѐ, и҆ а҆́бїе и҆зы́де кро́вь и҆ вода̀. И҆ ви́дѣвый свидѣ́тельствова, и҆ и҆́стинно є҆́сть свидѣ́тельство є҆гѡ̀: и҆ то́й вѣ́сть, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆́стинꙋ глаго́летъ, да вы̀ вѣ́рꙋ и҆́мете. Бы́ша бо сїѧ̑, да сбꙋ́детсѧ писа́нїе: ко́сть не сокрꙋши́тсѧ ѿ негѡ̀. И҆ па́ки дрꙋго́е писа́нїе глаго́летъ: воззрѧ́тъ на́нь, є҆го́же прободо́ша.
items.english_text: ...and Jesus in the midst. And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the Cross. And the writing was: JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS. This title then read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city: and it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin. Then said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate: "Write not: The King of the Jews; but that He said: I am King of the Jews." Pilate answered: "What I have written I have written." Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took His garments, and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also His coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout. They said therefore among themselves: "Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be": that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which saith: "They parted My raiment among them, and for My vesture they did cast lots." These things therefore the soldiers did. Now there stood by the Cross of Jesus His Mother, and His Mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene. When Jesus therefore saw His Mother, and the disciple standing by, whom He loved, He saith unto His Mother: "Woman, behold thy son!" Then saith He to the disciple: "Behold thy Mother!" And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home. After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, saith: "I thirst." Now there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and they filled a sponge with vinegar, and put it upon hyssop, and put it to His mouth. When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, He said: "It is finished": and He bowed His head, and gave up the ghost. The Jews therefore, because it was the Preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the Cross on the Sabbath day (for that Sabbath day was a high day), besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away. Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other who was crucified with Him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that He was dead already, they brake not His legs: but one of the soldiers with a spear pierced His side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knows that he saith true, that ye might believe. For these things were done, that the Scripture should be fulfilled: "A bone of Him shall not be broken." And again another Scripture saith: "They shall look on Him Whom they pierced."

items.slavonic_text: Не преда́ждь на́съ до конца̀, и҆́мене твоегѡ̀ ра́ди, и҆ не разорѝ завѣ́та твоегѡ̀, и҆ не ѡ҆ста́ви ми́лости твоеѧ̀ ѿ на́съ, А҆враа́ма ра́ди возлю́бленнагѡ ѿ тебѐ, и҆ за І҆саа́ка раба̀ твоего̀, и҆ І҆и҃лѧ ст҃а́го твоегѡ̀.
items.english_text: Deliver us not up utterly, for Thy name's sake, neither disannul Thou Thy covenant; and cause not Thy mercy to depart from us, for Abraham's sake Thy beloved, and for Isaac's sake Thy servant, and Israel's Thy holy one.

items.slavonic_text: И҆ моли́тва:
items.english_text: O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who hast long-suffered over our transgressions, and hast brought us even unto this present hour, wherein, hanging upon the life-creating Tree, Thou didst open the entrance into Paradise unto the prudent thief, and by death didst destroy death: Cleanse us sinners and Thine unworthy servants; for we have sinned and committed iniquity, and we are not worthy to lift up our eyes and to look upon the height...

items.slavonic_text: на высотꙋ̀ нб҃нꙋю, занѐ ѡ҆ста́вихомъ пꙋ́ть пра́вды твоеѧ̀, и҆ ходи́хомъ въ во́лѧхъ серде́цъ на́шихъ, но мо́лимъ твою̀ безмѣ́рнꙋю бла́гость, пощадѝ на́съ Гдⷭ҇и по мно́жествꙋ ми́лости твоеѧ̀: и҆ спасѝ на́съ и҆́мене твоегѡ̀ ра́ди ст҃а́гѡ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆счезо́ша въ сꙋетѣ̀ дні́е на́ши: и҆змѝ на́съ и҆з̾ рꙋкѝ сопроти́внагѡ, и҆ ѡ҆ста́ви на́мъ грѣхѝ на́ша, и҆ ᲂу҆мертвѝ плотско́е на́ше мꙋдрова́нїе, да ве́тхаго ѿложи́вше чл҃ка, въ но́ваго ѡ҆блече́мсѧ, и҆ тебѣ̀ поживе́мъ на́шемꙋ Влⷣцѣ и҆ Бл҃годѣ́телю: и҆ та́кѡ твои̑мъ послѣ́дꙋюще повелѣ́нїємъ, въ вѣ́чный поко́й дости́гнемъ, и҆́дѣже є҆́сть всѣ́хъ веселя́щихсѧ жили́ще. Ты́ бо є҆сѝ вои́стиннꙋ и҆́стинное весе́лїе, и҆ ра́дость любѧ́щихъ тѧ̀ Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е на́шъ, и҆ тебѣ̀ сла́вꙋ возсыла́емъ, со безнача́льнымъ твои́мъ Ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ, и҆ прест҃ы́мъ, и҆ бл҃ги́мъ, и҆ животворѧ́щимъ твои́мъ Дх҃омъ, ны́нѣ и҆ при́снѡ, и҆ во вѣ́ки вѣкѡ́въ, а҆ми́нь.
items.english_text: ...of heaven, because we have forsaken the path of Thy righteousness, and have walked in the wills of our own hearts. But we implore Thine immeasurable goodness: spare us, O Lord, according to the multitude of Thy mercy, and save us for Thy holy name's sake, for our days have vanished in vanity. Rescue us from the hand of the adversary, and forgive us our sins, and mortify our carnal mind; that, putting off the old man, we may put on the new, and live unto Thee, our Master and Benefactor; and thus, following Thy commandments, we may attain unto everlasting rest, where is the dwelling-place of all them that rejoice. For Thou art in truth the true joy and gladness of them that love Thee, O Christ our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.

items.slavonic_text: Подоба́етъ же и҆ сїѐ вѣ́дати, ꙗ҆́кѡ прїѧ́хомъ въ Палесті́нѣ, въ се́й ст҃ы́й де́нь вели́кагѡ Пѧтка̀, не твори́ти Преждеосвѧще́ннꙋю, нижѐ па́ки соверше́ннꙋю Лїтꙋргі́ю, но нижѐ трапе́зꙋ поставля́емъ, нижѐ ꙗ҆ди́мъ въ се́й де́нь Распѧ́тїа. А҆́ще же кто̀ бꙋ́детъ многонемо́щенъ, и҆лѝ престарѣ́лсѧ, и҆ не моги́й пребы́ти по́стенъ, дае́тсѧ є҆мꙋ̀ хлѣ́бъ и҆ вода̀, по захожде́нїи со́лнца. Си́це бо прїѧ́хомъ ѿ Ст҃ы́хъ за́повѣдей ст҃ы́хъ а҆пⷭ҇лъ, не ꙗ҆́сти въ вели́кїй Пѧто́къ, Гдⷭ҇не бо сло́во, є҆́же речѐ къ фарісе́ѡмъ Гдⷭ҇ь: ꙗ҆́кѡ є҆гда̀ ѿи́метсѧ ѿ ни́хъ Жени́хъ, тогда̀ постѧ́тсѧ въ ты̑ѧ днѝ: здѣ̀ бл҃же́ннѣйшїи а҆́пли воспрїѧ́ша, и҆ сїѐ ѡ҆брѧ́щеши во а҆пⷭ҇льскихъ преда́нїихъ, внима́тельнѡ сїѧ̑ проходѧ̀. Но и҆ пра́вильное посла́нїе ст҃ѣ́йшагѡ а҆рхїепⷭ҇кпа а҆леѯандрі́йскагѡ Дїонѵ́сїа, ꙗ҆́вѣ сїѐ предпоставлѧ́етъ.
items.english_text: *It is fitting to know also this: that we have received in Palestine, on this holy day of Great Friday, not to celebrate the Presanctified nor again the complete Liturgy; neither do we set a table, nor do we eat on this day of the Crucifixion.*[^262]

items.slavonic_text: И҆ пое́мъ стїхи̑ры самогла́сны.
items.english_text: All creation was altered by fear, beholding Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ: the sun was darkened, and the foundations of the earth were shaken; all things suffered with the Creator of all. O Thou Who didst endure willingly for our sake, Lord, glory to Thee! *(Twice.)*

items.slavonic_text: Всѧ̀ тва́рь и҆змѣнѧ́шесѧ стра́хомъ, * зрѧ́щи тѧ̀ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ ви́сима Хрⷭ҇тѐ, * со́лнце ѡ҆мрача́шесѧ, * и҆ землѝ ѡ҆снова̑нїѧ сотрѧса́хꙋсѧ, * всѧ̑ сострада́хꙋ Созда́вшемꋋ всѧ̑, * во́лею на́съ ра́ди, претерпѣ́вый, * Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀. Два́жды.
items.english_text: Ye wicked and lawless people, why do ye meditate on vain things? Why did ye condemn to death the Life of all? A great wonder! That the Creator of the world is delivered into the hands of the lawless, and the Lover of mankind is lifted up upon the Tree, that He may free the prisoners in hades, who cry: O long-suffering Lord, glory to Thee!

items.slavonic_text: Гла́съ в҃:
items.english_text: Today the blameless Virgin, seeing Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Word, weeping with a mother's bowels, was bitterly wounded in her heart; and groaning sorrowfully from the depths of her soul, tearing her face and hair, and beating her breast, she cried out piteously: Woe is me, divine Child! Woe is me, Light of the world! Why hast Thou set from mine eyes, O Lamb of God? Therefore the hosts of the bodiless were held with trembling, saying: O incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee!

items.slavonic_text: Лю́дїе ѕлочести́вїи и҆ беззако́ннїи, * вскꙋ́ю поꙋча́ютсѧ тще́тнымъ; * вскꙋ́ю Живота̀ всѣ́хъ на сме́рть ѡ҆сꙋди́ша; * ве́лїе чꙋ́до, ꙗ҆́кѡ Созда́тель мі́ра въ рꙋ́ки беззако́нныхъ предае́тсѧ, * и҆ на дре́во возвыша́етсѧ Чл҃колю́бецъ, * да ꙗ҆́же во а҆́дѣ ᲂу҆́зники свободи́тъ, зовꙋ́щыѧ: * долготерпѣли́ве Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
items.english_text: Beholding Thee hanging upon the Tree, O Christ, the Creator and God of all, she who bore Thee without seed cried bitterly: My Son, whither has the beauty of Thy countenance departed? I cannot bear to behold Thee unjustly crucified: make haste therefore to arise, that I also may see Thy three-day Resurrection from the dead!

items.english_text: Today the Master of creation stands before Pilate, and to the Cross is delivered the Creator of all: as a sheep led of His own will, He is nailed with nails, and in His side is pierced, and with a sponge is given drink by He Who rained down manna; upon the cheek is buffeted the Redeemer of the world, and by His own servants is mocked the Creator of all. O Master's love for mankind! For them that crucified Him He prayed to His Father, saying: Father, forgive them this sin; for the lawless know not what injustice they do.

items.slavonic_text: Дне́сь Влⷣка тва́ри предстои́тъ Пїла́тꙋ, * и҆ крⷭ҇тꙋ̀ предаетсѧ Зижди́тель всѣ́хъ: * ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́гнецъ приводи́мь свое́ю во́лею, * гвоздьмѝ пригвожда́етсѧ, * и҆ въ ре́бра прокола́етсѧ, * и҆ гꙋ́бою напаѧ́етсѧ ма́ннꙋ ѡ҆дожди́вый, * по лани́тѣ заꙋша́етсѧ И҆зба́витель мі́ра, * и҆ ѿ свои́хъ ра̑бъ порꙋга́етсѧ Созда́тель всѣ́хъ. * Ѡ҆ Влⷣчнягѡ чл҃вѣколю́бїѧ! * ѡ҆ распина́ющихъ молѧ́ше своего̀ Ѻ҆ц҃а̀, глаго́лѧ: * Ѻ҆́ч҃е, ѡ҆ста́ви и҆̀мъ грѣ́хъ се́й: * не вѣ́дѧтъ бо беззако́ннїи, что̀ непра́ведное содѣва́ютъ.
items.english_text: O how the lawless assembly condemned to death the King of creation! Not being ashamed of the benefits which He, putting them in remembrance, had confirmed before, saying unto them: My people, what have I done unto you? Have I not filled Judea with wonders? Have I not raised the dead with a single word? Have I not healed every disease and sickness? What then do ye render unto Me? Why do ye not remember Me? In return for healings, ye have laid wounds upon Me; instead of life, ye put Me to death; hanging upon the Tree as an evildoer the Benefactor, as a transgressor the Lawgiver, as a condemned man the King of all! O long-suffering Lord, glory to Thee!

items.slavonic_text: Ѡ҆ ка́кѡ беззако́нное со́нмище, * Цр҃ѧ̀ тва́ри ѡ҆сꙋдѝ на сме́рть! * не ᲂу҆стыдѣ́всѧ благодѣѧ́нїѧ, * ꙗ҆́же воспомина́ѧ пред̾ꙋтвержда́ше, глаго́лѧ къ ни̑мъ: * лю́дїе моѝ, что̀ сотвори́хъ ва́мъ; * не чꙋде́съ ли и҆спо́лнихъ І҆ꙋде́ю; * не мертвецы̀ ли воскреси́хъ є҆ди́нѣмъ сло́вомъ; * не всѧ́кꙋ ли болѣ́знь и҆сцѣли́хъ и҆ недꙋ́гъ; * что̀ ᲂу҆́бѡ мѝ воздаетѐ; * вскꙋ́ю не по́мните мѧ̀; * за и҆сцѣле́нїѧ ра̑ны мнѣ̀ наложи́вше, * за живо́тъ ᲂу҆мерщвлѧ́юще, * вѣ́шающе на дре́вѣ ꙗ҆́кѡ ѕлодѣ́ѧ, Бл҃годѣ́телѧ: * ꙗ҆́кѡ беззако́нна, Законода́вца: * ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нна, всѣ́хъ Цр҃ѧ̀: * долготерпѣли́ве Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
items.english_text: A fearsome and most glorious mystery is seen accomplished today: He Who is untouchable is held; He Who loosed Adam from the curse is bound; He Who tris the hearts and reins is unjustly tried; He Who shut up the abyss is shut up in prison; before Pilate stands He before Whom heavenly powers stand with trembling; with the hand of the creature the Creator is buffeted; to the Tree is condemned He Who judges the living and the dead; in the tomb is enclosed the Destroyer of hades! O Thou Who didst endure all things mercifully, and hast saved all from the curse, O innocent Lord, glory to Thee!

items.english_text: The Lord spoke unto Moses face to face, as if one should speak unto his friend; and he returned into the camp; but his minister Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle. And Moses said unto the Lord: Behold, Thou sayest unto me: Bring up this people; yet Thou hast not shown me whom Thou wilt send with me. But Thou hast said unto me: I know thee above all, and thou hast found grace with Me. If therefore I have found grace in Thy sight, manifest Thyself unto me, that I may clearly see Thee, that I may find grace in Thy sight, and that I may know that this great nation is Thy people. And the Lord said unto him: I Myself will go before thee, and I will give thee rest. And Moses said unto Him: If Thou Thyself go not with us, lead me not up hence. And how shall it be known truly that I and Thy people have found grace with Thee, unless Thou go with us? And so shall I and Thy people be glorified beyond all the nations that are upon the earth. And the Lord said unto Moses: I will do this word also that thou hast spoken; for thou hast found grace before Me, and I know thee above all. And Moses said: Show me Thy glory. And the Lord said unto Moses: I will go before thee in My glory, and I will call upon the name of the Lord before thee; and I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. And He said: Thou canst not see My face; for man shall not see My face, and live. And the Lord said: Behold, there is a place by Me, and thou shalt stand upon the rock; and when My glory passes by, I will put thee in a cleft of the rock, and will cover thee with My hand over thee, until I have passed by. And I will take away My hand, and then shalt thou see My back; but My face shall not be revealed unto thee.

И҆ ка́кѡ вѣ́домо бꙋ́детъ вои́стиннꙋ, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆брѣто́хъ благода́ть ᲂу҆ тебѐ, а҆́зъ же и҆ лю́дїе твоѝ, то́чїю и҆дꙋ́щꙋ тѝ съ на́ми; и҆ просла́вленъ бꙋ́дꙋ, а҆́зъ же и҆ лю́дїе твоѝ, па́че всѣ́хъ ꙗ҆зы́къ, є҆ли́цы сꙋ́ть на землѝ. Рече́ же Гдⷭ҇ь къ Мѡѷсе́ю: и҆ сїѐ тебѣ̀ сло́во, є҆́же ре́клъ є҆сѝ, сотворю̀: ѡ҆брѣ́лъ бо є҆сѝ благода́ть предо мно́ю, и҆ вѣ́мъ тѧ̀ па́че всѣ́хъ. И҆ глаго́ла Мѡѷсе́й: покажи́ ми сла́вꙋ твою̀. И҆ речѐ (Гдⷭ҇ь къ Мѡѷсе́ю): а҆́зъ пред̾идꙋ̀ пред̾ тобо́ю сла́вою мое́ю, и҆ воззовꙋ̀ ѡ҆ и҆́мени мое́мъ, Гдⷭ҇ь пред̾ тобо́ю: и҆ поми́лꙋю, є҆го́же а҆́ще ми́лꙋю: и҆ ᲂу҆ще́дрю, є҆го́же а҆́ще ще́дрю. И҆ речѐ: не возмо́жеши ви́дѣти лица̀ моегѡ̀: не бо̀ ᲂу҆́зритъ чл҃вѣ́къ лицѐ моѐ, и҆ жи́въ бꙋ́детъ. И҆ речѐ Гдⷭ҇ь: сѐ мѣ́сто ᲂу҆ менѐ, и҆ ста́неши на ка́мени. Є҆гда́ же пре́йдетъ сла́ва моѧ̀, и҆ положꙋ́ тѧ въ разсѣ́линѣ ка́мене, и҆ покры́ю рꙋко́ю мое́ю над̾ тобо́ю, до́ндеже мимоидꙋ̀. И҆ ѿимꙋ̀ рꙋ́кꙋ мою̀, и҆ тогда̀ ᲂу҆́зриши за̑днѧѧ моѧ̑: лицѐ же моѐ не ꙗ҆ви́тсѧ тебѣ̀.

items.slavonic_text: Стї́хъ: Прїимѝ ѻ҆рꙋ́жїе и҆ щи́тъ, и҆ воста́ни въ по́мощь мою̀.
items.english_text: The Lord blessed the latter days of Job more than the former; and he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses of the pasture. And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters. And he called the name of the first, Day; and the second, Cassia; and the third, Amalthea's Horn. And there were not found women so fair as the daughters of Job in all that is under heaven; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brethren. And Job lived after his affliction a hundred and seventy years; and all the years he lived were two hundred and forty-eight. And Job saw his sons, and his sons' sons, unto the fourth generation. And Job died, an old man, and full of days. And it is written that he shall rise again with those whom the Lord raises up: thus is it interpreted from the Syriac book. He dwelt in the land of Ausitis, on the borders of Idumaea and Arabia; and his name before was Jobab. And taking an Arabian wife, he begat a son whose name was Enon. And he was the son of his father Zaretha, a son of the sons of Esau, and of his mother Bosorra; so that he was the fifth from Abraham.

items.slavonic_text: Стї́хъ: Гдⷭ҇и Бж҃е спасе́нїѧ моегѡ̀, во дни̑ воззва́хъ и҆ въ нощѝ пред̾ тобо́ю.
items.english_text: Brethren: The word of the cross is foolishness unto them that perish, but unto us who are being saved it is the power of God. For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will reject the understanding of the prudent. Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this age? Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. For the Jews require signs, and the Greeks seek after wisdom; but we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumbling block, and unto the Greeks foolishness; but unto them that are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God. Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men. For see your calling, brethren, that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called. But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to put to shame the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to put to shame the mighty; and base things of the world, and things that are despised, hath God chosen, and things that are not, to bring to naught things that are; that no flesh should boast before God. But of Him are ye in Christ Jesus, Who of God was made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption: that, according as it is written: He that gloris, let him glory in the Lord. And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God. For I determined not to know anything among you, save Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.

items.slavonic_text: зꙋмѣ̀ мі́ръ премꙋ́дростїю Бг҃а, бл҃гоизво́ли Бг҃ъ бꙋ́йствомъ про́повѣди спастѝ вѣ́рꙋющихъ. Поне́же и҆ І҆ꙋде́е зна́менїа про́сѧтъ, и҆ Е҆́ллини премꙋ́дрости и҆́щꙋтъ: мы́ же проповѣ́дꙋемъ Хрⷭ҇та̀ распѧ́та, І҆ꙋде́емъ ᲂу҆́бѡ собла́знъ, Е҆́ллинѡмъ же безꙋ́мїе: са́мымъ же зва̑ннымъ І҆ꙋде́емъ же и҆ Е҆́ллинѡмъ, Хрⷭ҇та̀ Бж҃їю си́лꙋ и҆ Бж҃їю премꙋ́дрость. Занѐ бꙋ́ее Бж҃їе, премꙋ́дрѣе человѣ̑къ є҆́сть: и҆ немощно́е Бж҃їе, крѣпча́е человѣ̑къ є҆́сть. Ви́дите бо зва́нїе ва́ше, бра́тїе, ꙗ҆́кѡ не мно́зи премꙋ́дри по пло́ти, не мно́зи си́льни, не мно́зи бл҃горо́дни: но бꙋ̑ѧ мі́ра и҆збра̀ Бг҃ъ, да премꙋ̑дрыѧ посрами́тъ: и҆ немощна̑ѧ мі́ра и҆збра̀ Бг҃ъ, да посрами́тъ крѣ̑пкаѧ: и҆ хꙋдоро̑днаѧ мі́ра и҆ ᲂу҆ничиже́ннаѧ и҆збра̀ Бг҃ъ, и҆ не сꙋ̑щаѧ, да сꙋ̑щаѧ ᲂу҆праздни́тъ. Ꙗ҆́кѡ да не похва́литсѧ всѧ́ка пло́ть пред̾ Бг҃омъ. И҆з̾ негѡ́же вы́ є҆стѐ ѡ҆ Хрⷭ҇тѣ̀ І҆и҃сѣ, и҆́же бы́сть на́мъ премꙋ́дрость ѿ Бг҃а, пра́вда же и҆ ѡ҆сщ҃е́нїе и҆ и҆збавле́нїе: да, ꙗ҆́коже пи́шетсѧ: Хвалѧ́йсѧ, ѡ҆ Гдⷭ҇ѣ да хва́литсѧ. И҆ а҆́зъ прише́дъ къ ва́мъ, бра́тїе, прїидо́хъ не по превосхо́дномꙋ словесы̀ и҆лѝ премꙋ́дрости, возвѣща́ѧ ва́мъ свидѣ́тельство Бж҃їе. Не сꙋди́хъ бо вѣ́дѣти что̀ въ ва́съ, то́чїю І҆и҃са Хрⷭ҇та̀, и҆ сегѡ̀ распѧ́та.

items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, гла́съ є҃:
items.english_text: Thee Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, Joseph with Nicodemus took down from the Tree; and beholding Thee dead, naked, and unburied, he took up a compassionate lamentation, and weeping said: Woe is me, sweetest Jesus! Whom a little while ago the sun, seeing hanging upon the Cross, wrapped itself in darkness, and the earth quaked with fear, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain; but lo, now I behold Thee, for my sake willingly undergoing death! How shall I bury Thee, my God? Or with what winding-sheet shall I wrap Thee? With what hands shall I touch Thine incorrupt Body? Or what songs shall I sing for Thy departure, O Compassionate One? I magnify Thy Passions, I hymn also Thy Burial with the Resurrection, crying: Lord, glory to Thee!

provenance.verbatim_source: Thee Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, Joseph with Nicodemus took down from the Tree; and beholding Thee dead, naked, and unburied, he took up a compassionate lamentation, and weeping said: Woe is me, sweetest Jesus! I magnify Thy Passions, I hymn also Thy Burial with the Resurrection, crying: Lord, glory to Thee!

items.slavonic_text: Мѵроно́сицамъ жена́мъ при гро́бѣ предста́въ а҆́гг҃лъ вопїѧ́ше: мѵ́ра ме́ртвымъ сꙋ́ть прили́чна, Хрⷭ҇то́съ же и҆стлѣ́нїѧ ꙗ҆ви́сѧ чꙋ́ждь.
items.english_text: May He Who for the sake of us men and for our salvation, endured in the flesh the dread Passions, and the life-creating Cross, and the voluntary Burial, for the sake of our salvation, Christ our true God, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, and of all the Saints, have mercy on us and save us, as He is good and the Lover of mankind.

provenance.verbatim_source: May He Who for the sake of us men and for our salvation, endured in the flesh the dread Passions, and the life-creating Cross, and the voluntary Burial, for the sake of our salvation, Christ our true God, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, and of all the Saints, have mercy on us and save us, as He is good and the Lover of mankind.

items.english_text: *Troparion:* Willingly, my Son and Creator, dost Thou endure cruel death upon the Tree, the Virgin said, standing by the Cross with the beloved disciple.

items.english_text: *Ode 4. Heirmos:* Christ is my power, God and Lord, the venerable Church sings in godly manner, crying from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord.

items.english_text: *Troparion:* O unwaning Sun, eternal God, and Creator of all creation, O Lord, how dost Thou endure Passion upon the Cross? the pure Virgin said, weeping.

items.slavonic_text: Хрⷭ҇то́съ моѧ̀ си́ла, Бг҃ъ и҆ Гдⷭ҇ь, * честна́ѧ Цр҃ковь бг҃олѣ́пнѡ пое́тъ взыва́ющи, * ѿ смы́сла чи́ста ѡ҆ Гдⷭ҇ѣ пра́зднꙋющи.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Weeping, the unwedded Virgin said unto the noble counselor: Make haste, Joseph, go to Pilate, and beg to take down from the Tree thy Teacher.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Пла́чꙋщи глаго́лаше Браконеискꙋ́снаѧ ко бл҃гоѡбра́зномꙋ: * потщи́ся І҆ѡ́сифе къ Пїла́тꙋ пристꙋпи́ти, * и҆ и҆спросѝ снѧ́ти со дре́ва Оу҆чи́телѧ твоего̀.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Seeing the All-Pure shedding bitter tears, Joseph was troubled, and weeping went to Pilate, crying with tears: Give me the Body of my God!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.english_text: *Theotokion:* Seeing Thee wounded, and without glory, naked upon the Tree, my Child, I burn within my bowels, lamenting as a Mother, the Virgin uttered.

items.english_text: *Troparion:* Torn with grief, weeping, and wondering together with Nicodemus, Joseph took Thee down, and kissing the most pure Body, he wept and groaned, singing of Him as God.

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.english_text: *Troparion:* My only Hope and Life, Master, my Son and God, the Light of mine eyes had I, Thine handmaid; but now am I deprived of Thee, my sweet Child and darling!

items.english_text: *Troparion:* I see Thee dead, O Lover of mankind, Who didst quicken the dead and holdest all things, and I am sorely wounded in my bowels; I would fain die with Thee, the All-Pure said: for I cannot bear to behold Thee dead without breath.

items.english_text: *Troparion:* I marvel beholding Thee, O most good God and all-wise Lord, without glory, without breath, and formless; and weeping I hold Thee, for I hoped not, woe is me, to see Thee, my Son and God!

items.slavonic_text: Дивлю́ся зрѧ́щи тѧ̀, пребл҃гі́й Бж҃е, * и҆ премꙋ́дрый Гдⷭ҇и, * без̾ сла́вы, и҆ без̾ дыха́нїѧ, и҆ без̾ѻбра́зна, * и҆ пла́чꙋся держа́щи тѧ̀, * ꙗ҆́кѡ не надѣ́ѧхся, ᲂу҆вы̀ мнѣ̀, ви́дѣти тѧ̀, Сн҃е мо́й и҆ Бж҃е.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Wilt Thou not speak a word unto Thine handmaid, O Word of God? Wilt Thou not have compassion, O Master, on her who bore Thee? said the pure Virgin, lamenting and weeping, kissing the Body of her Lord.

provenance.verbatim_source:

Wilt Thou not speak a word unto Thine handmaid, O Word of God? Wilt Thou not have compassion, O Master, on her who bore Thee? said the pure Virgin, lamenting and weeping, kissing the Body of her Lord.

items.slavonic_text: Не и҆зглаго́леши ли рабѣ̀ твое́й сло́ва, Сло́ве Бж҃їй; * не ᲂу҆ще́дриши ли, Влⷣко, тебѐ Ро́ждшꙋю; * гла́ше Чⷭ҇таѧ, рыда́ющи, и҆ пла́чꙋщи, * ѡ҆блобыза́ющи Тѣ́ло Гдⷭ҇а своегѡ̀.
items.english_text: *Theotokion:* I consider, O Master, that no more shall I hear Thy sweet voice, nor see the beauty of Thy face, as Thine handmaid did before; for Thou hast set from mine eyes, my Son!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Помышлѧ́ю Влⷣко, ꙗ҆́кѡ ктомꙋ̀ сла́дкагѡ твоегѡ̀ не ᲂу҆слы́шꙋ гла́са, * ни добро́ты лица̀ твоегѡ̀ ᲂу҆зрю̀, ꙗ҆́коже пре́жде раба̀ твоѧ̀: * ꙗ҆́кѡ заше́лъ є҆сѝ, Сн҃е мо́й, ѿ ѻ҆́чїю мое́ю.
items.english_text: *Ikos:*[^280] Seeing her own Lamb drawn unto the slaughter, Mary followed with hair disheveled, together with the other women, crying thus: Whither goest Thou, Child? For what cause dost Thou accomplish this swift course? Is there again another marriage in Cana, and dost Thou now hasten thither, that Thou mayest make wine for them from water? Shall I go with Thee, Child, or shall I rather wait for Thee? Give me a word, O Word; pass me not by in silence, Thou Who didst keep me pure: for Thou art my Son and my God.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ikos:*[^280]
Seeing her own Lamb drawn unto the slaughter, Mary followed with hair disheveled, together with the other women, crying thus: Whither goest Thou, Child? For what cause dost Thou accomplish this swift course? Is there again another marriage in Cana, and dost Thou now hasten thither, that Thou mayest make wine for them from water? Shall I go with Thee, Child, or shall I rather wait for Thee? Give me a word, O Word; pass me not by in silence, Thou Who didst keep me pure: for Thou art my Son and my God.

items.slavonic_text: Конда́къ, гла́съ в҃:
items.english_text: *Ode 7. Heirmos:* An Angel made the furnace sprinkle dew for the righteous youths, but the command of God consuming the Chaldeans persuaded the tyrant to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

items.slavonic_text: На́съ ра́ди Распѧ́таго прїиди́те всѝ воспои́мъ, * того́ бо ви́дѣ Марї́а на дре́вѣ, и҆ глаго́лаше: * а҆́ще и҆ Распѧ́тїе терпи́ши, ты̀ є҆сѝ Сы́нъ, и҆ Бг҃ъ мо́й.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Where, my Son and God, is the good tidings of old which Gabriel spoke unto me, calling Thee King, Son, and God of the Most High? But now I see Thee, my sweet Light, a naked and wounded corpse!

provenance.verbatim_source:

Where, my Son and God, is the good tidings of old which Gabriel spoke unto me, calling Thee King, Son, and God of the Most High? But now I see Thee, my sweet Light, a naked and wounded corpse!

items.slavonic_text: І҆́косъ:
items.english_text: *Troparion:* O Thou Who deliverest from afflictions, now receive me with Thee, my Son and God, that I also, O Master, may descend into hades with Thee; leave me not alone, for I can no longer bear to live without seeing Thee, my sweet Light!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
O Thou Who deliverest from afflictions, now receive me with Thee, my Son and God, that I also, O Master, may descend into hades with Thee; leave me not alone, for I can no longer bear to live without seeing Thee, my sweet Light!

items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва:
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Weeping bitterly with the other myrrh-bearing women, and seeing Christ borne away, the Blameless Virgin said: Woe is me, what do I see! Whither goest Thou now, my Son, and leavest me alone?

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Weeping bitterly with the other myrrh-bearing women, and seeing Christ borne away, the Blameless Virgin said: Woe is me, what do I see! Whither goest Thou now, my Son, and leavest me alone?

items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ:
items.english_text: *Theotokion:* Fainting and weeping, the Blameless Virgin said unto the myrrh-bearing women: Mourn with me, and weep bitterly with me; for behold, my sweet Light and your Teacher is delivered unto the tomb!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: И҆знемога́ющи и҆ рыда́ющи, Непоро́чнаѧ, мѵроно́сицамъ гла́ше: * срыда́йте мѝ, и҆ спла́читеся го́рцѣ: * сѐ бо Свѣ́тъ мо́й сла́дкїй, и҆ Оу҆чи́тель ва́шъ, гро́бꙋ предае́тся.
items.english_text: *Ode 8. Heirmos:* Out of the flame didst Thou drop dew upon the righteous, and the sacrifice of the just didst Thou consume with water; for Thou doest all things, O Christ, merely by willing: Thee do we exalt unto all the ages!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Out of the flame didst Thou drop dew upon the righteous, and the sacrifice of the just didst Thou consume with water; for Thou doest all things, O Christ, merely by willing: Thee do we exalt unto all the ages!

items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь и҃. І҆рмо́съ:
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Seeing the Virgin weeping, Joseph was completely rent with grief, and cried bitterly: How shall I, O my God, now bury Thee, Thy servant? With what winding-sheets shall I wrap Thy Body?

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Seeing the Virgin weeping, Joseph was completely rent with grief, and cried bitterly: How shall I, O my God, now bury Thee, Thy servant? With what winding-sheets shall I wrap Thy Body?

items.office: ON HOLY AND GREAT FRIDAY, AT COMPLINE

items.slavonic_text: И҆з̾ пла́мене преподо́бнымъ ро́сꙋ и҆сточи́лъ є҆сѝ, * и҆ пра́веднагѡ же́ртвꙋ водо́ю попали́лъ є҆сѝ: * всѧ̑ бо твори́ши Хрⷭ҇тѐ, то́кмѡ є҆́же хотѣ́ти, * тѧ̀ превозно́симъ во всѧ̑ вѣ́ки.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Beyond all understanding surpasses Thy strange vision, O Lord Who upholdest all creation: therefore Joseph, carrying Thee as a dead man in his hands, with Nicodemus bears Thee and buris Thee.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Beyond all understanding surpasses Thy strange vision, O Lord Who upholdest all creation: therefore Joseph, carrying Thee as a dead man in his hands, with Nicodemus bears Thee and buris Thee.

items.slavonic_text: Па́че ᲂу҆ма̀ превзы́де стра́нное твоѐ видѣ́нїе носѧ́щаго тва́рь всю̀ Гдⷭ҇а: * сегѡ̀ ра́ди І҆ѡ́сифъ ꙗ҆́кѡ ме́ртва тѧ̀ на рꙋкꙋ̀ свое́ю, * и҆ съ Нїкоди́момъ но́ситъ и҆ погреба́етъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* A strange and most glorious mystery do I see, the Virgin cried unto her Son and Lord: how art Thou laid in a poor tomb, O Thou Who raisest up the dead in the tombs by Thy command?

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
A strange and most glorious mystery do I see, the Virgin cried unto her Son and Lord: how art Thou laid in a poor tomb, O Thou Who raisest up the dead in the tombs by Thy command?

items.slavonic_text: Стра́ннꙋю ви́жꙋ и҆ пресла́внꙋю та́йнꙋ, * Дв҃а вопїѧ́ше Сн҃ꙋ и҆ Гдⷭ҇ꙋ: * ка́кѡ въ хꙋдо́мъ гро́бѣ полага́ешися, * ме́ртвыѧ повелѣ́нїемъ возставля́ѧй во гробѣ́хъ;
items.english_text: *Theotokion:* Neither will I arise from Thy tomb, my Child, nor will I cease shedding tears, Thine handmaid, until I also descend into hades; for I cannot bear separation from Thee, my Son!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Theotokion:*
Neither will I arise from Thy tomb, my Child, nor will I cease shedding tears, Thine handmaid, until I also descend into hades; for I cannot bear separation from Thee, my Son!

items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ:
items.english_text: *Ode 9. Heirmos:* God cannot be seen of men, upon Whom the ranks of Angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O All-Pure, was the Word incarnate made visible unto men: Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts we call thee blessed.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God cannot be seen of men, upon Whom the ranks of Angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O All-Pure, was the Word incarnate made visible unto men: Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts we call thee blessed.

items.slavonic_text: Ни ѿ гро́ба твоегѡ̀ воста́нꙋ, Ча́до моѐ, * ни сле́зы точа́щи преста́нꙋ, Раба̀ твоѧ̀, * до́ндеже и҆ а҆́зъ сни́дꙋ во а҆́дъ: * не могꙋ́ бо терпѣ́ти разлꙋче́нїѧ твоегѡ̀, Сн҃е мо́й.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Joy shall never touch me henceforth, the Blameless Virgin said, weeping: my Light and my Joy is departed into the tomb; but I will not leave Him alone, here will I die, and be buried with Him!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Joy shall never touch me henceforth, the Blameless Virgin said, weeping: my Light and my Joy is departed into the tomb; but I will not leave Him alone, here will I die, and be buried with Him!

items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь ѳ҃. І҆рмо́съ:
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Heal now the wound of my soul, my Child, the All-Pure cried with tears: arise, and assuage my pain and sorrow; for Thou canst do whatsoever Thou willest, O Master, even though Thou hast been buried willingly.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
Heal now the wound of my soul, my Child, the All-Pure cried with tears: arise, and assuage my pain and sorrow; for Thou canst do whatsoever Thou willest, O Master, even though Thou hast been buried willingly.

items.office: ON HOLY AND GREAT FRIDAY, AT COMPLINE

items.slavonic_text: Ра́дость мнѣ̀ николи́же ѿсе́лѣ прико́снетсѧ, * рыда́ющи гла́ше Непоро́чнаѧ: * Свѣ́тъ мо́й и҆ Ра́дость моѧ̀ во гро́бъ за́йде: * но не ѡ҆ста́влю Є҆го̀ є҆ди́наго, * здѣ́ же ᲂу҆мрꙋ̀, и҆ спогребꙋ́ся Е҆мꙋ̀.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* O how the abyss of compassion is hidden from thee! the Lord said secretly unto His Mother: for willing to save My creation, I have chosen to die; but I will also arise, and will magnify thee, as God of heaven and earth.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*
O how the abyss of compassion is hidden from thee! the Lord said secretly unto His Mother: for willing to save My creation, I have chosen to die; but I will also arise, and will magnify thee, as God of heaven and earth.

items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ:
items.english_text: *Theotokion:* I will hymn Thy mercy, O Lover of mankind, and I worship the riches of Thy compassion, O Master: for willing to save Thy creation, Thou hast undergone death, said the All-Pure; but by Thy Resurrection, O Savior, have mercy on us all.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Theotokion:*
I will hymn Thy mercy, O Lover of mankind, and I worship the riches of Thy compassion, O Master: for willing to save Thy creation, Thou hast undergone death, said the All-Pure; but by Thy Resurrection, O Savior, have mercy on us all.

items.slavonic_text: Благообра́зный Їѡ́сифъ, съ дре́ва сне́мъ пречⷭ҇тое Тѣ́ло твоѐ, плащани́цею чи́стою ѡ҆бви́въ, и҆ вонѧ́ми во гро́бѣ но́вѣ покры́въ положѝ.
items.english_text: *Troparion, Tone 2:*[^287] The noble Joseph, having taken down Thy most pure Body from the Tree, wrapped it in a clean winding-sheet, and covering it with fragrant spices, laid it in a new tomb.

items.slavonic_text: Е҆гда̀ снизше́лъ є҆сѝ къ сме́рти, Животѐ безсме́ртный, тогда̀ а҆́да ꙋ҆мертви́лъ є҆сѝ блиста́нїемъ Бж҃тва̀: є҆гда́ же и҆ ꙋ҆ме́ршыѧ ѿ преиспо́днихъ воскреси́лъ є҆сѝ, всѧ̑ Си̑лы нбⷭ҇ныѧ взыва́хꙋ: Жизнода́вче Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е на́шъ сла́ва тебѣ̀.
items.english_text: *Troparion, in the same tone [Tone 2]:* When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life immortal, then didst Thou put hades to death with the radiance of Thy Divinity; and when Thou didst also raise up the dead from the subterranean depths, all the heavenly Powers cried out: O Life-giver, Christ our God, glory to Thee!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.english_text: *Troparion:* Falsely pretendest thou to love mankind, wretched, blind, all-destructive, faithless traitor, who didst sell the myrrh for a price!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Млⷭ҇ти твоеѧ̀ Гдⷭ҇и, и҆спо́лнь землѧ̀, ѡ҆правда́нїемъ твои̑мъ навчи́ мѧ. ѯ҃д
items.english_text: *Troparion:* What price hadst thou for the priceless heavenly Myrrh? What didst thou receive worthy of Him? Madness didst thou gain, most accursed Satan!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Бл҃гость сотвори́лъ є҆сѝ съ рабо́мъ твои́мъ, Гдⷭ҇и, по словесѝ твоемꙋ̀. ѯ҃є
items.english_text: *Troparion:* If thou art a lover of the poor, and grievest over the myrrh poured out for the purification of the soul, how sellest thou the Radiant One for gold?

provenance.verbatim_source:
