items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Въ то́йже де́нь, въ Нд҃лю шестꙋ́ю по Па́сцѣ, є҆́же ѿ рожде́нїѧ слѣпа́гѡ, пра́зднꙋемъ, Гд᷂ⷭа Бг҃а и҆ Сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хр᷂ⷭта̀ чꙋ́до, є҆́же оу҆́бѡ и҆ то̀ ѿ воды̀ содѣ́ѧсѧ, ꙗ҆́коже и҆ є҆́же ѡ҆ Самарѧны́ни и҆ ѡ҆ разсла́бленнѣмъ. Бы́сть же си́це: сꙋтꙋ̀ бесѣ́дꙋющꙋ І҆ꙋде́ѡмъ, и҆ себѐ ра́вна показꙋю́щꙋ Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ̀, и҆ пре́жде А҆враа́ма бы́ти, а҆́зъ є҆́смь глаго́лющꙋ, ѻ҆ни́ ка́менїе на него̀ ме́щꙋтъ. Оу҆́нъ же ѿходѧ̀ ѿтꙋ́дꙋ, ѡ҆брѣта́етъ слѣпа́го претыка́ющасѧ, [бя́ше же та́кѡ роди́лсѧ, ѻ҆́бразъ то́кмѡ є҆ди́нъ и҆ до́лный и҆мѣ́ѧ ѻ҆́чїю], Ѡ҆брѣ́тъ оу҆́бѡ є҆го̀ Сп҃съ си́це и҆мꙋ́ща, вопроша́емь быва́етъ ѿ оу҆чени́къ, [слы́шавшихъ є҆́же ѡ҆ разсла́бленномъ: сѐ здра́въ бы́лъ є҆сѝ, ктомꙋ̀ не согрѣша́й. И҆, ꙗ҆́кѡ грѣ́хъ роди́телей на ча́дѣхъ:] Оу҆чи́телю, кто̀ согрѣшѝ, се́й ли, и҆лѝ роди́тели є҆гѡ̀, да слѣ́пъ роди́сѧ; И҆́накѡ же, и҆ мнѣ́нїе нѣ́кое є҆пїкꙋ́рское содержа́ще, дꙋша́мъ предбыва́ти, и҆ согрѣши́вшымъ невеще́ственнѡ сходи́тисѧ въ тѣлеса̀, ꙗ҆̀же всѧ̑ ѿе́мля Хр᷂ⷭто́съ, речѐ: не си́хъ ра́ди, но да ꙗ҆вѧ́тсѧ дѣла̀ Бг҃ꙗ, си́рѣчь менѐ. Ни во ѡ҆ Ѻ҆ц҃ѣ̀ сло́во, а҆ є҆́же да̀, и҆зрече́нїѧ є҆́сть а҆ не вины̀. И҆ сѐ ре́къ Хр᷂ⷭто́съ, плюнꙋ́въ на зе́млю, и҆ бре́нїе сотвори́въ, и҆ пома́за є҆мꙋ̀ ѻ҆́чїю мѣ́ста, и҆ къ Сїлѡа́мскомꙋ и҆сто́чникꙋ и҆тѝ, и҆ оу҆мы́тисѧ повелѣва́етъ, да пока́жетъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ То́й є҆́сть въ нача́лѣ пе́рсть прїе́мый ѿ землѝ, и҆ созда́вый человѣ́ка. И҆ поне́же всѣ́хъ ѻ҆́ко бж҃е́ственнѣйше въ тѣлесѝ, сїѐ создава́етъ не сꙋ́щее, показва́ѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ дꙋше́вной си́лѣ движе́нїе то́й є҆́сть подава́ѧй: не пома́за же водо́ю, но плюнове́нїемъ. И҆ да вѣ́домо бꙋ́детъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ бл҃года́ть всѧ́кая ѿ плюнове́нїѧ оу҆́стъ бя́ше, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ къ Сїлѡа́мꙋ посла́ти того̀ хотѧ́ше. Оу҆мы́тисѧ же томꙋ̀ повелѣва́етъ, да не кто̀ та́мошнею земле́ю и҆ бре́нїемъ да́стъ цѣльбꙋ̀. Посыла́етъ же є҆го̀ къ Сїлѡа́мꙋ, да мно́ги и҆́мать и҆сцѣле́нїа послꙋ́хи, мно́ги бо срѣ́те и҆ды́й пома́заны бре́нїемъ и҆мѣ́ѧ ѻ҆́чи. Гл҃ютъ же нѣ́цыи, ꙗ҆́кѡ оу҆мы́вшемꙋсѧ не ѿложѝ, є҆́же бѣ̀ ѿ плюнове́нїа бре́нїе, но то́е бре́нїе приложе́нїемъ лꙋ́чшагѡ, во ѻ҆́чїю зда́нїа преѡбразова́шесѧ. Сїлѡа́мъ же, по́сланъ толкꙋ́етсѧ: крѣ́покъ бо та́й бѣ̀ гра́да І҆ерꙋсали́ма бя́ше. При Е҆зекі́и же ра́тникѡмъ ѡ҆бсѣ́дшымъ гра́дъ, и҆ Сїлѡа́ма ѿе́мшымъ, копа́тисѧ вода̀ ѿвсю́дꙋ, пре́днїѧ кла́дѧзи и҆ рѣ́ки и҆скопа́ша вну́трь, за принѧ́тїе воды̀. И҆ а҆́ще кто̀ повелѣ́нїемъ Прⷪ҇ро́ка И҆са́їи та́мѡ посыла́емь бя́ше, вода̀ па́ки и҆схожда́ше и҆ почерпа́шесѧ. А҆́ще ли же кто̀ ѿ ра́тникъ хотѧ́ше почерпстѝ, оу҆держава́хꙋсѧ воды̀ и҆сто́чницы, и҆ въ ѻ҆́нагѡ та́кѡ быва́ше. Да оу҆́бѡ пока́жетъ и҆ Хр᷂ⷭто́съ, ꙗ҆́кѡ то̀ Бг҃а и҆ са́мъ, сегѡ̀ ра́ди слѣпа́го посыла́етъ та́мѡ, и҆ свѣ́тъ а҆́бїе послѣ́дꙋетъ. Нѣ́цыи оу҆́бѡ воꙁмнѣ́ша, по́сланъ, Сїлѡа́мъ, толкова́тисѧ, и҆ настоя́щагѡ ра́ди слѣпца̀ по́сланна ѿ Хр᷂ⷭта̀. Воспѧ́щется оу҆́бѡ слѣпы́й, оу҆мы́вся, неизглаго́ланною нѣ́коею си́лою, ниже́ самомꙋ̀ пострада́вшемꙋ, та́инство оу҆вѣ́дѣвшемꙋ. Сосѣ́ди же и҆ и҆́накѡ зна́емїи є҆мꙋ̀, ви́дѣвше є҆го̀ добрѣ̀ прозрѣ́вша, сꙋмнѧ́щеся бяхꙋ̀: Оу҆́нъ же оу҆́бѡ и҆сповѣ́даше себѐ пре́жде бы́ти слѣ́па, и҆ ѡ҆ вино́вномъ прозрѣнїю вопроша́емь, цѣли́телѧ стра́сти Хр᷂ⷭта̀ проповѣ́даше. Фарїсе́ємъ оу҆́бѡ пресла́вное слы́шащымъ зна́менїе, па́ки Сп҃съ хꙋли́мь быва́етъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ Сꙋббѡ́ты не блюды́й. Въ Сꙋббѡ́тꙋ бо, ꙗ҆́коже во ѻ҆бы́чаѣ, и҆ є҆́же на слѣпо́мъ содѣ́ѧся. Ра́спрѧ оу҆́бѡ быва́етъ посредѝ си́хъ, ѻ҆́вѣмъ оу҆́бѡ глаго́лющымъ, ѿ Бг҃а бы́ти І҆и҃сꙋ, быва́емыхъ ра́ди чꙋде́съ, ѻ҆́вѣмъ же не ѿ Бг҃а, ꙗ҆́кѡ Сꙋббѡ́ты не храни́тъ. Бл҃го́е оу҆́бѡ мнѣ́нїе ѡ҆ не́мъ и҆мѣ́вшїи слѣпа́го вопроша́ютъ: Ты́ что̀ глаго́леши ѡ҆ не́мъ; Оу҆́нъ же Проро́ка є҆го̀ проповѣ́даетъ, є҆́же оу҆́бѡ ѻ҆́нѣхъ бя́ше честнѣ́йше. Оу҆нѝ же па́ки не вѣ́рꙋютъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ слѣ́пъ сꙋ́щꙋ, Хр᷂ⷭто́съ цѣльбꙋ дарова̀: оу҆́бѡ и҆ родителе́й є҆гѡ̀ призыва́ютъ, сосѣ́дѡмъ не вѣ́рꙋюще. Ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ па́че то̀ покры́ти хотѧ́ще: но и҆ вя́щше творя́тъ ꙗ҆вле́нно, родителемъ всѧ̑ и҆сповѣ́дающымъ, а҆́ще и҆ ѿ со́нмища ѿлꙋче́на бы́ти боѧ́щася, на ѻ҆́нагѡ во́зрастъ дѣѧ́нїе возводѧ́тъ. Но и҆ па́ки къ слѣпо́мꙋ глаго́лютъ: да́ждь сла́вꙋ Бг҃ꙋ, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѿ негѡ̀ и҆сцѣле́нъ, а҆ не ѿ Хр᷂ⷭта̀, грѣ́шенъ бо є҆́сть, ꙗ҆́кѡ разорѧ́етъ Сꙋббѡ́тꙋ. Се́й же дѣ́лы показа́ти хотя̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ є҆́сть: не вѣ́мъ глаго́летъ, є҆ди́но вѣ́мъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ слѣ́пъ сы́й, тѣ́мъ ви́ждꙋ. Па́ки оу҆́бѡ є҆мꙋ̀ реко́ша: ка́кѡ ѿве́рзе твоѝ ѻ҆́чи; Оу҆́нъ же стꙋжа́емь не пото́нцꙋ глаго́летъ, но составлѧ́етъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́ще не бы̀ ѿ Бг҃а бы́лъ, не бы̀ сицево́е зна́менїе сотвори́лъ. И҆ пе́рвѣе оу҆́бѡ досажда́емь быва́етъ ѿ ни́хъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆сповѣ́давый, и҆ оу҆чени́къ бы́ти ѡ҆́нагѡ, и҆ занѐ речѐ: никто́же ѿве́рзлъ є҆́сть ѻ҆́чи слѣпа́гѡ рожде́ннагѡ. Слѣпы̑ѧ бо и҆ дрꙋзі́и просвѣти́ша, рожде́нна же слѣ́па нижѐ є҆ди́нъ: порꙋга́вшеся оу҆́бѡ є҆мꙋ̀, дале́че ѿ со́нмища и҆згна́ша. По си́хъ же ѡ҆брѣта́етъ є҆го̀ І҆и҃съ, и҆ глаго́летъ є҆мꙋ̀: ты̀ вѣ́рꙋеши ли въ Сн҃а Бж҃їа; Оу҆́нъ же оу҆вѣ́дѣвъ, кто̀ є҆́сть, и҆́же съ ни́мъ глаго́лѧй, и҆ ви́димъ быва́ѧй тѣ́мъ, не бо вѣ́даше є҆го̀ пре́жде, ꙗ҆́кѡ слѣпы́й сы́й, поклони́ся є҆мꙋ̀, и҆ оу҆чени́къ є҆гѡ̀ бы́сть, бл҃года́нїе проповѣ́дꙋѧй. Рече́ся бы̀ сїѐ и҆ и҆зводи́тельнѡ: Слѣпы́й оу҆́бѡ, и҆ сꙋ́щїи ѿ ꙗ҆зы̑къ лю́дїе, и҆́хже преходѧ̀ клѣ́ветꙋ є҆́же на землѝ пожи́тїа а҆ не на нб҃сѝ, ѡ҆брѣ́те Хр᷂ⷭто́съ, най и҆ па́ки є҆вре́йскихъ ра́ди прїи́де люде́й: Преходѧ̀ же прїи́де и҆ ко ꙗ҆зы́кѡмъ. И҆ плюнꙋ́въ на зе́млю, и҆ бре́нїе сотвори́въ пома́за: клѣ́ветꙋ є҆́же навꙋчѝ а҆ пре́жде, занѐ ꙗ҆́кѡ ка́плѧ сни́де на зе́млю, и҆ воплоти́ся ѿ ст҃ы́ѧ Дв҃ы. Та́же и҆ бж҃е́ственное Кр҃ще́нїе предадѐ, є҆́же є҆́сть Сїлѡа́мъ. По се́мъ ѿ ꙗ҆зы̑къ хр᷂ⷭтїане́ти лю́дїе за Хр᷂ⷭта̀ на всѧ̑ дерза́ютъ, и҆ гони́ми быва́ютъ, и҆ свидѣ́тельствꙋютъ, и҆ послѣ́жде ѿ негѡ̀ проповѣ́дꙋютсѧ и҆ прославля́ютсѧ. Неисче́тною ми́лостїю твое́ю, Свѣтода́вче Хр᷂ⷭтѐ Бж҃е на́шъ, поми́лꙋй и҆ спасѝ на́съ, а҆ми́нь.

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь з҃. І҆рмо́съ:
items.english_text: On this same day, the Sixth Sunday after Pascha, we celebrate the miracle of our Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ wrought upon the man blind from birth, which indeed was also performed through water, even as the miracle of the Samaritan woman and that of the paralytic.[^1254] It came to pass thus: while Christ was conversing with the Jews, and showing Himself equal to the Father, and saying: "Before Abraham was, I am," they cast stones at Him (Jn 8:58–59). But He, departing thence, found a blind man stumbling—he had been born thus, having only the appearance of eyes and sunken sockets.[^1255] The Savior, finding him thus, was asked by His disciples, who had heard what was said concerning the paralytic: "Behold, thou art made whole; sin no more" (Jn 5:14), and that the sin of parents is visited upon children: "Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?" (Jn 9:2).[^1256] Otherwise also, holding a certain Epicurean notion that souls pre-exist, and having sinned immaterially, are joined into bodies—all of which Christ refuted, saying: "Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest," that is, Mine (Jn 9:3). Nor is the word spoken concerning the Father, and the "that" expresses the outcome and not the cause.[^1257] And having said this, Christ spat on the ground, made clay, and anointed the place of his eyes, and commanded him to go to the Pool of Siloam and wash, to show that He Himself in the beginning took dust from the earth and created man (Gen 2:7). And since the eye is the most divine member of all in the body, He creates that which did not exist, showing that He is the One Who gives motion also to the power of the soul. Nor did He anoint with water, but with spittle, that it might be known that all grace was from the spittle of His mouth, and that He intended to send him to Siloam. And He commanded him to wash, lest anyone should attribute the healing to the earth and clay of that place.[^1258] And He sends him to Siloam, that he might have many witnesses of the healing, for many met him as he walked with his eyes anointed with clay. And some say that when he washed, the clay from the spittle was not washed away, but that that clay, by the addition of that which was better, was transformed into the structure of eyes. Now "Siloam" is interpreted "Sent" (Jn 9:7); for it was a stronghold of the city of Jerusalem. In the days of Hezekiah, when enemies besieged the city and cut off Siloam, so that water was dug everywhere, they dug out the inner wells and streams within, for the reception of water. And if anyone was sent thither by the command of the Prophet Isaiah, the water again gushed forth and was drawn; but if any of the enemies wished to draw, the springs of water were withheld, and so it happened in their case. That Christ might therefore show that He also is of God, He sends the blind man thither, and light immediately follows. Some indeed thought that Siloam was interpreted "Sent" also on account of the present blind man sent by Christ.[^1259] The blind man then returned, having washed, by an ineffable power, the mystery being unknown even to him who had suffered it. And his neighbors and those who otherwise knew him, seeing him seeing well, were in doubt. But he confessed that he had formerly been blind, and being questioned concerning the cause of his receiving sight, proclaimed Christ, the healer of the affliction.[^1260] When the Pharisees heard of the marvelous sign, the Savior was again blasphemed, as not keeping the Sabbath; for on the Sabbath, as was His custom, that which was done unto the blind man was also performed. A division therefore arose among them: some saying that Jesus was of God on account of the miracles that were done, but others that He was not of God, because He kept not the Sabbath. Those who held a good opinion of Him questioned the blind man: "What sayest thou of Him?" And he proclaimed Him to be a Prophet, which was more honorable than their view. But they again did not believe that, when he was blind, Christ granted him healing; therefore they called his parents also, not believing his neighbors, wishing rather to conceal the matter; but they made it all the more evident, since the parents confessed everything, though fearing to be put out of the synagogue, referring the deed to his own age.[^1261] But again they say unto the blind man: "Give God the praise," for thou wast healed by Him and not by Christ; for He is a sinner, because He breaks the Sabbath. But he, wishing to show by deeds that He is God, said: "I know not; one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see." Again therefore they said unto him: "How opened He thine eyes?" But he, being vexed, did not speak in detail, but affirmed that if He were not of God, He could do no such sign. And at first he was reviled by them, because he had confessed, and was His disciple, and because he said: "Since the world began was it not heard that any man opened the eyes of one that was born blind" (Jn 9:32); for others also enlightened the blind, but one born blind none at all. Having mocked him therefore, they cast him far out of the synagogue.[^1262] After this Jesus found him, and said unto him: "Dost thou believe on the Son of God?" And he, having learned Who He was that was speaking with him and was seen by him—for he knew Him not before, being blind—worshiped Him, and became His disciple, proclaiming Thanksgiving.[^1263] This was said also allegorically: For the blind man is the people from among the Gentiles, whom Christ, passing by the calumny of living upon earth and not in heaven, found—even though He came again for the sake of the Hebrew people, yet passing by, He came also unto the Gentiles. And having spat upon the ground and made clay, He anointed him: which calumny He taught before, because He came down upon earth as a drop, and was incarnate of the Holy Virgin. Then He also delivered divine Baptism, which is Siloam. Thereafter, the Christian people from the Gentiles dare all things for Christ, and are persecuted, and bear witness, and afterward are proclaimed and glorified by Him.[^1264]

items.english_text: *Troparion:* When Thou didst arise from the dead, O King, the souls that were sleeping there arose together with Thee, glorifying Thy power, whereby the bonds of death were dissolved.[^1268]

provenance.verbatim_source:

When Thou didst arise from the dead, O King, the souls that were sleeping there arose together with Thee, glorifying Thy power, whereby the bonds of death were dissolved.[^1268]

items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Оу҆́трѡ ѵл҃ѳ
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Early in the morning the choir of women came to anoint Thee with myrrh; but having learned that Thou wast risen, O Lord, they rejoiced with the sacred disciples: through them grant us cleansing from evils.[^1269]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Ра́нѡ мѵропома́зати тѧ̀ же́нскїй прїи́де ли́къ, оу҆вѣ́дѣвше же, Гд᷂ⷭи, воста́вша тѧ̀, ра́довахꙋсѧ со сщ҃е́нными оу҆чн҃кѝ: и҆́миже пода́ждь на́мъ ѡ҆чище́нїе ѕѡ́лъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou didst anoint the eyes of the blind man with clay, and didst command him to go to Siloam; and having washed, immediately he saw, chanting unto Thee, O Christ, the King of all.[^1270]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst anoint the eyes of the blind man with clay, and didst command him to go to Siloam; and having washed, immediately he saw, chanting unto Thee, O Christ, the King of all.[^1270]

items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, Трⷪ҇ченъ:
items.english_text: The Father unoriginate, the Son co-unoriginate, and the most holy Spirit we praise, singing: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God, King of all![^1271]

provenance.verbatim_source: The Father unoriginate, the Son co-unoriginate, and the most holy Spirit we praise, singing: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God, King of all![^1271]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ, Бг҃оро́диченъ:
items.english_text: After childbearing thou didst appear a Virgin, O Pure One, for thou didst bear God, Who renewed nature by His own power, O all-undefiled one: Him entreat unceasingly, that we all may be saved.[^1272]

provenance.verbatim_source: After childbearing thou didst appear a Virgin, O Pure One, for thou didst bear God, Who renewed nature by His own power, O all-undefiled one: Him entreat unceasingly, that we all may be saved.[^1272]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: По Рождествѣ̀ Дв҃а ꙗ҆ви́лася є҆сѝ Ч᷂ⷭтаѧ, Бг҃а бо родила̀ є҆сѝ, ѡ҆бнови́вшаго є҆стество̀, Преч᷂ⷭтаѧ, си́лою свое́ю: є҆го́же молѝ (при́снѡ) спасти́ся всѣ̑мъ на́мъ.
items.english_text: *Katavasia:* Thou Who didst save the children that praised Thee in the fiery furnace: Blessed is the God of our Fathers![^1273]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Katavasia:*  
Thou Who didst save the children that praised Thee in the fiery furnace: Blessed is the God of our Fathers![^1273]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Катава́сіа:
items.english_text: *Ode 8. Heirmos:* The host of Angels, the assembly of men, the King and Creator of all: ye priests, praise; ye Levites, bless; ye peoples, supremely exalt unto all ages![^1274]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
The host of Angels, the assembly of men, the King and Creator of all: ye priests, praise; ye Levites, bless; ye peoples, supremely exalt unto all ages![^1274]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Въ пещѝ ѻ҆́гненнѣй пѣсносло́вцы спасы́й ѻ҆́троки, бл҃гослове́нъ Бг҃ъ Ѻ҆те́цъ на́шихъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* The angelic ranks, seeing Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, King of all, and all creation altering in fear, were dismayed, singing of Thy love for mankind.[^1275]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
The angelic ranks, seeing Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, King of all, and all creation altering in fear, were dismayed, singing of Thy love for mankind.[^1275]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь и҃. І҆рмо́съ:
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Hades below, seeing Thee, groaned, and swiftly surrendered the dead kept there from the ages, O Christ, who sang of Thy love for mankind.[^1276]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
Hades below, seeing Thee, groaned, and swiftly surrendered the dead kept there from the ages, O Christ, who sang of Thy love for mankind.[^1276]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: А҆́гг҃лѡвъ со́нмъ, человѣ́кѡвъ собо́ръ, Цр҃ѧ̀ и҆ Зижди́телѧ всѣ́хъ, сщ҃е́нницы по́йте, бл҃гослови́те леѵі́ти, лю́дїе превозноси́те во всѧ̑ вѣ́ки.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Working extraordinary wonders, O Christ, Thou wast of Thine own will lifted up upon the Cross, and didst join Thyself unto the dead, having slain hades, and by Thy fortitude Thou didst loose all the prisoners.[^1277]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
Working extraordinary wonders, O Christ, Thou wast of Thine own will lifted up upon the Cross, and didst join Thyself unto the dead, having slain hades, and by Thy fortitude Thou didst loose all the prisoners.[^1277]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: А҆́гг҃лстїи чи́нове на Кр᷂ⷭтѣ̀ тѧ̀ ви́дѣвше ви́сима, Хр᷂ⷭтѐ Всецарю̀, и҆ тва́рь всю̀ и҆змѣнѧ́юща стра́хомъ, оу҆жасо́шася, пою́ще твоѐ человѣколю́бїе.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou didst refashion the blind man who approached Thee, O Christ, commanding him to go unto the pool of Siloam, to wash and receive sight, and to proclaim Thee as God Who didst appear in the flesh for the salvation of the world.[^1278]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst refashion the blind man who approached Thee, O Christ, commanding him to go unto the pool of Siloam, to wash and receive sight, and to proclaim Thee as God Who didst appear in the flesh for the salvation of the world.[^1278]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: А҆́дъ до́лѣ тебѐ ви́дѣвъ, стена́ше, и҆ подава́ше ско́рѡ ме́ртвыѧ ѿ вѣ́ка та́мѡ храни̑мыѧ, Хр᷂ⷭтѐ, пѣсносло́вѧщыѧ твоѐ человѣколю́бїе.
items.english_text: *We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*[^1279]

provenance.verbatim_source: *We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*[^1279]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Сотворя́ѧ чꙋдеса̀, Хр᷂ⷭтѐ, и҆зря̑днаѧ, во́лею воздви́женъ бы́лъ є҆сѝ на Кр᷂ⷭтъ, и҆ съ ме́ртвыми совокꙋпи́лся є҆сѝ, оу҆мертви́вый а҆́да, и҆ всѧ̑ мꙋ́жествомъ ѡ҆рѣши́лъ є҆сѝ оу҆́зники.
items.english_text: *Triadikon:* O indivisible Trinity, unconfused Unity, God of all things and Creator of all, save from all temptations those who praise and faithfully worship Thy dominion![^1280]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Triadikon:*  
O indivisible Trinity, unconfused Unity, God of all things and Creator of all, save from all temptations those who praise and faithfully worship Thy dominion![^1280]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Бл҃гослови́мъ Ѻ҆ц҃а̀, и҆ Сн҃а, и҆ ст҃а́го Дх҃а, Гд᷂ⷭа.
items.english_text: O all-undefiled Virgin, full of the grace of God, pray ever unto thy Son, that He put me not to shame in the day of judgment, but number me among the chosen sheep.[^1281]

provenance.verbatim_source: O all-undefiled Virgin, full of the grace of God, pray ever unto thy Son, that He put me not to shame in the day of judgment, but number me among the chosen sheep.[^1281]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Трⷪ҇ченъ:
items.english_text: *We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord, singing and supremely exalting Him unto all ages.*[^1282]

provenance.verbatim_source: *We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord, singing and supremely exalting Him unto all ages.*[^1282]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Трⷪ҇це нераздѣ́льнаѧ, Є҆ди́нице неслїѧ́ннаѧ, Бж҃е всѧ́ческихъ, и҆ Зижди́телю всѣ́хъ, пѣсносло́вѧщыѧ и҆ вѣ́рнѡ покланя́ющыѧся держа́вѣ твое́й, ѿ всѧ́кихъ и҆скꙋше́нїй спаса́й.
items.english_text: *Katavasia:* The Son and God, begotten of the Father before the ages, and in latter times incarnate of the Virgin Mother: ye priests, praise; ye peoples, supremely exalt unto all ages![^1283]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Katavasia:*  
The Son and God, begotten of the Father before the ages, and in latter times incarnate of the Virgin Mother: ye priests, praise; ye peoples, supremely exalt unto all ages![^1283]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: ѵ҃м Въ Недѣ́лю ѡ҆ Слѣпо́мъ
items.english_text: *Ode 9. Heirmos:* For the Mighty One hath done great things unto thee, preserving thee a pure Virgin after childbearing, as having borne without seed thine own Creator: therefore, O Theotokos, we magnify thee.[^1285]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
For the Mighty One hath done great things unto thee, preserving thee a pure Virgin after childbearing, as having borne without seed thine own Creator: therefore, O Theotokos, we magnify thee.[^1285]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь ѳ҃. І҆рмо́съ:
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou wast nailed to the tree of the Cross, O Christ God, and didst vanquish all the opposing powers of the enemy, and didst destroy the primal curse, O Savior: therefore do we worthily magnify Thee.[^1286]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
Thou wast nailed to the tree of the Cross, O Christ God, and didst vanquish all the opposing powers of the enemy, and didst destroy the primal curse, O Savior: therefore do we worthily magnify Thee.[^1286]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Ꙗ҆́кѡ сотворѝ тебѣ̀ вели́чїѧ Си́льный, Дв҃ꙋ ч᷂ⷭтаѧ тѧ̀ по Рж᷂ⷭтвѣ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ ро́ждшꙋю без̾ сѣ́мене своего̀ Творца̀: тѣ́мъ тѧ̀ Бцⷣе велича́емъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* When hades below saw Thee with Thy soul, O Word, it groaned, and in fear released all the dead, who recognized the dominion of Thy power: therefore do we worthily magnify Thee.[^1287]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
When hades below saw Thee with Thy soul, O Word, it groaned, and in fear released all the dead, who recognized the dominion of Thy power: therefore do we worthily magnify Thee.[^1287]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: На дре́вѣ кр᷂ⷭти́чнѣмъ пригвозди́лсѧ є҆сѝ Хр᷂ⷭтѐ Бж҃е, и҆ всѧ̑ побѣди́лъ є҆сѝ вра̑жїѧ сопроти́внаѧ нача̑ла, и҆ пе́рвꙋю кля́твꙋ потреби́лъ є҆сѝ Сп҃се: тѣ́мже тѧ̀ по до́лгꙋ велича́емъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Beholding Him working signs and dread wonders, the assembly of the Hebrews through envy slew Him Who despoiled hades by His Resurrection, and Who, as Mighty, raises all.[^1288]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
Beholding Him working signs and dread wonders, the assembly of the Hebrews through envy slew Him Who despoiled hades by His Resurrection, and Who, as Mighty, raises all.[^1288]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Ꙗ҆́кѡ ви́дѣ тѧ̀, Сло́ве, а҆́дъ до́лѣ съ дꙋше́ю, воздохнꙋ̀, и҆ всѧ̑ ме́ртвыѧ стра́хомъ ѡ҆дрѣшѝ, позна́вшыѧ держа́вꙋ вла́сти твоеѧ̀: тѣ́мже тѧ̀ по до́лгꙋ велича́емъ.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou didst rise from the dead, as Thou hadst said, O Giver of life, and didst appear unto the holy disciples after Thy Rising, having wrought signs and refashioned the blind man: with them we magnify Thee unto the ages.[^1289]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst rise from the dead, as Thou hadst said, O Giver of life, and didst appear unto the holy disciples after Thy Rising, having wrought signs and refashioned the blind man: with them we magnify Thee unto the ages.[^1289]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Воста́лъ є҆сѝ, ꙗ҆́коже ре́клъ є҆сѝ, Животода́вче, и҆з̾ ме́ртвыхъ, и҆ ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ ст҃ы̑мъ Оу҆чн҃кѡ́мъ по Воста́нїи, зна́менїа сотвори́вый, и҆ восꙋи́вый слѣпца̀: съ ни́миже тѧ̀ во вѣ́ки велича́емъ.
items.english_text: The Light of the Father I revere, the Light of the Son I glorify, the Light of the right Spirit I hymn: one Light, indivisible, understood in three Persons, God and King of all creation.[^1290]

provenance.verbatim_source: The Light of the Father I revere, the Light of the Son I glorify, the Light of the right Spirit I hymn: one Light, indivisible, understood in three Persons, God and King of all creation.[^1290]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Свѣ́тъ Ѻ҆ц҃а̀ чтꙋ̀, свѣ́тъ сла́влю и҆ Сн҃а, свѣ́тъ воспѣва́ю Дх҃а пра́ваго, Є҆ди́нъ Свѣ́тъ, нераздѣ́льный, въ трїе́хъ лицѣ́хъ разꙋмѣва́емый, Бг҃а Цр҃ѧ̀ всеѧ̀ тва́ри.
items.english_text: Having appeared more spacious than the heavens, O pure Virgin, thou didst contain in the flesh the uncontainable God, and didst bear the Redemption of all who hymn thee with unwavering faith.[^1291]

provenance.verbatim_source: Having appeared more spacious than the heavens, O pure Virgin, thou didst contain in the flesh the uncontainable God, and didst bear the Redemption of all who hymn thee with unwavering faith.[^1291]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ, Бг҃оро́диченъ:
items.english_text: *Katavasia:* Thee, the Mother of God beyond mind and word, who didst ineffably give birth in time unto the Timeless One, we, the faithful, magnify with one accord.[^1292]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Katavasia:*  
Thee, the Mother of God beyond mind and word, who didst ineffably give birth in time unto the Timeless One, we, the faithful, magnify with one accord.[^1292]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Ꙗ҆ви́вшися простра́ннѣйшая нб҃съ, Дв҃о чи́стаѧ, вмѣсти́ла є҆сѝ пло́тїю Бг҃а невмѣсти́маго, и҆ родила̀ є҆сѝ всѣ́хъ И҆збавле́нїе, вѣ́рою несꙋмнѣ́нною воспѣва́ющихъ тѧ̀.
items.english_text: *Exapostilarion of Pascha, once:* Having fallen asleep in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst rise again, raising Adam from corruption and abolishing death: O Pascha of incorruption, salvation of the world![^1293]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Exapostilarion of Pascha, once:*  
Having fallen asleep in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst rise again, raising Adam from corruption and abolishing death: O Pascha of incorruption, salvation of the world![^1293]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Тѧ̀ па́че оу҆ма̀ и҆ словесѐ Мт҃рь Бж҃їю, въ лѣ́то Безлѣ́тнаго неизрече́ннѡ ро́ждшꙋю, вѣ́рнїи є҆диномꙋ́дреннѡ велича́емъ.
items.english_text: Enlighten my spiritual eyes, O Lord, blinded by darksome sin, implanting humility, O Compassionate One, and wash them with tears of repentance.[^1294]

provenance.verbatim_source: Enlighten my spiritual eyes, O Lord, blinded by darksome sin, implanting humility, O Compassionate One, and wash them with tears of repentance.[^1294]

items.slavonic_text: Пло́тїю оу҆снꙋ́въ ꙗ҆́кѡ ме́ртвъ, Цр҃ю̀ и҆ Гд᷂ⷭи, тридне́венъ воскре́слъ є҆сѝ, А҆да́ма воздви́гъ ѿ тлѝ, и҆ оу҆праздни́въ сме́рть, Па́сха нетлѣ́нїѧ, мі́ра спасе́нїе.
items.english_text: Passing by, our Savior found a man blind, lacking eyes; and having spat upon the ground and made clay, He anointed him, and sent him to Siloam to go and wash; and having washed, he came seeing Thy light, O my Christ.[^1295]

items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ, Подо́бенъ: Жєны̀ оу҆слы́шите:
items.english_text: O Lord, while the tomb was sealed by the lawless, Thou camest forth from the sepulcher, even as Thou wast born of the Theotokos: Thine incorporeal Angels understood not how Thou didst take flesh; the soldiers guarding Thee perceived not...[^1297] when Thou didst rise: for both things were sealed unto the inquirers, but wonders were made manifest unto those who worship the mystery in faith; grant joy and great mercy unto us who sing thereof.[^1298]

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Оу҆́трѡ ѵм҃а
items.english_text: O Lord, Who didst shatter the eternal bars and burst asunder the bonds, Thou didst rise from the tomb, leaving behind Thy grave-clothes, for a testimony of the true three-day Burial of Thine; and Thou didst go before into Galilee, Thou Who wast guarded in the cave: great is Thy mercy, O ungraspable Savior, have mercy on us and save us.[^1299]

items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: когда̀ воскре́слъ є҆сѝ, стрегꙋ́щїи тѧ̀ во́ини: ѻ҆́боѧ бо запеча́ташася и҆спытꙋ́ющымъ, ꙗ҆ви́шася же чꙋдеса̀, покланя́ющымся вѣ́рою та́инствꙋ: є҆́же воспѣва́ющымъ, возда́ждь на́мъ ра́дость, и҆ ве́лїю ми́лость.
items.english_text: O Lord, the women ran unto the tomb to see Thee, the Christ Who didst suffer for our sake; and having come, they found an Angel sitting upon the stone, seized with fear, and he cried unto them, saying: The Lord is risen! Say unto the disciples that He is risen from the dead, saving our souls.[^1300]

provenance.verbatim_source: O Lord, the women ran unto the tomb to see Thee, the Christ Who didst suffer for our sake; and having come, they found an Angel sitting upon the stone, seized with fear, and he cried unto them, saying: The Lord is risen! Say unto the disciples that He is risen from the dead, saving our souls.[^1300]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Гд᷂ⷭи, вереѝ вѣ̑чныѧ сокрꙋши́вый, и҆ оу҆́зы растерза́вый, ѿ гро́ба воскре́слъ є҆сѝ, ѡ҆ста́вль твоѧ̑ погреба́льная, во свидѣ́телство и҆́стиннагѡ тридне́внагѡ твоегѡ̀ Погребе́нїѧ: и҆ предвари́лъ є҆сѝ въ Галїле́и, въ пеще́рѣ стрего́мый: вели́кая твоѧ̀ мл᷂ⷭть, непостижи́ме Сп҃се, поми́лꙋй, и҆ спасѝ на́съ.
items.english_text: O Lord, even as Thou camest forth from the sealed tomb, so didst Thou enter, while the doors were shut, unto Thy disciples, showing them the bodily sufferings which Thou didst endure, O long-suffering Savior: for as of the seed of David, Thou didst undergo wounds; but as the Son of God, Thou didst set the world free: great is Thy mercy, O ungraspable Savior, have mercy on us and save us.[^1301]

provenance.verbatim_source: O Lord, even as Thou camest forth from the sealed tomb, so didst Thou enter, while the doors were shut, unto Thy disciples, showing them the bodily sufferings which Thou didst endure, O long-suffering Savior: for as of the seed of David, Thou didst undergo wounds; but as the Son of God, Thou didst set the world free: great is Thy mercy, O ungraspable Savior, have mercy on us and save us.[^1301]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Гд᷂ⷭи, ꙗ҆́коже и҆зше́лъ є҆сѝ ѿ запеча́таннагѡ гро́ба, та́кѡ вше́лъ є҆сѝ, и҆ две́ремъ заключе́ннымъ ко Оу҆чени́кѡмъ твои̑мъ, пока́зꙋя и҆̀мъ тѣлє́сная страда́нїѧ, ꙗ҆̀же подъя́лъ є҆сѝ Сп҃се долготерпѣли́вый: ꙗ҆́кѡ ѿ сѣ́мене Дв҃дова, ꙗ҆́звы претерпѣ́лъ є҆сѝ: ꙗ҆́кѡ Сн҃ъ же Бж҃їй, мі́ръ свободи́лъ є҆сѝ: вели́кая твоѧ̀ мл᷂ⷭть, непостижи́ме Сп҃се поми́лꙋй, и҆ спасѝ на́съ.
items.english_text: O Lord, King of the ages and Creator of all, Who for our sake didst accept Crucifixion and Burial in the flesh, that Thou mightest deliver us all from hades: Thou art our God; besides Thee we know none other.[^1302]

provenance.verbatim_source: O Lord, King of the ages and Creator of all, Who for our sake didst accept Crucifixion and Burial in the flesh, that Thou mightest deliver us all from hades: Thou art our God; besides Thee we know none other.[^1302]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: И҆́ны стїхи̑ры А҆нато́лїєвы.
items.english_text: O Lord, who shall declare Thy radiant wonders? Or who shall recount Thy dread mysteries? For having become man for our sake as Thou Thyself didst will, Thou didst manifest the dominion of Thy power: for by Thy Cross Thou didst open paradise unto the robber, and by Thy Burial Thou didst shatter the bars of hades; and by Thy Resurrection Thou didst enrich all things, O Compassionate One: Lord, glory to Thee![^1303]

provenance.verbatim_source: O Lord, who shall declare Thy radiant wonders? Or who shall recount Thy dread mysteries? For having become man for our sake as Thou Thyself didst will, Thou didst manifest the dominion of Thy power: for by Thy Cross Thou didst open paradise unto the robber, and by Thy Burial Thou didst shatter the bars of hades; and by Thy Resurrection Thou didst enrich all things, O Compassionate One: Lord, glory to Thee![^1303]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Гд᷂ⷭи, Цр҃ю̀ вѣкѡ́въ, и҆ Тво́рче всѣ́хъ, на́съ ра́ди Распя́тїе и҆ Погребе́нїе пло́тїю прїе́мый, да на́съ ѿ а҆́да свободѝши всѣ́хъ: ты́ є҆сѝ Бг҃ъ на́шъ, ра́звѣ тебѐ и҆но́гѡ не вѣ́мы.
items.english_text: The Myrrh-bearing women, having reached Thy tomb very early, sought to anoint Thee with myrrh, the immortal Word and God; and having been informed by the Angel's words, they returned with joy, to announce openly unto the Apostles: That Thou, the Life of all, art risen, and hast granted cleansing and great mercy unto the world.[^1304]

provenance.verbatim_source: The Myrrh-bearing women, having reached Thy tomb very early, sought to anoint Thee with myrrh, the immortal Word and God; and having been informed by the Angel's words, they returned with joy, to announce openly unto the Apostles: That Thou, the Life of all, art risen, and hast granted cleansing and great mercy unto the world.[^1304]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Гд᷂ⷭи, пресїя́ющаѧ твоѧ̑ чꙋдеса̀ кто̀ и҆сповѣ́сть; и҆лѝ кто̀ возвѣсти́тъ стра̑шнаѧ твоѧ̑ та́инства; вочеловѣ́чивыйся бо на́съ ра́ди, ꙗ҆́кѡ са́мъ восхотѣ́лъ є҆сѝ, держа́вꙋ ꙗ҆ви́лъ є҆сѝ Си́лы твоеѧ̀. Кр᷂ⷭто́мъ бо твои́мъ разбо́йникꙋ ра́й ѿве́рзлъ є҆сѝ, и҆ Погребе́нїемъ твои́мъ вереѝ а҆́дѡвы сокрꙋши́лъ є҆сѝ: Воскр᷂ⷭнїемъ же твои́мъ всѧ́чєскаѧ ѡ҆богати́лъ є҆сѝ Бл҃гоꙋтро́бне, Гд᷂ⷭи сла́ва тебѣ̀.
items.english_text: *Verse: Look upon me, and have mercy on me.*[^1305]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Verse: Look upon me, and have mercy on me.*[^1305]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: Мѵроно́сицы жєны̀, гро́бъ тво́й дости́гше, ѕѣлѡ̀ ра́нѡ и҆ска́хꙋ тебѐ мѵ́ры пома́зати, безсме́ртнаго Сло́ва и҆ Бг҃а, и҆ А҆́гг҃ла гл҃ы ѡ҆гласи́вшеся, возвраща́хꙋся ра́достїю, А҆п᷂ⷭтолѡмъ возвѣсти́ти ꙗ҆́вѣ: ꙗ҆́кѡ воскре́слъ є҆сѝ Животѐ всѣ́хъ, и҆ пода́лъ є҆сѝ мі́рови ѡ҆чище́нїе, и҆ ве́лїю ми́лость.
items.english_text: *Idiomelon of the Blind Man.*

items.slavonic_text: Самогла́сенъ Слѣпа́гѡ.
items.english_text: Having become incarnate for the bowels of mercy, O Christ God, by the compassion of Thine ineffable mercies Thou didst vouchsafe divine radiance unto him who was deprived of light from the womb, having touched his pupils with dust by Thy creative fingers: do Thou Thyself even now, O Giver of light, illuminate also the spiritual senses of our soul, as the only begrudgeless Giver.[^1306]

provenance.verbatim_source: Having become incarnate for the bowels of mercy, O Christ God, by the compassion of Thine ineffable mercies Thou didst vouchsafe divine radiance unto him who was deprived of light from the womb, having touched his pupils with dust by Thy creative fingers: do Thou Thyself even now, O Giver of light, illuminate also the spiritual senses of our soul, as the only begrudgeless Giver.[^1306]

items.office: ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA, OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS

items.day_or_date: Synaxarion of the Menaion. Then the present Synaxarion:*[^1252]
items.slavonic_text: За милосе́рдїе ми́лости воплоти́выйся Хр᷂ⷭтѐ Бж҃е, свѣ́та лише́ннаго ѿ оу҆тро́бы, милосе́рдїемъ неизрече́нныхъ щедро́тъ, сїя́нїѧ Бж҃е́ственнагѡ сподо́билъ є҆сѝ, сегѡ̀ зѣни́цамъ пе́рстїю созда́тельными пе́рсты твои́ми прикосны́выйся: са́мъ и҆ ны́нѣ Свѣтода́телю, и҆ на̑ша ѡ҆зарѝ дꙋше́вная чꙋ́вства, ꙗ҆́кѡ є҆ди́нъ независтнода́тель.
items.english_text: Who shall utter Thy mighty acts, O Christ? Or who shall number the multitude of Thy wonders? For as Thou wast seen two-fold upon earth in Thy goodness, so didst Thou bestow two-fold healings upon the sick: for not only didst Thou open the bodily eyes of the man blind from the womb, but the spiritual ones also; therefore did he confess Thee as the hidden God, Who grantest great mercy unto all.[^1307]

provenance.verbatim_source: Who shall utter Thy mighty acts, O Christ? Or who shall number the multitude of Thy wonders? For as Thou wast seen two-fold upon earth in Thy goodness, so didst Thou bestow two-fold healings upon the sick: for not only didst Thou open the bodily eyes of the man blind from the womb, but the spiritual ones also; therefore did he confess Thee as the hidden God, Who grantest great mercy unto all.[^1307]

items.slavonic_text: Стїхи́ра Е҆ѵⷢльскаѧ, гла́съ п҃:
items.english_text: Mary's tears were not shed warmly in vain; for behold, she was accounted worthy both of the instructing Angels and of the sight of Jesus Himself; yet she still minded earthly things, as a weak woman: therefore also she was sent away from touching Christ; but yet she was dispatched as a herald unto Thy disciples, bearing the good tidings unto them, announcing Thine ascent unto the Father's inheritance: with her, vouchsafe us also Thine appearance, O Master and Lord.[^1310]

items.slavonic_text: Марї́ины сле́зы не всꙋ́е пролива́ютсѧ те́плѣ: сѐ бо сподо́бися и҆ оу҆ча́щихъ А҆́гг҃лѡвъ, и҆ видѣ́нїа самагѡ̀ І҆и҃са: но є҆щѐ земна̑ѧ мꙋ́дрствꙋетъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ жена̀ немощна́ѧ: тѣ́мже и҆ ѿсыла́етсѧ не прикаса́тися Хр᷂ⷭтꙋ̀, но ѻ҆ба́че проповѣ́дница посыла́етсѧ твои̑мъ Оу҆чени́кѡмъ, и҆̀мже бл҃говѣствова́нїе нося́щи, є҆́же ко Ѻ҆те́ческомꙋ жре́бїю восхо́дъ возвѣща́ющи: съ не́юже сподо́би и҆ на́съ ꙗ҆вле́нїа твоегѡ̀, Влⷣко Гд᷂ⷭи.

items.english_text: The robber on the cross, having believed Thee to be God, O Christ, confessed Thee purely from the heart, crying: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom![^1312]

items.slavonic_text: Разбо́йникъ на Кр᷂ⷭтѣ̀ Бг҃а тѧ̀ бы́ти вѣ́ровавъ, Хр᷂ⷭтѐ, и҆сповѣ́да тѧ̀ чи́стѣ ѿ се́рдца: помянѝ мѧ̀ Гд᷂ⷭи, вопїѧ̀, во Цр᷂ⷭтвїи твое́мъ.
items.english_text: Him Who blossomed forth life for our race upon the tree of the Cross, and dried up the curse that came from the tree, let us sing in harmony as Savior and Creator.[^1313]

provenance.verbatim_source: Him Who blossomed forth life for our race upon the tree of the Cross, and dried up the curse that came from the tree, let us sing in harmony as Savior and Creator.[^1313]

items.slavonic_text: И҆́же на дре́вѣ кр᷂ⷭтнѣмъ, жи́знь процвѣ́тшаго ро́дꙋ на́шемꙋ, и҆ и҆зсꙋши́вша ю҆́же ѿ дре́ва кля́твꙋ, ꙗ҆́кѡ Сп҃са и҆ Содѣ́телѧ согла́снѡ воспои́мъ.
items.english_text: When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, between two condemned robbers, the one indeed, blaspheming Thee, was justly condemned; but the other, confessing Thee, made his abode in paradise.[^1314]

items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.slavonic_text: На Гд᷂ⷭи воззва́хъ, поста́вимъ стїхѡ́въ ѕ҃, пра́здника г҃. И҆ Мине́и г҃.
items.english_text: Being Light unto all human nature, and the Eye unto the body of this world, O God and Word, and recognized as the Maker and Fashioner of eyes: now also by the mingling of clay and spittle, Thou dost ineffably refashion the blind man, Thy fingers fashioning both sight and vision; which having attained, he who was previously known among those born as one entirely blind to the sun, sees Thee, the sweet Sun, beholding the form of Him Who created him for our sake in Thine ineffable compassion.[^1328]

provenance.verbatim_source: Being Light unto all human nature, and the Eye unto the body of this world, O God and Word, and recognized as the Maker and Fashioner of eyes: now also by the mingling of clay and spittle, Thou dost ineffably refashion the blind man, Thy fingers fashioning both sight and vision; which having attained, he who was previously known among those born as one entirely blind to the sun, sees Thee, the sweet Sun, beholding the form of Him Who created him for our sake in Thine ineffable compassion.[^1328]

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS

items.slavonic_text: Гла́съ є҆. Подо́бенъ: Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡвъ:
items.english_text: Deprived of limbs, and enriched by the configuration of human bodily instrumental parts, he that was previously blind from his mother’s womb considered that he was not a complete creation on account of the lack of eyes, whence by his feet came many stumblings of the body, striking against stones: yet having acquired through Thee this wealth also, so that he sees the light of the world, he announcs Thee, the Master of lights, as God and Lord over creations, and the Maker of all the universe.[^1329]

provenance.verbatim_source: Deprived of limbs, and enriched by the configuration of human bodily instrumental parts, he that was previously blind from his mother’s womb considered that he was not a complete creation on account of the lack of eyes, whence by his feet came many stumblings of the body, striking against stones: yet having acquired through Thee this wealth also, so that he sees the light of the world, he announcs Thee, the Master of lights, as God and Lord over creations, and the Maker of all the universe.[^1329]

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.section: At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of Tone 5:*[^1311]
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.slavonic_text: Свѣ́тъ всемꙋ̀ є҆стествꙋ̀ человѣ́ческомꙋ, и҆ Ѻ҆́ко тѣ́лꙋ мі́ра сегѡ̀, сы́й Бж҃е и҆ Сло́ве, и҆ ѻ҆че́съ ѻ҆́кчїй Содѣ́тель и҆ Зижди́тель познава́емь: и҆ ны́нѣ ѿ смѣше́нїа бре́нїа и҆ плюнове́нїа, слѣпа́го неизрече́ннѡ восꙋ́аеши, пе́рсты твои́ми созида́ющими, и҆ зре́нїе, и҆ ви́дѣнїе: є҆́же и҆ оу҆лꙋчи́въ, пре́жде въ рожде́нныхъ зна́емый, со́лнца ѿню́дъ не ви́дѧ: тебѐ сла́дкое ви́дитъ Сл҃нце, зрѧ̀ ѻ҆́бразъ, на́съ ра́ди, за бл҃гоꙋтро́бїе неизрече́нное Созда́вшагѡ.
items.english_text: With lips, and soul, and mind, he that was formerly blind confessed Him Who creatively gave pupils of the eyes from dust and spittle and ocular enlightenment, as the all-cosmic Overseer and Master of creatures, Who became man solely for compassion on His creature; and he proclaimed Him as almighty God, Whom the scribes, being totally unable to behold through envy and because of his converse with them, acting ever more blindly, judged worthy of expulsion from the synagogue, Him Who once gave the blind man pupils, both spiritual and bodily.[^1330]

provenance.verbatim_source: With lips, and soul, and mind, he that was formerly blind confessed Him Who creatively gave pupils of the eyes from dust and spittle and ocular enlightenment, as the all-cosmic Overseer and Master of creatures, Who became man solely for compassion on His creature; and he proclaimed Him as almighty God, Whom the scribes, being totally unable to behold through envy and because of his converse with them, acting ever more blindly, judged worthy of expulsion from the synagogue, Him Who once gave the blind man pupils, both spiritual and bodily.[^1330]

items.office: ON THE SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.section: At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of Tone 5:*[^1311]
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: ON THE SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.slavonic_text: Оу҆стны̀ и҆ дꙋше́ю и҆ оу҆мо́мъ, ѿ пе́рсти зижди́тельски, и҆ плюнове́нїа, ѻ҆че́съ зѣ́ницы да́вшаго, и҆ ѻ҆́чїее просвѣще́нїе, и҆́же пре́жде слѣпы́й и҆сповѣ́даше, тва́ремъ всемї́рнаго Смотри́телѧ и҆ Строи́телѧ, за милосе́рдїе то́кмѡ созда́нїа, вочеловѣ́чшагося, и҆ проповѣ́даше ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃а всеси́льнаго, є҆го́же кни́жницы за́вистїю, и҆ є҆́же къ ни̑мъ бесѣ́дованїа, ѿню́дъ не могꙋ́ще зрѣ́ти, слѣпотетствꙋюще мно́жае, и҆згна́на ѿ собо́рища сꙋ́дѧтъ, и҆ногда̀ зѣ́ницы да́вшаго слѣпо́мꙋ, дꙋше́вныѧ и҆ тѣле̑сныѧ.
items.english_text: He that was born blind said in his reasoning: Did I then be born without eyes on account of parental sins? Was I born for a rebuke on account of the unbelief of the Gentiles? I am at a loss to ask when it is night, when it is day; my feet cannot endure the stumbling against stones; for I saw not the sun shining, nor Him Who created me in His image: but I pray Thee, O Christ God: look upon me, and have mercy on me![^1331]

provenance.verbatim_source: He that was born blind said in his reasoning: Did I then be born without eyes on account of parental sins? Was I born for a rebuke on account of the unbelief of the Gentiles? I am at a loss to ask when it is night, when it is day; my feet cannot endure the stumbling against stones; for I saw not the sun shining, nor Him Who created me in His image: but I pray Thee, O Christ God: look upon me, and have mercy on me![^1331]

items.slavonic_text: Ѡ҆ земны́хъ всѣ́хъ небре́гше, и҆ на мꙋ́ки мꙋ́жески дерзнꙋ́вше, блаже́нныхъ наде́ждъ не погрѣши́сте, но нб᷂ⷭнагѡ Цр᷂ⷭтвїя наслѣ́дницы бы́сте, прехва́льнїи Мч҃нцы: и҆мꙋ́ще дерзнове́нїе къ человѣколю́бцꙋ Бг҃ꙋ, мі́рꙋ ми́ръ и҆спроси́те, и҆ дꙋша́мъ на́шымъ ве́лїю мл᷂ⷭть.
items.english_text: As Jesus passed by from the temple, He found a man blind from birth, and taking compassion, placed clay upon his eyes, and said unto him: Go, wash in Siloam; and having washed, he received sight, sending up glory unto God; but his neighbors said unto him: Who opened thine eyes, which none of those that see could heal? And he cried aloud and said: A Man called Jesus, He said unto me: Wash in Siloam, and I received sight; He is truly the One of Whom Moses spake in the Law, Christ the Messiah, He is the Savior of our souls.[^1337]

items.slavonic_text: Стї́хъ: Гд᷂ⷭи, да не ꙗ҆́ростїю твое́ю:
items.english_text: *Martyrikon:* O Lord, Thy passion-bearers, having emulated the cup of Thy Passion, abandoned worldly beauty and became companions of the Angels: by their supplications grant peace unto our souls, O Christ God, and great mercy.[^1344]

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Со А҆́гг҃лы нб҃наѧ, съ человѣ́ки земна̑ѧ, во гла́сѣ ра́дованїѧ Бцⷣе вопіе́мъ тѝ: ра́дꙋйсѧ врата̀ нб҃съ ѿве́рзшаѧ, ра́дꙋйсѧ є҆ди́но земноро́дныхъ Спасе́нїе, ра́дꙋйсѧ Чⷭ҇та́ѧ, ра́дꙋйсѧ Бл҃года́тнаѧ, ро́ждшаѧ Бг҃а воплоще́ннаго.
items.english_text: Together with the heavenly Angels, with earthly men, in a voice of rejoicing we cry unto thee, O Theotokos: Rejoice, thou who hast opened the gates of heaven; rejoice, the only salvation of earthborn mortals; rejoice, pure one; rejoice, full of grace, who didst give birth to God incarnate![^1345]

provenance.verbatim_source: Together with the heavenly Angels, with earthly men, in a voice of rejoicing we cry unto thee, O Theotokos: Rejoice, thou who hast opened the gates of heaven; rejoice, the only salvation of earthborn mortals; rejoice, pure one; rejoice, full of grace, who didst give birth to God incarnate![^1345]

items.slavonic_text: Пре́жде Крⷭ҇та̀ твоегѡ̀ Ще́дре и҆ Воскрⷭ҇нїѧ, и҆дꙋ́щꙋ тѝ: слѣпы́й ѿ рожде́нїѧ взыва́ше те́плѣ: Сн҃е Дв҃довъ поми́лꙋй, да́ждь мѝ свѣ́тъ ѻ҆чесе́мъ, да ᲂу҆зрю́ тѧ и҆ а҆́зъ: є҆гѡ́же зѣ́ницы пома́завъ бре́нїемъ ѿ плюнове́нїѧ Сло́ве, томꙋ̀ свѣ́тъ свѣ́тлѡ да́лъ є҆сѝ.
items.english_text: Before Thy Cross and Resurrection, O Compassionate One, as Thou wast going on the way, the man blind from birth cried warmly: O Son of David, have mercy on me! Grant light unto mine eyes, that I also may behold Thee! And having anointed his pupils with clay made from spittle, O Word, Thou didst brightly grant him light.[^1347]

items.slavonic_text: Гла́съ є҃:
items.english_text: O Lord, while the tomb was sealed by the lawless, Thou camest forth from the tomb, even as Thou wast born of the Theotokos. Thine incorporeal Angels understood not how Thou wast incarnate; the soldiers who guarded Thee perceived not when Thou didst rise: for both events were sealed unto those who would search them out, but the wonders were revealed unto those who worship the mystery in faith. Unto us who hymn it, render joy and great mercy.[^1353]

items.slavonic_text: Оу҆вы̀ мнѣ̀! комꙋ̀ ᲂу҆подо́бихсѧ а҆́зъ; непло́днѣй смоко́вницѣ: и҆ бою́сѧ проклѧ́тїѧ съ посѣче́нїемъ: но нб҃ный Дѣ́лателю Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е, ѡ҆лѧденѣ́вшꙋю мою̀ дꙋ́шꙋ, плодоно́снꙋ покажѝ, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ блꙋ́днаго сы́на прїими́ мѧ, и҆ поми́лꙋй мѧ̀.
items.english_text: Woe is me! Unto what have I likened myself? Unto the barren fig tree; and I fear the curse together with the cutting down: but O heavenly Husbandman, Christ God, make fruitful my fallow soul, and receive me as the prodigal son, and have mercy on me![^1354]

items.slavonic_text: О҆слѣпле́нїе ꙗ҆ви́сѧ слѣпы́й, не́гли ви́дѧщымъ, ѡ҆мрача́ѧ и҆ ра́зꙋмы и҆ дꙋ́ши и҆ ᲂу҆́мъ, зрѧ́щымъ є҆гѡ̀ безго́дное прозрѣ́нїе, и҆ пригласи́вше вопроша́хꙋ съ лю́тостїю: ка́кѡ ны́нѣ зри́ши, ꙗ҆́кѡ є҆ди́нъ ѿ свѣ́тъ ви́дѧщихъ, слѣ́пъ сы́й ѿ рожде́нїѧ, и҆ присѣда́й стєза́мъ и҆ просѧ́й; тѣ́мже показа̀ свѣ́тъ Подака́ющаго, и҆ Созда́вшаго свѣти̑ла въ мі́рѣ: ѿ ни́хже проповѣ́даетсѧ Сн҃ъ Бж҃їй пребезнача́льный, во послѣ́днѧѧ и҆з̾ Дв҃ы человѣ́къ ꙗ҆вле́йса за милосе́рдїе, ѿ Бж҃ественнагѡ Дх҃а.
items.english_text: The blind man became blindness unto those who supposedly see, darkening their reasons, souls, and mind as they beheld his unexpected recovery of sight; and having summoned him, they questioned him with malice: How seest thou now as one of those who behold the light, being blind from birth, and sitting beside the ways and begging? Therefore he showed forth the Giver of light, Who created the luminaries in the world, by Whom the Son of God is proclaimed, Who is before all beginning, Who in these last times appeared as man from the Virgin through the divine Spirit for compassion's sake.[^1358]

items.slavonic_text: Ꙗ҆́коже бре́мѧ и҆ земно́е тѧжконо́сїе зрѧ́шесѧ, въ мі́рѣ ходѧ̀ слѣпы́й, и҆ по сто́гнамъ но́ги сокрꙋша́ѧй, не́гли ꙗ҆́коже зрѣ́нїемъ незало́гъ богати́лсѧ, тѣ́мже прибѣга́етъ къ Свѣтода́телю, ѿ негѡ́же прїе́млетъ свѣ́тъ зрѣ́ти, и҆ ѻ҆чи́ма свои́ма ви́дѣти Творца̀, по подо́бїю своемꙋ̀ и҆ по ѻ҆́бразꙋ, созда́вшаго є҆стество̀ человѣ́ческое ѿ землѝ пе́рвѣе, и҆ ны́нѣ пе́рстїю и҆ плюнове́нїемъ просвѣти́вшаго є҆гѡ̀ зѣ́ницы, и҆ да́вшаго человѣколю́бнѡ ви́дѣти со́лнце.
items.english_text: As a burden and an earthly weight he seemed, walking in the world as blind and bruising his feet along the thoroughfares, enriched without pledge of vision; therefore he ran unto the Giver of light, from Whom he received sight to behold the light, and with his eyes to see the Creator, Who in His own likeness and image created human nature from the earth at the first, and now with dust and spittle enlightened his pupils, granting him in His love for mankind to behold the sun.[^1360]

items.slavonic_text: Соѡбра́зна ᲂу҆зрѣ̀ чл҃вѣ́ческомꙋ ѻ҆́бразꙋ Сло́ва О҆ч҃а, свѣ́тъ ви́дѣвъ слѣпы́й, ѿ негѡ́же свѣтоно́сное и҆ дненача́лное ви́дѣ со́лнце, ꙗ҆́коже и҆ про́чїи человѣ́цы, ра́дꙋѧсѧ зрѣ́нїю новоѧвле́ннѣйшемꙋ, и҆́мже враща́шесѧ пра́вѡ и҆ды́й, и҆ безтрꙋ́днѣ проходѧ̀ стєзѝ, и҆ просвѣти́вшаго Сн҃а Бж҃їѧ познава́ѧ, вочл҃вѣ́чшагосѧ кра́йнагѡ ра́ди бл҃гоꙋтро́бїѧ, и҆ є҆́же бѣ̀ пребы́вша Бг҃а, чл҃вѣ́ка бы́вша, и҆ прїи́мша є҆́же не бѣ̀, неслїѧ́нное же соблюда́юща си́хъ соединенїе.
items.english_text: Conformed to the human image, the blind man, having seen the light, beheld the Word of the Father, from Whom he saw the light-bearing and day-originating sun even as other men, rejoicing in the newly revealed vision, by which he walked straightly, traversing the paths without labor, and acknowledging the Son of God Who enlightened him, Who became man for the sake of extreme tender mercy, and Who, remaining God as He was, became man and assumed what He was not, preserving the unconfused union of these natures.[^1362]

items.slavonic_text: Гдⷭ҇и мимоходѧ̀ пꙋте́мъ, ѡ҆брѣ́лъ є҆сѝ человѣ́ка слѣ́па ѿ рожде́нїѧ, и҆ ᲂу҆дивлє́ни бы́вше Оу҆чн҃цы̀, вопроша́хꙋ тѧ̀ гл҃юще: Оу҆чи́телю, кто̀ согрѣшѝ; се́й ли, и҆лѝ роди́тели є҆гѡ̀, да слѣ́пъ роди́сѧ; ты́ же Сп҃се мо́й возопи́лъ є҆сѝ къ ни̑мъ: ни се́й согрѣшѝ, ни роди́тели є҆гѡ̀, но да ꙗ҆вѧ́тсѧ дѣла̀ Бж҃їѧ на не́мъ: мнѣ̀ подоба́етъ дѣ́лати дѣла̀ Посла́вшагѡ мѧ̀, ꙗ҆́же никто́же мо́жетъ дѣ́лати, и҆ сїа̑ ре́къ, плюнꙋ́въ до́лꙋ, и҆ бре́нїе сотво́рь, пома́залъ є҆сѝ ѻ҆́чи є҆гѡ̀, ре́къ къ немꙋ̀: и҆дѝ ᲂу҆мы́йсѧ въ Сїлѡа́мстѣй кꙋпѣ́ли. О҆́нъ же ᲂу҆мы́всѧ, здра́въ бы́сть, и҆ вопїѧ́ше къ тебѣ̀: вѣ́рꙋю Гдⷭ҇и, и҆ поклони́сѧ тебѣ̀. Тѣ́мже вопіе́мъ и҆ мы̀: поми́лꙋй на́съ.
items.english_text: O Lord, as Thou wast passing by along the way, Thou didst find a man blind from birth; and the Disciples, being astonished, questioned Thee, saying: Teacher, who sinned: this man or his parents, that he was born blind? But Thou, my Savior, didst cry out unto them: Neither did this man sin, nor his parents, but that the works of God might be revealed in him. It behooves Me to work the works of Him that sent Me, which no man can do. And having said this, having spat on the ground and made clay, Thou didst anoint his eyes, saying unto him: Go, wash in the pool of Siloam. And having washed, he became whole, and cried unto Thee: I believe, Lord! and he worshipped Thee. Therefore we also cry aloud: Have mercy on us![^1363]

items.english_text: *On Monday of the Blind Man, the Three-Ode Canon, whose acrostic is: Δόξα Θεῷ πρέπει, that is: Glory is fitting unto God.*[^1364]

items.english_text: Let us sing unto the Lord, Who hath wrought marvelous wonders in the Red Sea, a song of victory: for He hath been glorified.[^1365]

items.english_text: *Troparion [D]:* By Thy precious Cross, O Lord, we all have been delivered from the ancient curse: therefore do we glorify Thy goodness.[^1366]

items.english_text: Having beheld the strange sight of the gleaming Angel, and considering the divine Resurrection of the Creator, the Myrrh-bearing women were filled with joy.[^1368]

items.english_text: *Troparion [Th]:* Beholding God crucified in the flesh, the sun was darkened, and the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split asunder.[^1371]

items.english_text: *Troparion [O]:* After Thy Rising Thou didst appear unto the Apostles, O Compassionate One, and didst fill them with ineffable gladness.[^1373]

items.english_text: *Troparion [P]:* Having descended unto the gates of hades, O Christ, Thou didst raise up all that were below together with Thyself, O Lover of mankind, and didst lift up those who hymn Thy power.[^1378]

items.english_text: Thou didst pour forth life unto the dead, O Christ, and having risen on the third day, Thou didst ascend in glory, while Thy venerable Disciples beheld Thee.[^1379]

items.english_text: Render Thy Son and the God of all merciful unto us, O all-pure Virgin, who hymn thee in faith.[^1380]

items.office: ON MONDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION

items.slavonic_text: Побѣ́дꙋ до́блествїѧ слѣпы́й на ви́дѧщихъ до конца̀ взѧ́тъ, ꙗ҆́ко Содѣ́телѧ сегѡ̀ и҆ Созда́телѧ всѣ́хъ и҆ слѣ́пъ сы́й ᲂу҆зрѣ̀, ви́дѣвъ косꙋчеле́нїе созда́вшеесѧ ѿ плюнове́нїѧ, и҆ си̑мъ є҆ди́нѣмъ позна́вый Просвѣти́вшаго, и҆ Сн҃а Бж҃їѧ, и҆ Влады́кꙋ всемї́рнаго: є҆го́же ви́дѧще за́висти ѕло́бою ѡ҆слѣплѧ́еми, всесма̀ не ви́дѣша, и҆ сїа̑ многосꙋгꙋ́бѡ ви́дѧще, ѿ сегѡ̀ чꙋде́съ дѣ́йствїа пресла̑внаѧ є҆ди́нѣми гласы̑.
items.english_text: With lips, soul, and mind, he that was previously blind confessed Him Who creatively gave pupils of the eyes from dust and spittle and total enlightenment, as the cosmic Overseer of creatures and Arranger, Who became man solely out of compassion for His creation, and proclaimed Him as almighty God; Whom the scribes, being totally unable to behold through envy and because of his converse with them, acting ever more blindly, judged worthy of expulsion from the synagogue, Him Who once gave the blind man pupils, both spiritual and bodily.[^1383]

provenance.verbatim_source: With lips, soul, and mind, he that was previously blind confessed Him Who creatively gave pupils of the eyes from dust and spittle and total enlightenment, as the cosmic Overseer of creatures and Arranger, Who became man solely out of compassion for His creation, and proclaimed Him as almighty God; Whom the scribes, being totally unable to behold through envy and because of his converse with them, acting ever more blindly, judged worthy of expulsion from the synagogue, Him Who once gave the blind man pupils, both spiritual and bodily.[^1383]

items.office: ON MONDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS

items.day_or_date: ON MONDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.slavonic_text: Сомнѣ́телемъ кни́жникомъ слѣпы̑мъ, косꙋчи́выйсѧ, пре́жде слѣ́пъ сы́й, ꙗ҆ви́сѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ не́гли ника́коже ви́дѧ: но ло́жнѡ є҆́же зрѣ́ти Сп҃са ра́ди притворѧ́ѧсѧ, ѡ҆слѣплѧ́тисѧ хотѧ́щымъ, помраче́нїи пле́мене, въ ни́хже сїѧ́етъ сла́дкое коистиннꙋ̀ Со́лнце, сꙋккѡторо́дїетвїе ѡ҆бновлѧ́ѧй содѣ́лавый ли́къ: и҆́же сн҃о́вное сегѡ̀ свѣтодѣ́ѧй, и҆ покрове́нїе взема́ѧй, и҆ свѣ́тъ и҆́же въ си́хъ пре́жде слѣпы̑мъ подадѐ: и҆ ны́нѣ зрѧ́ще, Свѣтопода́телѧ мі́рови проповѣ́дꙋютъ.
items.english_text: The blind man won the victory of valor over those who see unto the end, for being blind he beheld Him as Maker of this world and Creator of all, having seen the structure formed from spittle, and by this alone recognized the Enlightener, both the Son of God and the cosmic Master; Whom those seeing, blinded by the malice of envy, saw not at all, even while beholding these most marvelous workings of wonders manifoldly with one voice.[^1384]

provenance.verbatim_source: The blind man won the victory of valor over those who see unto the end, for being blind he beheld Him as Maker of this world and Creator of all, having seen the structure formed from spittle, and by this alone recognized the Enlightener, both the Son of God and the cosmic Master; Whom those seeing, blinded by the malice of envy, saw not at all, even while beholding these most marvelous workings of wonders manifoldly with one voice.[^1384]

items.office: ON MONDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS

items.day_or_date: ON MONDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, гла́съ и҃:
items.english_text: Unto the doubting, blind scribes, he that was previously blind appeared intertwined, as though seeing not at all, but falsely feigning to see for the Savior's sake unto those wishing to be blinded, the darkened race in whom the sweet Sun truly shines, renewing the sabbath-born choir; He Who wrought its filial light, taking away the covering, and granted light unto those formerly blind among them: and now, seeing, they proclaim the Giver of light unto the world.[^1385]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto the doubting, blind scribes, he that was previously blind appeared intertwined, as though seeing not at all, but falsely feigning to see for the Savior's sake unto those wishing to be blinded, the darkened race in whom the sweet Sun truly shines, renewing the sabbath-born choir; He Who wrought its filial light, taking away the covering, and granted light unto those formerly blind among them: and now, seeing, they proclaim the Giver of light unto the world.[^1385]

items.office: ON MONDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.season_or_tone: SUNDAY OF THE BLIND MAN AND FEAST OF THE ASCENSION
items.day_or_date: ON MONDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT VESPERS
items.slavonic_text: Пра́вды Со́лнце мы́сленное Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е, и҆з̾ ᲂу҆тро́бы свѣ́та лишѐннаго, твои́мъ пречⷭ҇тымъ прикоснове́нїемъ просвѣти́вшее ѻ҆́боюдꙋ, и҆ на́ша ѻ҆́чи дꙋше́вныѧ ѡ҆зари́вшее, сы́ны днѐ покажѝ, да вѣ́рою вопіе́мъ тѝ: мно́гое твоѐ и҆ неизрече́нное, є҆́же на на́съ благоꙋтро́бїе, Человѣколю́бче сла́ва тебѣ̀.
items.english_text: O Christ God, noetic Sun of righteousness, Who by Thy most pure touch didst on both sides enlighten him who from the womb was deprived of light, and didst illumine our spiritual eyes: make us to appear as sons of the day, that in faith we may cry unto Thee: For Thy great and ineffable tender mercy toward us, O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee![^1386]

provenance.verbatim_source: O Christ God, noetic Sun of righteousness, Who by Thy most pure touch didst on both sides enlighten him who from the womb was deprived of light, and didst illumine our spiritual eyes: make us to appear as sons of the day, that in faith we may cry unto Thee: For Thy great and ineffable tender mercy toward us, O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee![^1386]

items.slavonic_text: Воскрⷭ҇нїе даѧ́й ро́дꙋ человѣ́ческомꙋ, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѻ҆вча̀ на заколе́нїе веде́сѧ: ᲂу҆страши́шасѧ сегѡ̀ кнѧ́зи а҆́дстїи, и҆ вза́шасѧ врата̀ плаче́внаѧ: вни́де бо Цр҃ь сла́вы Хрⷭ҇то́съ, глаго́лѧ сꙋ́щымъ во ᲂу҆́захъ: и҆зыди́те, и҆ сꙋ́щымъ во тмѣ̀, ѿкры́йтесѧ.
items.english_text: Giving Resurrection unto the human race, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter: the princes of hades were terrified of Him, and the gates of weeping were lifted up; for Christ, the King of glory, entered in, saying unto those in bonds: Come forth! and unto those in darkness: Reveal yourselves![^1387]

provenance.verbatim_source: Giving Resurrection unto the human race, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter: the princes of hades were terrified of Him, and the gates of weeping were lifted up; for Christ, the King of glory, entered in, saying unto those in bonds: Come forth! and unto those in darkness: Reveal yourselves![^1387]

items.slavonic_text: Гдⷭ҇и, и҆ стра́ха твоегѡ̀ бою́сѧ, и҆ лꙋка́вое твори́ти не престаю̀. Кто̀ на сꙋди́щи сꙋдїи не бои́тсѧ; и҆лѝ кто̀ и҆сцѣли́тисѧ хотѧ̀, врача̀ прогнѣ́ваетъ, ꙗ҆́коже а҆́зъ; долготерпѣли́ве Гдⷭ҇и, на не́мощь мою̀ ᲂу҆милосе́рдисѧ, и҆ поми́лꙋй мѧ̀.
items.english_text: O Lord, I both fear Thy judgment and cease not from doing evil. Who at the judgment seat fears not the judge? Or who, desiring to be healed, provokes the physician to wrath as I do? O Long-suffering Lord, have compassion upon my weakness, and have mercy on me![^1389]

provenance.verbatim_source: O Lord, I both fear Thy judgment and cease not from doing evil. Who at the judgment seat fears not the judge? Or who, desiring to be healed, provokes the physician to wrath as I do? O Long-suffering Lord, have compassion upon my weakness, and have mercy on me![^1389]

items.slavonic_text: Мч҃ениченъ:
items.english_text: *Martyrikon:* Armed with the shield of faith and strengthened by the sign of the Cross, Thy saints, O Lord, manfully gave themselves over unto torments, and abolished the deceit and audacity of the devil. By their supplications, as almighty God, send down peace upon the world, and great mercy upon our souls.[^1391]

items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, гла́съ и҃:
items.english_text: Incarnate for the tender mercy of Thy loving-kindness, O Christ God, by the compassion of Thine ineffable compassions Thou didst account him who was deprived of light from the womb worthy of the divine radiance, having touched his pupils with dust by Thy creative fingers: Thyself also now, O Giver of light, enlighten our spiritual senses, as the only grudgeless Giver![^1392]

items.slavonic_text: За милосе́рдїе ми́лости воплоти́выйсѧ Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е, свѣ́та лишѐннаго ѿ ᲂу҆тро́бы, милосе́рдїемъ неизрече́нныхъ щедро́тъ, сїѧ́нїѧ Бж҃ественнагѡ сподо́билъ є҆сѝ, сегѡ̀ зѣ́ницамъ пе́рстїю созда́тельными пе́рсты твои́ми прикосну́выйсѧ: са́мъ и҆ ны́нѣ Свѣтода́телю, и҆ на́ша ѡ҆зарѝ дꙋшє́внаѧ чꙋ́вства, ꙗ҆́кѡ є҆ди́нъ независтнода́тель.

items.slavonic_text: По а҃-мъ стїхосло́вїи сѣда́ленъ.
items.english_text: O Lord, Thou wast called dead, Who didst put death to death; Thou wast placed in a tomb, Who didst empty the tombs: above, the soldiers guarded the tomb; below, Thou didst raise the dead from all eternity. O almighty and incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee![^1396]

items.slavonic_text: Сꙋдїи сѣдѧ́щꙋ, и҆ А҆́гг҃лѡмъ предстоѧ́щымъ, трубѣ̀ гласѧ́щей, и҆ пла́мени горѧ́щꙋ, что̀ сотвори́ши дꙋшѐ моѧ̀ ведо́ма на сꙋ́дъ; тогда́ бо лю̑таѧ твоѧ̑ предста́нꙋтъ, и҆ та̑йнаѧ твоѧ̑ ѡ҆блича́тсѧ согрѣшє́нїѧ: тѣ́мже пре́жде конца̀ возопи́й къ Сꙋдїи: Бж҃е, ѡ҆чи́сти мѧ̀ и҆ спаси́ мѧ.
items.english_text: When the Judge sits and the Angels stand by, the trumpet sounding and the flame burning, what wilt thou do, O my soul, being led unto judgment? For then thy wicked deeds shall stand forth, and thy secret transgressions shall be exposed. Therefore before the end cry aloud unto the Judge: O God, cleanse me and save me![^1398]

provenance.verbatim_source: When the Judge sits and the Angels stand by, the trumpet sounding and the flame burning, what wilt thou do, O my soul, being led unto judgment? items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ, Бг҃оро́диченъ:
items.english_text: O all-holy Mother of God, wall of Christians: deliver thy people as is thy wont, who fervently call upon thee; stand against our enemies and lofty thoughts, that we may cry unto thee: Rejoice, full of grace![^1401]

items.slavonic_text: Мт҃и Бж҃їѧ прест҃а́ѧ, стѣно̀ хрⷭ҇тїа́нъ, и҆зба́ви лю́ди твоѧ̑ ѡ҆бы́чнѡ, зовꙋ́щыѧ къ тебѣ̀ прилѣ́жнѡ: сопроти́въ ста́ни врагѡ́въ, и҆ возвыша́ющихсѧ мы́слей, да вопіе́мъ тѝ: ра́дꙋйсѧ Блгⷣтнаѧ.

items.slavonic_text: Гла́съ є҃. Подо́бенъ: Собезна́чальное Сло́во:
items.english_text: Having received sight through the spittle of Him Who fashioned the human composition, he that was previously blind, who from birth saw not the great sun, is beheld; therefore from his soul he sends up thanksgiving unto God, seeing His image, the image fashioned according to the likeness of Him Who fashioned it.[^1403]

provenance.verbatim_source: Having received sight through the spittle of Him Who fashioned the human composition, he that was previously blind, who from birth saw not the great sun, is beheld; therefore from his soul he sends up thanksgiving unto God, seeing His image, the image fashioned according to the likeness of Him Who fashioned it.[^1403]

items.slavonic_text: Прозрѣ́вый, плюнове́нїемъ Созда́вшагѡ чл҃вѣ́ческое составле́нїе, ви́дитсѧ, пре́жде слѣпы́й, не ви́дѧй ѿ рожде́нїѧ вели́кагѡ со́лнца, тѣ́мже и҆ блгⷣаре́нїе Бг҃ꙋ возсыла́етъ ѿ дꙋшѝ, сегѡ̀ зрѧ̀ ѻ҆́бразъ, по подо́бїю, созда́нный ѻ҆́бразъ созда́вшагѡ.
items.english_text: *Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*[^1404]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and for ever and unto ages of ages. Amen. The same.*[^1404]

items.slavonic_text: На хвали́техъ стїхи̑ры ѻ҆кто́иха.
items.english_text: O Lord, Who didst shatter the eternal bars and break bonds asunder, Thou didst rise from the tomb, leaving behind Thy grave-clothes as a witness of Thy true three-day Burial; and Thou didst go before into Galilee, Thou Who wast guarded in the cave. Great is Thy mercy, O incomprehensible Savior: have mercy on us and save us![^1407]

Great is Thy mercy, O incomprehensible Savior: have mercy on us and save us![^1407]

items.day_or_date: ON TUESDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS
items.slavonic_text: Гдⷭ҇и, вереѝ вѣ̑чныѧ сокрꙋши́вый, и҆ ᲂу҆́зы растерза́вый, ѿ гро́ба воскре́слъ є҆сѝ, ѡ҆ста́вль твоѧ̑ погреба́лнаѧ, во свидѣ́телство и҆́стиннагѡ тридне́внагѡ твоегѡ̀ Погребе́нїѧ: и҆ предва́рилъ є҆сѝ въ Галиле́и, въ пеще́рѣ стрего́мый: ве́лїѧ твоѧ̀ мл҃ть, непостижи́ме Сп҃се поми́лꙋй, и҆ спаси́ на́съ. Два́жды.
items.english_text: Overlook the multitude of my transgressions, O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, and cleanse all mine iniquities, granting me the thought of return, as the only Lover of mankind, I pray Thee; and have mercy on me![^1408]

provenance.verbatim_source: Overlook the multitude of my transgressions, O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, and cleanse all mine iniquities, granting me the thought of return, as the only Lover of mankind, I pray Thee; and have mercy on me![^1408]

items.slavonic_text: Мно́жества прегрѣше́нїй мои́хъ пре́зри Гдⷭ҇и, ѿ Дв҃ы рожде́йсѧ, и҆ всѧ̑ ѡ҆чи́сти беззакѡ́нїа моѧ̑, по́мыслъ мнѣ̀ подаѧ́й ѡ҆браще́нїѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ є҆ди́нъ чл҃вѣколю́бецъ, молю́сѧ, и҆ поми́лꙋй мѧ̀.
items.english_text: *Martyrikon:* Thy passion-bearers, O Lord, emulating the angelic ranks, endured torments as though incorporeal, having a single-minded hope: the enjoyment of promised blessings. By their supplications, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and great mercy unto our souls![^1409]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Martyrikon:*  
Thy passion-bearers, O Lord, emulating the angelic ranks, endured torments as though incorporeal, having a single-minded hope: the enjoyment of promised blessings. By their supplications, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and great mercy unto our souls![^1409]

items.office: ON TUESDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS

items.slavonic_text: Кто̀ возглаго́летъ си̑лы твоѧ̑ Хрⷭ҇тѐ; и҆лѝ кто̀ и҆зочте́тъ чꙋде́съ твои́хъ мно́жества; сꙋгꙋ́бъ бо ꙗ҆́кѡ ви́дѣнъ бы́лъ є҆сѝ на землѝ за бл҃гость, сꙋгꙋ́бы и҆ цѣльбы̑ недꙋ́гꙋющымъ подава́лъ є҆сѝ, не то́чїю бо тѣле́сныѧ ѻ҆́чи ѿве́рзлъ є҆сѝ и҆́же ѿ ᲂу҆тро́бы слѣпо́мꙋ, но и҆ дꙋше́вныѧ: тѣ́мже Бг҃а тѧ̀ и҆сповѣ́даше та́йщагосѧ, и҆ всѣ̑мъ подаю́ща ве́лїю ми́лость.
items.english_text: Who shall declare Thy powers, O Christ? Or who shall recount the multitude of Thy wonders? For as Thou wast seen as two-fold upon earth in Thy goodness, so two-fold healings didst Thou grant unto the sick; for not only the bodily eyes didst Thou open of him who was blind from the womb, but also the spiritual: therefore he confessed Thee as the God Who was hidden, and Who grantest great mercy unto all.[^1410]

provenance.verbatim_source: Who shall declare Thy powers, O Christ? Or who shall recount the multitude of Thy wonders? For as Thou wast seen as two-fold upon earth in Thy goodness, so two-fold healings didst Thou grant unto the sick; for not only the bodily eyes didst Thou open of him who was blind from the womb, but also the spiritual: therefore he confessed Thee as the God Who was hidden, and Who grantest great mercy unto all.[^1410]

items.office: ON TUESDAY OF THE BLIND MAN, AT MATINS

items.slavonic_text: Сїѧ́нїе свѣтоно́сное просїѧ́вшее, зрѧ́ще проѧвле́ннѡ въ сꙋбкѡ́тꙋ, свѣтоно́сномꙋ слѣпцꙋ̀, зако́нни Мѡѷсе́а смꙋща́еми, мра́комъ ѡ҆слѣплѧ́ющесѧ, зрѧ́ще сѣ́нь, ѡ҆сѣне́нїѧ не разꙋмѣ́юще покрыва́ющагѡ зако́ны, и҆з̾ негѡ́же не ви́дѣша Свѣтода́телѧ, и҆ сꙋбкѡ́ты Содѣ́телѧ, сло́вомъ косꙋчи́вшагѡ слѣпа́го, и҆змове́нїемъ, и҆ плюнове́нїа но́вымъ бренотворе́нїемъ, съ ни́мже слѣша́еми Бг҃а тогѡ̀ ᲂу҆зри́мъ, ѡ҆слѣпле́нїе фарїсе́йское ѡ҆блича́юще, зрѣ́нїемъ є҆́же ѿ лꙋ́чшагѡ.
items.english_text: Beholding the light-bearing radiance that shone forth clearly on the Sabbath for the light-bearing blind man, the keepers of the Law of Moses were confounded, being blinded by darkness; beholding the shadow, they understood not the overshadowing of the Law that covered them, from which they saw not the Giver of light and the Maker of the Sabbath, Who intertwined the blind man by word, by washing, and by the new clay-making from spittle; with whom let us, hearing, behold that God, rebuking the Pharisaic blindness with the sight that is from what is better.[^1412]

provenance.verbatim_source: Beholding the light-bearing radiance that shone forth clearly on the Sabbath for the light-bearing blind man, the keepers of the Law of Moses were confounded, being blinded by darkness; beholding the shadow, they understood not the overshadowing of the Law that covered them, from which they saw not the Giver of light and the Maker of the Sabbath, Who intertwined the blind man by word, by washing, and by the new clay-making from spittle; with whom let us, hearing, behold that God, rebuking the Pharisaic blindness with the sight that is from what is better.[^1412]

items.slavonic_text: Оу҆́тро возсїѧ̀ во тмѣ̀ пребыва́ющемꙋ но́щи неви́дѣнїа, многоболѣ́зненномꙋ слѣпо́мꙋ, во стрꙋѧ́хъ кꙋпѣ́ли Сїлѡа́мскїѧ и҆змове́нномꙋ, свѣ́тъ ѻ҆чесе́мъ бж҃твеннымъ повелѣ́нїемъ, тѣ́мже свѣтоно́сный невѣ́дїй ви́дитсѧ, мра́къ тмы̀ почетко́рныхъ зако́нныхъ и҆з̾ѡблича́ѧ кни́жниковъ, и҆ помраче́нное си́хъ неви́дѣнїе, возсїѧ́вшими просвѣща́ѧй свѣтоно́сными, и҆з̾ ни́хже ѡ҆слѣпле́нїе пре́жде сѣно́вныхъ пи́сменъ косꙋча́етсѧ, ѿ Сло́ва на́мъ пода́емыми свѣ́тлыми сїѧ̑ньми.
items.english_text: The dawn shone forth unto him who remained in the darkness of the night of blindness, the long-suffering blind man washed in the streams of the pool of Siloam, light unto his eyes by the divine command; therefore the light-bearing one is seen unknowing, exposing the gloom of the darkness of the legalistic scribes who honor letters, and enlightening their darkened ignorance with the light-bearing rays that have shone forth, from which the blindness of the shadowy letters of old is intertwined by the bright radiances granted unto us by the Word.[^1414]

provenance.verbatim_source: The dawn shone forth unto him who remained in the darkness of the night of blindness, the long-suffering blind man washed in the streams of the pool of Siloam, light unto his eyes by the divine command; therefore the light-bearing one is seen unknowing, exposing the gloom of the darkness of the legalistic scribes who honor letters, and enlightening their darkened ignorance with the light-bearing rays that have shone forth, from which the blindness of the shadowy letters of old is intertwined by the bright radiances granted unto us by the Word.[^1414]
